population_rationale: Resource-poor indigenous shifting cultivator (jhum) households in north-east India, an LMIC; small-scale subsistence farming. Evidence: "shifting cultivation provides primary livelihood to 0.44 million (10.03%) of the resource-poor forest-dwelling farm families" [p.4, Study area]
concept_rationale: Measures adaptation decisions (changes in timing of five shifting cultivation calendar activities) and tests their association with perceptions; perception is not studied alone. Evidence: "Results reveal that three-fourths (~ 76%) of the respondents made alterations in the shifting cultivation calendar as an adaptation strategy to climate change." [p.1, Abstract]
context_rationale: Rainfed hill agriculture with explicit temperature and rainfall trends/dry spells driving the research question. Evidence: "There have been many changes in the jhum (shifting cultivation) cycle under the conditions of increasing atmospheric temperature and erratic rainfall" [p.2, Introduction]
methodology_rationale: Household survey (n=600) plus IMD gridded climate data analysed with Spearman trend tests, chi-square and Cramer's V. Evidence: "We conducted chi-square tests of independence (Eq. 2), and calculated Cramer’s V (Eq. 3) to ascertain the strength of the association." [p.5, Analysis and comparison]
geography_rationale: India (lower-middle-income). Evidence: "The present study was conducted in the NEI (Fig. 1)." [p.3, Study area]
period_language_rationale: Published online June 2023, English. Evidence: "Published online: 17 June 2023" [p.1 header]

population_rationale: Cattle farmers (agro-pastoralists/herders, herd mean ~64 head, cattle as main activity) in northern Benin; not commercial or industrial operations, so the generic-farmer rule applies. Evidence: "Breeders' choice criteria were: to have cattle farming as the main activity; be at least 50 years old; have at least 10 heads of cattle." [p.3, 2.3 Exploratory investigation]
concept_rationale: Documents seven adaptation strategies actually adopted and analyses determinants of their adoption (uptake_adoption), going beyond perception alone. Evidence: "Seven (7) major adaptation strategies were identified that have been developed by cattle farmers" [p.6, 3.4] | "binary logistic regression with a stepwise backward elimination of predictors was performed to identify the most determinant variables affecting cattle farmers’ choice of adaptation strategies" [p.3, 2.5]
context_rationale: Livestock production with explicit climate stress (declining rainfall, rising temperature, drought-related forage scarcity) driving the research question. Evidence: "Cattle farming is directly impacted by climate change (CC), as it utilizes resources whose seasonality and productivity are strongly climate-dependent." [p.1, Abstract]
methodology_rationale: Primary survey of 360 farmers with semi-structured questionnaires, frequency analysis and logistic regression, plus station climate records. Evidence: "Data collection was carried out from November 2018 to April 2019" [p.2, 2.2] | "a total of 360 cattle farmers were surveyed during this study" [p.3, 2.3]
geography_rationale: Benin is a lower-middle-income country. Evidence: "Benin, a developing country in West Africa" [p.1, Introduction]
period_language_rationale: Published 2020 in English. Evidence: "Heliyon 6 (2020) e04373" [p.1 header]

population_rationale: Communal pastoral and agro-pastoral households in Ngamiland, Botswana (upper-middle-income); small-scale subsistence livestock keepers, not commercial ranchers. Evidence: "The majority of residents follow an agro-pastoral lifestyle keeping multispecies livestock." [p.4, Study area]
concept_rationale: Documents coping and adaptation strategies (livelihood diversification, self-help groups, flood recession farming) and adaptive capacity enablers/constraints. Evidence: "The aim of this study is to investigate the ways in which pastoral communities cope and adapt to constraints due to environmental and policy changes in Ngamiland, Botswana." [p.2, Introduction]
context_rationale: Semi-arid setting where drought and rainfall variability are among the main constraints studied; climate is one of several drivers (with policy and disease), but is an explicit stressor and a stated focus (climate variability, drought). Evidence: "Respondents mentioned recurrent drought and decreasing and more irregular rainfall patterns as a primary risk factor." [p.6, Results 3.1.4]
methodology_rationale: Empirical participatory rural appraisal: 112 semi-structured interviews, 26 key informants, 6 FGDs, NVivo thematic analysis. Evidence: "A total of 112 households in the 6 study villages participated in semi-structured interviews." [p.4, Research methodology]
geography_rationale: Botswana, upper-middle-income. Evidence: "Ngamiland District, North-western Botswana" [p.3, Study area]

population_rationale: Up-country vegetable farmers in Sri Lanka with small farms (mean 0.639 ha); not commercial-scale. Evidence: "Mean farmland size was 253.02 perches (0.639 ha), and mean household size was four." [p.6, 27.5.1]
concept_rationale: Measures adopted adaptation options and drivers/barriers of adaptation, beyond perceptions. Evidence: "which adaptation options are farmers currently adopting? (iii) which factors influence the commonly used adaptation options?" [p.2-3, Introduction]
context_rationale: Climate variability (erratic rainfall, drought, temperature) drives the research question in rain-fed vegetable farming. Evidence: "Sri Lanka is already experiencing climate change and the consequent, erratic rainfall and extreme swings between droughts and intense rainfall" [p.2, Introduction]
methodology_rationale: Survey of 150 farmers analysed with multinomial logit, plus qualitative interview material. Evidence: "The study analyzes factors affecting climate change by using a multinomial logit (MNL) model." [p.6, Methods]
geography_rationale: Sri Lanka, lower-middle-income. Evidence: "We selected Nuwara Eliya, Welimada, Badulla, and Bandarawela divisional secretariats as the study area" [p.3, 27.3]
period_language_rationale: Published 2022, English. Book chapter is eligible by period/language. Evidence: "© The Author(s) 2022" [p.1]

population_rationale: Subsistence rain-fed Matengo smallholder farmer groups in Tanzania (LMIC). Evidence: "Subsistence rain-fed agriculture is the mainstay of the Matengo farmers’ economy in both villages." [p.3, Materials and Methods]
concept_rationale: Documents adaptation processes (group formation, diffusion of fish farming, tree planting, beekeeping, hydro-mill) and livelihood outcomes in response to climate change and variability. Evidence: "Their adaptation strategies to these CC&V include working in farmer groups, rural–rural migration and adoption of improved cooking stoves" [p.4, Results]
context_rationale: Agricultural setting with explicit climate stressors (drought, erratic rains, dry spells) framing the research question. Evidence: "recurrent droughts, El Niño rains of 1997–1998, change of rainfall season (onset and offset, durations, increasing dry spells), crop failures, increasing temperatures" [p.4, Results]
methodology_rationale: Empirical case study with group interviews using checklists, FGDs, observation and satellite image analysis. Evidence: "Information gathered from farmer groups’ interviews, FGD, observations and informal interviews were subjected to content analysis." [p.4, Materials and Methods]
geography_rationale: Tanzania (low/lower-middle income). Evidence: "The study was conducted in the Matengo highlands, located in Mbinga district, Ruvuma region" [p.3, Materials and Methods]
period_language_rationale: Published 2012, English. Evidence: "Springer-Verlag Berlin Heidelberg 2012" [p.1 footer]

population_rationale: Small-scale ecological farmers in China (UMIC) defined with reference to FAO smallholder definition; up to ~13 ha, though some farms are market-oriented. Authors frame them as smallholders and analyse them as such. Evidence: "we defined small-scale farms in this study as those with a cultivated acreage not exceeding 200 mu (~13.3 hectares), with exceptions for agroforestry or orchards." [p.6, Research Methods]
concept_rationale: Documents perceptions and impacts, but also adoption of ecosystem-based and socio-economic adaptation measures and their perceived effectiveness. Evidence: "farmers apply diverse ecological practices alongside socio-economic measures to build resilience." [p.1-2, Abstract]
context_rationale: Explicit climate hazards (drought, heavy rain, heat) in agricultural settings drive the research question. Evidence: "heavy precipitation in North China (2021), extended drought in South China (2021 and 2022), and unprecedented rainfall in the Pearl River Delta" [p.5, Research Methods]
methodology_rationale: Empirical study using interviews, farm visits and structured surveys of 28 farms. Evidence: "the lead researcher conducted in-depth interviews (online and in person), farm visits, structured surveys, and follow-up conversations" [p.6, Research Methods]
geography_rationale: China, upper-middle-income. Evidence: "A total of 28 ecological farms were studied: Beijing (5), Tianjin (1), Hebei (5), Guangxi (8), and Guangdong (9)" [p.6, Research Methods]
period_language_rationale: Published online 10 September 2025 (within 2005-2025 window), English. Evidence: "Published online September 10, 2025" [p.1]

population_rationale: Farmers (paddy, vegetables, small livestock) in one hill village in Nagaland, India (LMIC); small-scale farming with 65 paddy households, 78 ring-well beneficiaries. Evidence: "About 65 farming household cultivate paddy in the lowland area of Tzuvi valley" [p.2, Findings]
concept_rationale: Documents adoption of climate resilient technologies and their yield/income outcomes. Evidence: "all the climate resilient technologies greatly solved farmers farming problems and boost up the economy of the farmer as well." [p.1, Abstract]
context_rationale: Drought, dry spells and floods explicitly drive interventions. Evidence: "The major climate challenges encounters are flood and prolong dry spell like situation (drought)." [p.2, Methodology]
methodology_rationale: Empirical case study reporting measured yields, incomes and costs for demonstrated technologies, though methods are thinly described (borderline quality, not an exclusion). Evidence: "A yield as high as 41 q/ha was obtained from SRI as compared to conventional method (29.3 q/ha) with an additional income of Rs. 37,250/-." [p.3, Findings]
geography_rationale: India, lower-middle income. Evidence: "Krishi Vigyan Kendra, MOKOKCHUNG (NAGALAND) INDIA" [p.1]
period_language_rationale: Published June 2015, English. Evidence: "VOLUME 10 | ISSUE 1 | JUNE, 2015 | 90-94" [p.1 header]

population_rationale: Smallholder farmers in rural Ghana (68.9% farm <=2 ha), rain-fed. Evidence: "Smallholder farmers were randomly selected using the Census and Survey Processing System (CSPro) software in the seven farming communities." [p.6, 3.4]
concept_rationale: Measures intention and adoption of CSA practices (adoption/behaviour change). Evidence: "to analyze smallholder farmers' intention and adoption behavior toward CSA practices in rural Ghana" [p.1, Abstract]
context_rationale: Drought and rainfall variability in drought-prone districts drive the research question. Evidence: "These districts were selected because they are among the most vulnerable to drought in Ghana" [p.6, 3.1]
methodology_rationale: Household survey (n=350) with SEM. Evidence: "Three hundred and fifty (350) household surveys were conducted in the seven study communities." [p.6, 3.2]
geography_rationale: Ghana is lower-middle income.

population_rationale: Boro rice cultivators in haor (lowland) areas of Bangladesh; generic farmer label, smallholder context. Evidence: "using 378 boro cultivator's data which were collected from selected 'haor' (lowland) in Sylhet" [p.1, Abstract]
concept_rationale: Analyses adaptation strategies (changing crop varieties, shifting crop to livestock) and determinants of farmers' adaptation decisions, plus barriers to adaptation. Evidence: "determining the factors those significantly affect rice farm cultivator's decision of adaptability in flood-prone areas in Bangladesh" [p.2, Introduction]
context_rationale: Early flash floods and unpredictable weather drive the study. Evidence: "A Study on Early Flash Flood-prone Areas in Bangladesh" [p.1, Title]
methodology_rationale: Primary household survey with chi-square, confrontation matrix and ordered logit. Evidence: "The ordered logit model had been estimated using the STATA 16.0 version." [p.3, 2.4]
geography_rationale: Bangladesh is lower-middle income.
period_language_rationale: Published 2023, English. Evidence: "Environment and Ecology Research 11(2): 274-283, 2023" [p.1]

lead_rationale: Both reviewers uncertain on concept. Primary object is fire-mitigation/conservation policy (CAC vs PES) in a lab-in-the-field game; drought is a treatment, not the adaptation being assessed. Recommend exclude; co-authors may retain if risk-reduction decisions under drought are accepted as an adaptation process.
second_reviewer_summary: Smallholders in a drought-risk framed field experiment on fire-mitigation policies (CAC vs PES). All criteria are met except that the concept is fire-conservation policy evaluation with drought as a treatment, and the measured behaviour (fire control, fire-free investment) is a lab-in-the-field game decision, so adaptation alignment is marginal. Leaning include under the inclusive-at-margin rule if the lead accepts risk-reduction decisions under drought as adaptation processes; otherwise exclude.
exclusion_reason: Concept criterion borderline: study is framed as an ex-ante fire-mitigation/conservation policy assessment; response to drought risk is analysed but adaptation (vs mitigation/conservation) is not the stated aim.
population_rationale: Active smallholder farmers in Para, Brazil. Evidence: "We sampled 576 smallholder farmers in 40 communities in the municipalities of Paragominas, Ipixuna, São Domingos do Capim, and Irituia in the state of Pará, Brazil." [p.5, Sec 4]
concept_rationale: Measures smallholders' decisions between uncontrolled fire, controlled fire and fire-free techniques under drought-risk (climate change) scenarios and fire policies (decision-making/behaviour change), which aligns with risk-management adaptation; but the framing is fire-mitigation and forest-conservation policy (carbon emissions, biodiversity), so a mitigation/conservation reading is plausible and adaptation is not the stated objective. Evidence: "We compare CAC and PES under a stable climate and a climate change scenario." [p.2, Introduction] | "droughts increase the exogenous component of fire risk, reducing farmers' incentives to control own fires and to invest in fire-free techniques" [p.1, Abstract]
context_rationale: Drought risk under climate change is an experimental treatment and a research question. Evidence: "Is there a human-mediated, self-reinforcing loop between droughts (climate change) and fire use" [p.2, Introduction]
methodology_rationale: Framed field experiment with 384 farmers and questionnaires; empirical. Evidence: "This paper reports on a framed field experiment, testing smallholders' fire use and control on private land in the Brazilian Amazon." [p.1, Introduction]
geography_rationale: Brazil is upper-middle income.

population_rationale: Smallholder rain-fed farmers in Zimbabwe. Evidence: "In Zimbabwe smallholder areas are predominantly semi-arid and rain-fed." [p.2, Introduction]
concept_rationale: Documents uptake of soil/water management and crop choice strategies, disaggregated by gender of household head. Evidence: "The identified differences in the uptake and usage of soil and water management practices within and across analogues, are shown in Table 9.3." [p.4, Results]
context_rationale: Climate-induced risks and warming/rainfall change drive the question (climate analogues). Evidence: "Surveys were carried out in smallholder areas at two 2050s climate analogue sites to assess smallholder climate-induced risks" [p.1, Abstract]
methodology_rationale: Household survey of 627 households with statistical comparison (chi-square). Evidence: "A total of 627 respondents representing different smallholder households were interviewed using semi-structured questionnaires at the study sites." [p.4, Methodology]
geography_rationale: Zimbabwe (lower-middle income).
period_language_rationale: Published 2015, English. Evidence: "© Springer International Publishing Switzerland 2015" [p.1]

population_rationale: Heads of farm households (avg 2.85 ha cropland) in Ghana and Burkina Faso; generic farmers, not commercial. Evidence: "The average household cultivates approximately 2.85 ha of cropland and majorly use rudimentary techniques" [p.5, Section 3.3]
concept_rationale: Analyses adoption of 12 adaptation strategies and determinants. Evidence: "identiﬁes factors that inﬂuence the number and choice of strategies implemented" [p.1, Abstract]
context_rationale: Weather extremes (drought, heat, flood) drive the study. Evidence: "The study area is prone to dry spell, heat wave and frequent ﬂooding." [p.3, Section 3.1]
methodology_rationale: Household survey of 450 households; Poisson and multivariate probit. Evidence: "This study uses data obtained from 450 heads of farm households in Upper East Ghana and Southwest Burkina Faso." [p.2, Introduction]
geography_rationale: Ghana and Burkina Faso.
period_language_rationale: Published 2017, English. Evidence: "Weather and Climate Extremes 16 (2017) 1–13" [p.1 header]

lead_rationale: R2 include. Sampled households average ~2 ha despite 'large-scale' wording; drought-driven drip-irrigation adoption measured. Population is the only doubt; include under the inclusive-at-margin rule.
second_reviewer_summary: Survey of 216 Xinjiang cotton households on how drought, hail and disease disasters shape adoption of drip irrigation. Concept, context and methods fit under the inclusive reading. The only doubt is farm scale: the paper describes large-scale production, but sampled households average about 2 ha and are not clearly commercial, so I include.
population_rationale: Cotton farm households in Xinjiang, but the authors call the area one of large-scale production, report large acreage, mostly leased land, hired labour and household incomes of 100,000-300,000 yuan; text says mean 2.172 ha while Table 3 shows 6.943 ha. Generic 'farmers' in an LMIC (China, upper-middle income) would be included unless clearly commercial-scale; borderline. Evidence: "As a representative area of large-scale production, the technology adoption behavior in agricultural production has certain typicality." [p.2, Section 2.1] | "Most cotton farmers have large acreage." [p.5, Section 3.2.2]
concept_rationale: Adoption of drip irrigation water-saving technology as a response to disaster types (drought, hail, frost), disaster stage and remediation. Evidence: "this study uses a binary logistic model to analyze the impact of disaster types and stages on cotton farmers’ application of drip irrigation water-saving technology" [p.1, Abstract]
context_rationale: Climate hazards (drought, hail, frost, wind) in arid Xinjiang drive the research question. Evidence: "The agricultural ecological environment in Xinjiang is fragile, and serious natural disasters often occur." [p.3, Section 2.2]
methodology_rationale: Questionnaire survey of 216 farmers analysed with binary logistic regression. Evidence: "A total of 216 questionnaires were collected, and few of the data were missing in some questionnaires." [p.4, Section 3.1]
geography_rationale: China is upper-middle-income (codebook explicit).
period_language_rationale: Published 2022, English. Evidence: "ORIGINAL RESEARCH published: 15 July 2022" [p.1]

population_rationale: Small-scale aquafarmers in Ghana (25 fish farmers plus 15 stakeholders); farmers are analysed as a distinct group for adaptation. Evidence: "The aim of this paper is to assess the awareness level and perception as well as adaptation strategies adopted by small scale aquafarmers on climate change" [p.3, Abstract]
concept_rationale: Beyond perceptions, the study records adaptation strategies actually adopted by farmers (tree planting, embankments, boreholes, stocking time), so it is not perception-only. Evidence: "With regards to adaptation strategies to cope with the impacts of climate change, 32% planted trees around ponds to serve as shade to reduce evaporation" [p.12, Results 3.4]
context_rationale: Aquaculture production with explicit climate hazard link (temperature, rainfall, floods, drought) driving the research question. Evidence: "Rainfall and temperature are the two most important climatic factors that affect aquaculture operations in Ghana." [p.9, Results 3.1]
methodology_rationale: Questionnaire survey (n=40) with descriptive statistics plus meteorological trend analysis. Evidence: "The study adopted stratification and simple random sampling technique in obtaining 40 respondents" [p.3, Abstract]
geography_rationale: Ghana (lower-middle income). Evidence: "Sunyani Aquaculture Zone of Brong Ahafo region of Ghana" [p.3, Public interest statement]

lead_rationale: Both reviewers: documentary literature review with no empirical data; fails methodology (literature reviews excluded).
second_reviewer_summary: Spanish-language review article on small-scale agriculture, crop diversification and adaptation in Nicaragua. Methods are a documentary literature synthesis with no empirical data or measurement approach, so it fails the methodology criterion (literature reviews excluded). Other criteria are met.
exclusion_reason: Methodology: literature-based documentary review/synthesis with no empirical data (excluded as literature review/conceptual).
population_rationale: Small-scale agricultural producers in Nicaragua are the stated subject (generic, discussed conceptually). Evidence: "Analizar estrategias integrales para optimizar los sistemas de producción agrícola a pequeña escala" [p.3, Introducción]
concept_rationale: Discusses adaptation strategies (crop diversification, water harvesting, cooperatives, training) but only as literature-based proposals; no adaptation action measured in any population. Evidence: "Señalar estrategias de adaptación ante el cambio climático que contribuyan a la resiliencia de la producción agrícola a pequeña escala" [p.3, Introducción]
context_rationale: Climate change, drought and rainfall variability frame the agricultural analysis. Evidence: "La falta de estos sistemas deja a las cosechas dependientes de las precipitaciones naturales más vulnerables" [p.6]
methodology_rationale: Authors state a documentary/literature-review approach with no primary data or empirical analysis; protocol excludes literature reviews and purely conceptual work. Evidence: "Este artículo se fundamentó en un enfoque documental basado en fuentes primarias y secundarias para procesar la información." [p.4, Material y métodos] | "Se realizó una revisión detallada de la literatura disponible" [p.4, Material y métodos]
geography_rationale: Nicaragua (lower-middle income). Evidence: "Producción Agrícola Sostenible y Seguridad Alimentaria en Nicaragua" [p.1]
period_language_rationale: Published 2024, Spanish. Evidence: "Vol. 12, No. 23, enero – junio 2024" [p.1]

population_rationale: Smallholder farmers in Climate Smart Villages, Nyando basin, Kenya (90 CSV adopters, 32 non-CSV). Evidence: "especially among poor rural small-scale farmers" [p.2, Abstract]
concept_rationale: Analyses adoption/dis-adoption of CSA practices and determinants of scaling, plus household decision-making. Evidence: "the study’s main objective was to assess determinants and or barriers and strategies to boost scaling up pathways for adopted CSA practices in Nyando basin" [p.2, Abstract]
context_rationale: Climate shocks (floods, drought, rainfall variability, pests) drive the question. Evidence: "Climate variant was the main cause of floods, drought, and the occurrence of new pests on crops and livestock." [p.2, Abstract]
methodology_rationale: Household panel surveys with logistic regression, t-tests and Engel curves. Evidence: "Primary data was collected for baseline, end-line and financial diaries panel data from 122 households." [p.2, Abstract]
geography_rationale: Kenya (lower-middle income). Evidence: "This study took place in Nyando basin which traverses through Kisumu and Kericho counties." [p.5, Methods 2.1]

lead_rationale: Both reviewers uncertain on population. Intensive, export-oriented pond aquaculture with farm budgets aggregated across sizes and no smallholder analysis; adaptation is modelled, not observed. Recommend exclude.
second_reviewer_summary: Cost-benefit modelling of autonomous adaptation by shrimp and catfish pond farms in the Mekong delta under sea-level-rise scenarios. Concept, context, method and geography are acceptable under the inclusive rule. The population is the issue: export-oriented, intensive, aggregated farm budgets with no smallholder analysis, so I lean towards exclusion but do not find commercial scale clearly established.
population_rationale: Farm-level analysis of pond shrimp and catfish grow-out farms in an LMIC. Catfish is described as intensive, export-oriented and highly capitalised/integrated, and data are aggregated across all farm sizes, so smallholders are not analysed as a distinct group; only improved extensive shrimp is linked to small-scale farmers. Borderline under the commercial-scale exclusion. Evidence: "Farming striped catfish in ponds is carried out at intensive scale" [p.7, Section 2] | "By using base production data aggregated for all farm sizes, we assume homogenous farm adaptation behaviour" [p.20, 7.1.3] | "improved extensive shrimp culture is more sustainable, both environmentally and economically, especially for small-scale farmers" [p.4, Executive Summary]
concept_rationale: Documents and costs farm-level autonomous adaptation (raising pond dikes, increased water pumping, input adjustments) and its effect on net income and NPV; adaptation actions and economic outcomes are the object of analysis. Evidence: "The first objective of this paper is to present an economic analysis of the direct costs of implementing a series of adaptation options at the farm level" [p.5, Introduction]
context_rationale: Aquaculture (agricultural production) with explicit climate drivers: sea level rise, flooding, salinity intrusion, drier dry seasons. Evidence: "sea level rise and attendant increased flooding (both coastal and riverine) and coastal salinity intrusion threaten the long-term viability of this important industry" [p.4, Executive Summary]
methodology_rationale: Applies a measurable method: farm-level cost-benefit analysis using survey-based production budgets, stakeholder interviews and GIS overlay of hydraulic model outputs. Not a review. Evidence: "interviews were conducted with 13 stakeholders comprising shrimp and catfish farmers, provincial aquaculture staff" [p.8, 3.2.1]
geography_rationale: Vietnam (lower-middle income), Mekong River delta. Evidence: "Autonomous adaptation to climate change by shrimp and catfish farmers in Vietnam's Mekong River delta" [p.1, title]
period_language_rationale: Published 2012, English. Evidence: "(2012). Autonomous adaptation to climate change by shrimp and catfish farmers in Vietnam's Mekong River delta." [p.2, citation]

population_rationale: Farmers in Susa county, Iran, a generic farmer sample (mean 13.6 ha, range 2-50 ha) with no sign of commercial/industrial scale; study frames its concern as smallholder/farm-level adaptation. Farm size range is somewhat wide, but the generic-farmer rule applies. Evidence: "Participants had an average of 13.6 ha of farmland distributed over a range of 2–50 ha." [p.4, 4.1]
concept_rationale: Documents adaptation strategies used by farmers (irrigation, crop change, drought-tolerant varieties) and the barriers to adopting them; this is adaptation process (uptake, decision-making constraints), not perception alone. Evidence: "Three major strategies were included: a new irrigation system (35 farmers) change in the type of cultivation (31 farmers); and planting of drought-tolerant varieties (26 farmers)." [p.5, 4.2]
context_rationale: Agriculture in drought-prone, semi-arid southwest Iran; drought and water scarcity drive the research question. Evidence: "Frequent and prolonged drought causing severe water shortages has led to the salinization and desertification of arable land" [p.2, Introduction]
methodology_rationale: Empirical qualitative case study with focus groups and key-informant interviews and thematic analysis. Evidence: "A systematically data-driven inductive thematic analysis was used to identify the main issues emerging from the data" [p.4, Methodology]
geography_rationale: Iran, treated as LMIC per codebook (Iran listed explicitly). Evidence: "Susa county, a historic region in Khuzestan province, located in southwestern Iran near the Iraqi border" [p.3, Methodology]
period_language_rationale: Published 2021, English. Evidence: "Journal of Arid Environments 189 (2021) 104487" [p.1 header]

lead_rationale: R2 include. Learning from seasonal forecasts and use of climate information by pastoralists is an adaptation process (knowledge/learning, access to climate information).
second_reviewer_summary: Survey of East African pastoralists testing whether they update rainfall expectations after receiving seasonal forecasts. It addresses learning and use of climate information services under drought risk, which fits adaptation processes; no behaviour change is measured, so concept is the only mild doubt. Include.
population_rationale: Pastoralists and agropastoralists (subsistence herders) in southern Ethiopia and northern Kenya. Evidence: "We test whether pastoralists in southern Ethiopia and northern Kenya update their expectations in response to forecast information." [p.1, Summary]
concept_rationale: Measures access to a climate information service (receipt of DMC seasonal forecast) and learning (belief updating) as an adaptation-relevant process, which fits learning/decision-making/access to services. However, the authors state they study only the updating process, not behavioural responses or outcomes, and the measured variable is subjective rainfall expectation. Borderline against the 'perception/awareness alone' exclusion. Evidence: "because we look solely at the updating process and not at outcomes" [p.16, note 4] | "Decision takers must then be able and willing to change behavior in response to updated climate beliefs." [p.2, Introduction]
context_rationale: Drought and rainfall variability in arid and semi-arid lands drive the research question. Evidence: "an area that has suﬀered repeated serious droughts in recent years" [p.2, Introduction]
methodology_rationale: Household survey with subjective probability elicitation and econometric (selection model, Tobit/OLS) estimation. Evidence: "The survey also included a novel elicitation of respondents’ subjective probability distribution over the upcoming climate state." [p.7, 4(a)]
geography_rationale: Ethiopia and Kenya. Evidence: "four in southern Ethiopia (Dida Hara (DH), Dillo (DI), Finchawa (FI), Wachile (WA)) and six in northern Kenya" [p.6, 4(a)]
period_language_rationale: Published 2007 (online 2006), English. Evidence: "World Development Vol. 35, No. 3, pp. 480–497, 2007" [p.1 header]

population_rationale: Empirical chapters study smallholder crop farmers, mixed crop-livestock households, pastoralists and young farmers in SSA (Malawi, Uganda, Zambia, Zimbabwe, Tanzania, Eritrea, Cameroon, Nigeria). Ch5 samples extension officers rather than farmers, but the subject is small-scale farmers. Evidence: "The focus of the book was predominantly dryland agricultural systems in which resourceconstrained smallholder farmers operate." [Ch13, p.1]
concept_rationale: Ch3 (multinomial logit of adaptation choice), Ch4 (adaptation strategies used), Ch5 (CA adoption), Ch7 (adaptation practices), Ch8-10 (gendered/youth adaptation and coping) assess adaptation processes. Ch2 (impact modelling critique), Ch11 (literature review) and Ch1/13 do not. Ch6 and Ch12 are borderline (see notes). Book-level concept is met by at least 6 chapters. Evidence: "Chapters 3-7 document a variety of local adaptation" [Ch1, p.8 (verbatim except en-dash)] | "This chapter explores perceptions of rural farmers in the Kigezi Highlands of climate change and variability, the types of crops they grow, and their planting times per season." [Ch4, p.2]
context_rationale: Rainfall variability, drought, dry spells and floods drive the research questions in all the empirical chapters (e.g. Kabale heavy rain and dry spells; Kalomo drought-prone; Omay arid agroecological region IV; Kilosa pastoralist drought). Evidence: "Conservation agriculture (CA) is one strategy that is being promoted in Zambia not only for improved productivity for food security for the majority rural population, but also as a climate change adaptation measure." [Ch5, Introduction]
methodology_rationale: Chapters 3, 4, 7, 8, 9, 10 use household surveys, FGDs, key-informant interviews; Ch5 uses interviews plus district reports; Ch6 FGD scoring plus rainfall records. Ch2 and Ch11 are reviews/critiques and Ch12 is a document-based policy assessment. The book as a unit contains measurable empirical methods. Evidence: "A total of 900 survey questionnaires were administered, substantiated by focus group discussions and key informant interviews in all districts." [Ch3, p.5] | "A total of 24 focus group discussions were conducted with 140 participants" [Ch9, Methods]
geography_rationale: All case studies are in LMICs: Malawi, Uganda, Zambia, Zimbabwe, Tanzania, Eritrea, Cameroon, Nigeria. Evidence: "the contributions include case studies from eight countries covering diverse issues such as crop modeling, economics of adaptation, vulnerability studies, livelihood analysis" [Ch1, p.7]
period_language_rationale: Published 2017/2018 (Elsevier/Academic Press), English. Evidence: "Beyond Agricultural Impacts ISBN 978-0-12-812624-0 http://dx.doi.org/10.1016/B978-0-12-812624-0.00001-6 © 2017 Elsevier Inc." [Ch1, p.1]

lead_rationale: Both reviewers: vulnerability/adaptive-capacity index with no adaptation action measured; codebook explicitly excludes 'vulnerability index without coping/adaptation responses'.
second_reviewer_summary: Cross-sectional household survey in a Bangladeshi delta that builds hazard vulnerability indices and links them to food consumption. Adaptive capacity is a proxy index of assets; no adaptation action or outcome of an adaptation response is assessed, and the sample is general delta households rather than smallholder producers. Fails the concept criterion (vulnerability-only).
exclusion_reason: Concept: vulnerability/adaptive-capacity index analysis with no adaptation action measured; population (mixed delta occupations) and agricultural context also borderline.
population_rationale: Sample is all delta-resident households (421) with heads in seven occupations; farmers are only ~26% and fishers ~21%, many are unskilled labourers, grocers, drivers, office workers. Smallholders are not analysed as a distinct group in a way that defines the population; interaction results by occupation do include farmer and fisher heads. Evidence: "main occupation of household head” variable (having seven categories – unskilled labourer, farmer, fisherman, office employee, boatman, driver, and grocer)" [p.9, 3.2.3] | "over 70% the sample consists of the unskilled, farming, and fishing categories." [p.10, 4.1]
concept_rationale: Study builds exposure-sensitivity, adaptive capacity (asset proxy) and vulnerability indices and regresses them on food access. No adaptation action, practice, or response is measured; this is a vulnerability index assessment (codebook: vulnerability index without coping/adaptation responses = exclude). Evidence: "We computed separate vulnerability indices for flood, cyclone, and riverbank erosion and assessed their effects on household food access through regression modelling." [p.1, Abstract] | "many researchers assess AC indirectly by using a household’s possession of five types of assets or capitals" [p.3, Section 2]
context_rationale: Clear climate hazard drivers (floods, cyclones, riverbank erosion) but the setting is delta households generally, with food access (not agricultural production) as outcome; agriculture is not the explicit focus (authors argue for moving beyond agriculture). Evidence: "improving food security in climatic hazard-prone areas of developing country deltas would require moving beyond agriculture or natural resources focus" [p.1, Abstract]
methodology_rationale: Structured household survey, PCA-weighted indices and GLM/logistic regression: a measurable empirical method. Evidence: "A structured questionnaire was used for data collection." [p.6, 3.1]
geography_rationale: Bangladesh (lower-middle income). Evidence: "Hatiya Upazilla (sub-district) of Noakhali District in the South-eastern part of Bangladeshi coasts" [p.3, 3.1]

population_rationale: Subsistence smallholder homestead farmers in Potshini, South Africa (upper-middle-income). Evidence: "Potshini, a Zulu subsistence farming community in the Okhahlamba Municipality of the Bergville district in South Africa" [p.2, Introduction]
concept_rationale: Documents adoption processes, decision-making, learning and dissemination of water-harvesting/water-use innovations (trench beds, run-on ditches, drip) by farmers, framed around drought and dry-spell risk and ability to adapt. Evidence: "The methodology focuses on fostering farmers’ critical thinking and ability to adapt their own agricultural practices to improve their livelihoods within the context of a changing environment." [p.3, Introduction]
context_rationale: Semi-arid, dry-spell-prone rainfed setting where water scarcity and drought risk drive the innovations; climate framing is explicit although not centred on climate change. Evidence: "investing in agricultural innovations is inherently risky, particularly in semi-arid regions prone to drought or dry-spells." [p.2, Introduction] | "Biophysical influences on innovation adoption include climate constraints, such as hail, frost and lack of rain in winter, as well as dry spells" [p.6, 3.3]
methodology_rationale: Participatory case studies, 55 structured interviews, matrix scoring and instrumented on-farm comparisons. Evidence: "Fifty-five structured interviews were conducted with the aid of local interpreters" [p.3, 2.1]
geography_rationale: South Africa (upper-middle-income). Evidence: "Bergville district of South Africa" [p.1, Abstract]

population_rationale: Cocoa farmers in Ghana described as small-scale; farm sizes in sample about 1.4-3.5 ha; no commercial-scale focus. Evidence: "productivity and income differential between small-scale cocoa farmers who adapt to climate change and those who do not adapt" [p.9, Conclusions]
concept_rationale: Measures adoption of climate change adaptation technologies, determinants, and effects on productivity and income. Evidence: "we employ propensity score matching to control for selection bias and to analyse adoption of adaptation technologies, its determinants as well as impact on cocoa productivity and incomes" [p.1, Abstract]
context_rationale: Cocoa production under rising temperature and unpredictable rainfall drives the research question. Evidence: "One of the key challenges that cocoa farmers have experienced in recent times is the issue of climate change, especially with unpredictable rainfall and rising temperature" [p.1, Introduction]
methodology_rationale: Structured household survey with logit and propensity score matching. Evidence: "The main data collection instrument used was a structured questionnaire." [p.3, 3.1]
geography_rationale: Ghana (lower-middle income). Evidence: "cocoa farmers in the Western and Brong-Ahafo Regions of Ghana" [p.2, 3.1]
period_language_rationale: Published 2020, English. Evidence: "Technology in Society 62 (2020) 101288" [p.1 header]

population_rationale: Smallholder cocoa households in Ghana (LMIC) compared across certified and non-certified groups. Evidence: "Smallholder cocoa production in Ghana provides an important case" [p.4, Methods] | "In Ghana, cocoa is produced predominantly by smallholder farmers" [p.4, Methods]
concept_rationale: Assesses uptake of climate-resilient measures and strategies, responses and recovery during the 2015-16 drought, and adaptability (adaptation processes and outcomes). Evidence: "certification has a strong effect on the adoption of basic management, e.g. fertilization, but a weak influence on more complex resilience strategies" [p.2, Abstract]
context_rationale: Explicit climate hazard (2015-16 El Nino drought) drives the research question in a cocoa production setting. Evidence: "We take the case of the 2015–16 drought-shock to cocoa production in Ghana" [p.2, Abstract]
methodology_rationale: Household survey, biophysical measurements and Coarsened Exact Matching with ATT estimation: measurable empirical method. Evidence: "we used Coarsened Exact Matching (CEM; Iacus et al., 2016), followed by estimation of the average treatment effect on the treated (ATT)" [p.8, Data analysis]
geography_rationale: Ghana is a lower-middle-income country. Evidence: "four districts of Ghana, Juabeso district (Western Region) and Fanteakwa South, Abuakwa North, and Suhum districts (Eastern Region)" [p.5, Study area]
period_language_rationale: Published 2022, English. Evidence: "JOURNAL OF LAND USE SCIENCE 2022, VOL. 17, NO. 1, 407–428" [p.2 header]

population_rationale: Ethnic minority smallholder cardamom cultivators in Yunnan (China) and Lao Cai (Vietnam), semi-subsistence livelihoods. Evidence: "Focusing on four case study villages, two in Yunnan, and two in northern Vietnam, we analyse the coping and adaptation strategies Hmong, Yao, Hani, and Yi minority farmers have adopted." [p.1, Abstract]
concept_rationale: Documents coping and adaptation strategies and livelihood diversification after the 2016 extreme winter. Evidence: "We examine how different households and village communities are attempting to cope with and/or adapt to external shocks" [p.2, Introduction]
context_rationale: Extreme cold, snow and hail events destroyed cardamom harvests; climate hazard drives the question. Evidence: "extreme weather in 2016 decimated the cardamom plantations of hundreds of farming households" [p.1, Abstract]
methodology_rationale: Multi-sited ethnographic interviews with thematic coding; qualitative empirical case study. Evidence: "Utilising a multi-sited ethnographic approach, the first and third authors completed semi-structured and conversational interviews" [p.2, Introduction]
geography_rationale: China (upper-middle income) and Vietnam (lower-middle income). Evidence: "Honghe Prefecture, Yunnan Province, China" [p.2]

lead_rationale: Both reviewers: researcher-managed on-station agronomic trial with no farmer adoption analysis (codebook exclusion: crop trial without adoption analysis).
second_reviewer_summary: A six-year on-station experiment comparing conservation-agriculture and conventional rice systems under variable rainfall. Climate framing and adaptation intent are clear, but the design is a researcher-managed agronomic trial with no farmer adoption or participation analysis, which the criteria exclude. Marginal under a very inclusive reading because it reports yields and gross margins.
exclusion_reason: Population and methodology: on-station agronomic experiment with no smallholder participants or adoption analysis.
population_rationale: On-station experiment at the AfricaRice research station; no smallholder households or farmers are studied or sampled (smallholders only referred to as the target of the findings). Evidence: "The study was conducted from 2015 to 2020 under rainfed upland conditions at the M'bé Africa Rice Center (AfricaRice) research station" [p.7, 2.1]
concept_rationale: Evaluates CA cropping systems as climate-risk adaptation options, with yield and economic return outcomes, but only agronomic performance, no farmer adoption/decisions. Evidence: "This study aimed to evaluate CA cropping systems that can minimize both economic and climatic risks under erratic climatic conditions" [p.2, Abstract]
context_rationale: Erratic rainfall and water stress drive the research question in rice production. Evidence: "upland rice is particularly sensitive to drought, especially at the flowering stage" [p.3, Introduction]
methodology_rationale: Agronomic field trial with no farmer adoption analysis; matches the codebook exclusion 'crop variety trial without farmer adoption analysis'. Evidence: "Six different cropping systems were tested from June 2015 and until end of 2016 in a randomized block design, with four replicates" [p.9, 2.2.2]
geography_rationale: Cote d'Ivoire, lower-middle income. Evidence: "research station in the center of Côte d’Ivoire" [p.7]
period_language_rationale: Published 2022 (manuscript 2021), English. Evidence: "Field Crops Research, 2022, 277, pp.108418" [p.1]

population_rationale: Rural customary-land farming families in Cela, Angola; subsistence smallholder agriculture, not commercial. Evidence: "The traditional occupation and source of family income essentially comes from agriculture." [p.7, Population]
concept_rationale: Heavy on vulnerability, land governance and perceptions, but it documents adaptation/coping practices (seed storage, restoring cassava/yams and small livestock, migration, planting in humid plots) and an adaptation deficit. Borderline but acceptable. Evidence: "Different strategies for coping/adapting to environment changes were also registered." [p.1, Abstract] | "nowadays we are restoring the cassava and yams plantation as well as animal breeding" [p.18, Results]
context_rationale: Recurrent drought and erratic rainfall drive the research question in an agricultural setting. Evidence: "The management of community rural land in Angola is aggravated by recurrent drought cycles" [p.1, Abstract]
methodology_rationale: Qualitative empirical study: 30 group and 68 individual interviews. Evidence: "there were in total, 30 group interviews and 68 individual interviews, involving a total of 414 people." [p.9, Methods]
geography_rationale: Angola is lower-middle income. Evidence: "one of 12 in the South Kwanza province, Angola" [p.6]
period_language_rationale: Published 2019, English. Evidence: "© Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2019" [p.1]

population_rationale: Farmers (rice and upland crops) and local officers in Tinh Bien district, Vietnam; authors refer to smallholder farmers on marginal lands. Not commercial-scale. Evidence: "being felt particularly acutely by smallholder farmers on marginal lands, such as those in the study area" [p.13, Conclusion]
concept_rationale: Documents farmers' and institutions' adaptation responses (crop switching, varieties, ponds, drip irrigation, canals) to variable water availability. Evidence: "They commonly switch to crops that require less water (e.g., cassava, peanut). They choose other rice varieties." [p.11, 3.3.2]
context_rationale: Climate-driven water availability (rainfall, temperature, drought, flood trends) drives the question. Evidence: "This paper explores climate factors affecting water resource availability in agriculture and some recent adaptations being adopted by farmers" [p.2, Abstract]
methodology_rationale: Key-informant interviews, field observation and 25 years of hydro-meteorological data. Evidence: "Fourteen people (six officers and eight farmers) were interviewed individually" [p.5, 2.2.1]
geography_rationale: Vietnam, lower-middle income. Evidence: "The study was conducted in Tinh Bien, a district of An Giang province" [p.3, Introduction]
period_language_rationale: 2024, English. Evidence: "IOP Conf. Series: Earth and Environmental Science 1306 (2024) 012014" [p.2 header]

population_rationale: Inland artisanal fishing households (small-scale, FAO traditional definition) in Ghana. Evidence: "In Ghana, fishing is practised on a small scale by rural fishing communities, largely along the Volta basins." [p.1, Introduction]
concept_rationale: Measures adaptation strategies used and their effect on catch per unit effort (outcome). Evidence: "This study assessed whether or not climate change adaptation strategies used by inland artisanal fishers improve fish catchability" [p.1, Abstract]
context_rationale: Climate change effects on inland fisheries (temperature, rainfall variability) drive the question; fisheries are within the agricultural scope. Evidence: "The country is expected to experience rising temperatures, increasing rainfall variability and sea-level rise" [p.2]
methodology_rationale: Household survey with econometric (CMP ordered probit) analysis. Evidence: "Primary data was collected using a semi-structured questionnaire." [p.2, 2.1]
geography_rationale: Ghana is lower-middle income. Evidence: "The study was conducted along the Volta Basin in the Brong Ahafo Region of Ghana." [p.2, 2.1]

population_rationale: Small-scale Hilsa fishers (fisheries) in coastal Bangladesh, an LMIC; sample described as very poor small-scale fishers. Evidence: "Climate change adaptation strategies for small-scale Hilsa fishers in the coastal area of Bangladesh" [p.1 title]
concept_rationale: Documents social, economic and ecological adaptation strategies (credit, alternative livelihoods, networking, participation in planning, technology change). Evidence: "what are small-scale fishers’ techniques for social, economic, and ecological adaptation to climate change?" [p.3, Introduction]
context_rationale: Fishery livelihoods under climate stress (cyclones, storm surges, flooding, temperature and rainfall change) drive the research question. Evidence: "various climate-related events, like cyclones, storm surges, coastal flooding, and sea level rise, threaten" [p.2, Introduction]
methodology_rationale: Mixed-method: in-depth interviews, FGDs, structured household questionnaires and secondary sources, with content analysis. Evidence: "A total of 240 in-depth interviews along with three focus group discussions were conducted" [p.5, 3.2]
geography_rationale: Bangladesh (lower-middle income). Evidence: "fieldwork was conducted in the southern Bangladeshi fishing communities of Shyamnagar, Kalapara and Cox’s Bazar Sadar Upazilas" [p.4, 3.1]

population_rationale: Smallholder family farmers (<70 ha) in semi-arid Bahia, Brazil. Evidence: "In this study area, smallholders are defined as owning less than 70 ha of land." [p.2, footnote 1]
concept_rationale: Tests and evaluates adaptation technologies (drip irrigation, balanced animal feed) and their economic returns, alongside a vulnerability diagnosis. Evidence: "test and evaluate the contribution that efficient irrigation and a balanced animal feed could have in increasing farmers’ resilience" [p.12, Discussion]
context_rationale: Drought, rainfall decline and warming in the semi-arid Sertão drive the question. Evidence: "average temperatures have increased~2 °C and rainfall has decreased~350 mm" [p.1, Abstract]
methodology_rationale: Climate trend analysis, baseline survey, on-farm monitoring with investment analysis and feeding trials. Evidence: "Sixteen farmers using drip irrigation systems (out of 40 total) were selected and monitored regularly for a period of 2–5 years" [p.5, 2.3]
geography_rationale: Brazil, upper-middle income. Evidence: "Our study focuses on the Bacia do Jacuípe county (hereafter BDJ), a territory within the Sertão in Bahía State" [p.4, 2.1]

population_rationale: Smallholder farming households (mean 2.1-2.5 ha common) in Kenya. Evidence: "from a sample population of 22,488 smallholders, a sample size of 100 households was drawn" [p.3-4, Research methods]
concept_rationale: Beyond perceptions, the study ranks current/desired adaptation strategies and measures adaptive capacity and adaptation constraints. Evidence: "The third objective targeted to evaluate current, and desired, adaptation options and ranking the resulting data using a Weighted Average Index" [p.2, Background]
context_rationale: Drought, rainfall variability and rising temperatures affecting crops and livestock drive the study. Evidence: "shifting precipitation patterns, rising temperatures, and intensifying droughts" [p.1, Abstract]
methodology_rationale: Household survey with indices and correlation analysis, plus met data, FGDs and KIIs. Evidence: "This study employed a cross-sectional survey (Kothari 2004) which captured data from the farming households across the four administrative Wards" [p.3, Research methods]
geography_rationale: Kenya (lower-middle income). Evidence: "Trans-Mara East sub-County, Kenya, is one of the five sub-Counties in Narok County" [p.3, Study area]

lead_rationale: R2 include (high). Adaptive and maladaptive strategies are measured among 506 smallholders, so not perception-only.
second_reviewer_summary: Cross-sectional survey of 506 smallholder/subsistence farmers in Libya measuring climate beliefs, risk perception and adaptive and maladaptive strategies. Because adaptation strategies are measured, it is not a perception-only study. All criteria are met.
population_rationale: Population stated as subsistence and smallholder farmers in Libya (upper-middle income). About 47% of respondents have a non-farming main occupation, but the label is generic farmers. Evidence: "The study population comprised subsistence and smallholder farmers who are primarily the backbone of agricultural activities in Libya" [p.3, 2.1]
concept_rationale: Mostly perception, awareness and risk-perception scales (excluded alone), but a Likert 'adaptation assessment' scale, maladaptation and self-efficacy are also measured and compared by socio-economic group; no concrete adaptation practice is measured. Genuine borderline, leaning include. Evidence: "The assessment of the adaptation of farmers towards climate change scored a mean of 16.15 ± 3.76 (range: 5–24)" [p.6, Results]
context_rationale: Arid/semi-arid Libya; irregular rainfall, extreme heat and drought drive the question. Evidence: "exposure to climate risks such as irregular rainfall, extreme heat, and droughts" [p.3, 2.1]
methodology_rationale: Structured questionnaire survey of 506 farmers analysed with t-tests, ANOVA and correlations. Evidence: "The final research sample included 506 farmers" [p.4, 2.2]
geography_rationale: Libya is upper-middle income. Evidence: "climatevulnerable regions of Libya" [p.3, 2.1]

population_rationale: Cocoa farmers in Ghana described as predominantly low-income smallholders; average sample farm 8 ha, above the 2-5 ha national mean but not commercial-scale. Evidence: "the majority of cocoa farmers in Ghana are low-income smallholders" [p.3, 2.1]
concept_rationale: Measures adoption and extent of income diversification as a climate coping/adaptation strategy and its determinants, plus income share from diversification. Evidence: "applied a Heckman two-step regression to investigate the probability and extent of cocoa farm income diversification" [p.1, Abstract]
context_rationale: Climate impacts (unpredictable rainfall, prolonged dry season) on cocoa yield drive the research question. Evidence: "unpredictable rainfall patterns (98.3%)" [p.5, 3.2]
methodology_rationale: Survey of 400 farmers with Heckman and beta regression. Evidence: "We gathered primary data from interviews with 400 cocoa farmers using the multi-stage sampling technique." [p.3, 2.2]
geography_rationale: Ghana, lower-middle income. Evidence: "The study was conducted in the Tepa and Bekwai Cocoa districts in the Ashanti Region of Ghana" [p.3, 2.1]

population_rationale: Low-input smallholder crop-livestock households in Nkayi District, Zimbabwe, disaggregated by wealth class. Evidence: "smallholder crop livestock farmers in a typical dryland agro-ecological zone in Zimbabwe" [p.1, Abstract]
concept_rationale: Simulates adoption and outcomes (yield, net returns, vulnerability, poverty) of adaptation packages (heat/drought-tolerant varieties, legumes, soil fertility) under climate scenarios. Evidence: "They consisted of switching to heat-tolerant long-duration cereal varieties (to retain cereal lifecycles) and to drought-tolerant legume varieties." [p.6, 2.2.2]
context_rationale: Drought-prone dryland; hotter, drier, more variable climate drives the analysis. Evidence: "Rainfed agriculture (<650 mm average annual rainfall) with frequent droughts (occurring in two out of five years)" [p.3, 2.1]
methodology_rationale: Crop, livestock and economic models calibrated with a survey of 160 households and field data, plus stakeholder workshops; model with empirical data qualifies. Evidence: "The simulations were calibrated with household-specific data collected by a study with 160 randomly selected farm households" [p.5, 2.2]
geography_rationale: Zimbabwe, lower-middle income. Evidence: "Nkayi District, Western Zimbabwe" [p.1, Abstract]

population_rationale: Apple farmers in Himachal Pradesh, India; 80-90% of apple cultivation is by small and marginal farmers. Evidence: "About 80–90% of apple cultivation is done by small and marginal farmers (landholding <1 hectare)" [p.3, Study Area]
concept_rationale: Goes beyond perception: documents farmers' adaptive responses (hail nets, agrochemicals, upslope shift of orchards, crop diversification) and compares them with scientists' recommended strategies. Perception is the main focus, so this is a mild borderline. Evidence: "farmers’ micro-scale adaptation to climate change seeks to resort to two kinds of fixes" [p.9, Conclusion] | "Farmers are resorting to a geographical fix in moving apple cultivation from lower hills to higher hills" [p.7, Section 29.5]
context_rationale: Agricultural setting with explicit climate stressors (reduced snowfall, erratic rainfall, warming, hail) driving the research question. Evidence: "apple cultivation is experiencing productionrelated difficulties due to adverse impacts of climate change" [p.4, Study Area]
methodology_rationale: 70 semi-structured farmer interviews plus scientist interviews and triangulation with meteorological data and reports. Evidence: "70 semi-structured interviews were conducted with apple farmers in Rohru and Jubbal districts" [p.4, Methodology]
geography_rationale: India (lower-middle income). Evidence: "The geographical context of my study is the Shimla district of Himachal Pradesh in India." [p.1, Abstract]
period_language_rationale: Published 2021, English. Evidence: "© Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2021" [p.1]

population_rationale: 584 smallholder horticultural farmers in East Java, mean land below 0.5 ha. Evidence: "73 smallholder farmers were selected per village using simple random sampling, yielding a total sample of 584 respondents" [p.4, Methods]
concept_rationale: Analyses adaptive financial behaviour (formal climate credit access, precautionary savings) as determinants-of-adoption style outcomes under climate risk. Evidence: "two adaptive strategies: accessing formal climate credit to support climate-resilient investments, and allocating post-harvest income into precautionary savings" [p.1, Abstract]
context_rationale: Agricultural setting with climate stress (temperature variability, drought, unpredictable rainfall) motivating site choice and the research question. Evidence: "increasing exposure to climate-induced challenges such as temperature variability, drought, and unpredictable rainfall patterns" [p.4, Methods]
methodology_rationale: Structured household survey analysed with IV-Probit/IV-Tobit. Evidence: "Data were gathered through enumeratoradministered structured surveys." [p.4]
geography_rationale: Indonesia (upper-middle income). Evidence: "This study was conducted in East Java Province" [p.4]

lead_rationale: Both reviewers uncertain on context. The stress is soil sodicity, not a climate hazard; climate is not what drives the research question. Recommend exclude.
second_reviewer_summary: Participatory on-farm trials with smallholders in sodic soils of Haryana, testing integrated soil-crop management with yield and income outcomes and some farmer practice surveys. The design is acceptable, but the stress addressed is soil sodicity and only loosely climate; whether this meets the climate-hazard and adaptation criteria is a judgement call for the lead.
population_rationale: Small-scale wheat farmers in sodic Ghaghar basin (small/marginal to large farmers in trials, farmer-level replicates). Evidence: "This study focuses on small–scale production systems in sodicity– affected Ghaghar basin of Haryana, India" [p.3, Methods]
concept_rationale: Evaluates adaptation practices (tolerant variety, nutrient and weed management, reclamation) with yield and income outcomes. Evidence: "participatory research trials on land reclamation (gypsum/pressmud) and crop management (varieties, nutrient management and weed control) practices were undertaken during 2016–2020" [p.1, Abstract]
context_rationale: Climate framing is explicit ('climate resilient') but the driving stress is soil/water sodicity and herbicide resistance, not a climate hazard; semi-arid monsoonal climate is only site description. Genuine borderline against the 'environmental change without climate specificity' rule. Evidence: "Maximizing opportunities for climate resilient agriculture is vital for global food security" [p.1, Abstract]
methodology_rationale: On-farm participatory trials plus a 105-farmer practice survey and economic analysis; but primarily an agronomic trial without adoption analysis (crop-trial exclusion). Evidence: "randomly selected 105 farmers [40 small and marginal (<2 ha), 40 medium (2–4 ha) and 25 large (>10 ha) farmers]" [p.5]
geography_rationale: India. Evidence: "sodicity–prone Ghaghar Basin of Haryana, India" [p.1]

lead_rationale: Both reviewers: on-station crop trial with no farmer adoption analysis (methodology exclusion).
second_reviewer_summary: On-station randomised block trials of drought-tolerant cereals and legumes in semi-arid Zimbabwe. The climate-smart crop framing is relevant, but the study is an agronomic crop trial with no farmer adoption, perception or livelihood analysis, which falls under the methodology exclusion.
exclusion_reason: Methodology: on-station agronomic crop trial with no farmer adoption analysis (and concept: no adaptation process or farmer outcome measured).
population_rationale: Targets smallholder farmers in drought-prone Zimbabwe as the beneficiary population, but no farmers are studied (on-station trials). Evidence: "as climate smart crops for production in smallholder communities affected by climate change and variability" [p.5, Introduction]
concept_rationale: Tests agronomic performance of candidate climate-smart crops; no adoption, decision-making or farmer behaviour is assessed, only crop yield under drought. Evidence: "the objective of this study was to test the agronomic performance of a group of commonly grown cereal crops" [p.5, Introduction]
context_rationale: Drought in semi-arid Zimbabwe drives the research question. Evidence: "the station had 115 mm of rainfall, which was 28.75% of the normal seasonal average (400 mm)" [p.6, Results]
methodology_rationale: Randomized complete block crop trials on a research station and university department with no farmer adoption analysis; codebook excludes crop variety trial without farmer adoption analysis. Evidence: "The experimental design for both trials was a randomized complete block design" [p.5, Materials and Methods]
geography_rationale: Zimbabwe, lower-middle income. Evidence: "Makoholi Research Station in Masvingo Province, Zimbabwe" [p.5, Methods]
period_language_rationale: 2017, English. Evidence: "Afr. J. Food Agric. Nutr. Dev. 2017; 17(3): 12280-12294" [p.1]

lead_rationale: Both reviewers: workshop/opinion paper with no adaptation process or outcome measured and no assessment method.
second_reviewer_summary: A Current Opinion paper describing a four-day co-design workshop of researchers and practitioners to frame a future rangeland research agenda. It does not measure adaptation processes or outcomes and applies no assessment method, so concept and methodology clearly fail, even though the climate context and LMIC geography are met.
exclusion_reason: Concept and methodology: workshop/co-design reflection, no adaptation process or outcome measured, no empirical method on producers.
population_rationale: Participants are researchers and practitioners from collaboratives (herder groups, conservancies, ranchers, tribes) in Kenya, Mongolia and the US; no producer households are studied. Evidence: "researchers and practitioners from Kenya, Mongolia and the US West, gathered to develop a research-for-action project" [p.1, Abstract]
concept_rationale: Documents a research co-design workshop; no adaptation action or outcome is assessed, adaptation is only the motivation. Evidence: "The workshop goal was to co-design a research-for-action research project." [p.2, Workshop process]
context_rationale: Climate change impacts on water, pasture and pastoral livelihoods are named as the challenge driving the project. Evidence: "climate change and its impact on water, pasture and pastoral livelihoods is the immediate challenge to rangeland SESs" [p.3, The research project]
methodology_rationale: Conceptual/reflective account of one workshop (Current Opinion article) with no systematic data collection or analysis of adaptation; closest to opinion/conceptual piece. Evidence: "A focused research project and methodology was developed following the workshop and is not the subject of this paper." [p.5]
geography_rationale: Kenya and Mongolia are LMICs (US also involved). Evidence: "Social–ecological resilience to these changes has never been more urgent in our regions of focus, Kenya, Mongolia and the US West" [p.1]
period_language_rationale: 2016, English. Evidence: "Current Opinion in Environmental Sustainability 2016, 20:8–14" [p.1]

population_rationale: Rice/wheat farm families in one Iranian village; smallholder context (resource-poor farmers referenced), no commercial-scale focus. Evidence: "The farm families of Bakian were the target population (N ¼ 270)." [p.4, Method]
concept_rationale: Analyses adoption of co-produced adaptation strategies and their income, yield, quality of life and resilience impacts. Evidence: "identify the factors contributing to adoption of the co-produced knowledge and investigate the corresponding social, economic and environmental impacts" [p.1, Abstract]
context_rationale: Drought-induced water scarcity under climate change drives the study. Evidence: "Bakian has experienced severe meteorological and hydrological droughts in the" [p.2, Case description]
methodology_rationale: Mixed methods: interviews, participant observation, document analysis and a survey of 150 farmers. Evidence: "A mixed-method research was conducted comprising a case study on 19 informants selected using purposive sampling and a survey of 150 rice producers" [p.1, Abstract]
geography_rationale: Iran, upper-middle income. Evidence: "the Iran’s government applied the knowledge co-production approach and implemented an integrated participatory crop management (IPCM) project in the Bakian village, Fars province" [p.1, Abstract]

lead_rationale: R1 uncertain, R2 exclude: climate is one background stressor in a sustainability-transition gaming study; no climate adaptation is measured as such.
second_reviewer_summary: A participatory gaming and backcasting study with smallholder coffee farmers in Nicaragua, framed around a sustainability transition of agroforestry landscapes. Climate change appears only as one background stressor and no climate adaptation is measured as such. This is a marginal call resolved towards exclusion; a lead favouring inclusiveness could treat the climate-risk framing of the game as sufficient.
exclusion_reason: Context criterion borderline: climate change is one of several stressors framing a sustainability-transition study; not clearly the driver of the research question.
population_rationale: Smallholder coffee-based agroforestry farmers in rural Nicaragua (LMIC); farms of 2.4-10.7 ha. Evidence: "Tuma-La Dalia is the main town within the municipality and is surrounded by several remote smallholder communities." [p.3, Study area]
concept_rationale: Documents farmer decision-making, social learning, participation and co-produced management pathways for diversified agroforestry; these are adaptation processes, although framed as sustainability transition. Evidence: "we organized five participatory game sessions to explore farmer decision-making processes, farming strategies and to develop new networks and stimulate social learning among farmers" [p.1, Abstract]
context_rationale: Climate change is one of several drivers (with pests, price crises, land-use change); risk in the game is defined as income loss from climate change or pests. Climate is not clearly the research-question driver, so this is borderline between background and explicit hazard link. Evidence: "Risk was defined as income losses in case of coffee failure due to climate change or pest and diseases" [p.5, Methods] | "the alternation of drought and excessive rainfall" [p.3, Study area]
methodology_rationale: Empirical action research with serious-game sessions, pre/post-game surveys, video analysis and a backcasting workshop. Evidence: "we applied an action research approach based on participatory forecasting through serious gaming and participatory backcasting workshops" [p.2, Introduction]
geography_rationale: Nicaragua (lower-middle income). Evidence: "The municipality Tuma-La Dalia (13°08′N 85°44′W) is situated on the border of the Matagalpa and the Jinotega departments in central Nicaragua" [p.3, Study area]

lead_rationale: Both reviewers: biophysical soil moisture/temperature trial with no producers or adoption analysis.
second_reviewer_summary: A two-season soil-moisture and temperature field experiment comparing conservation farming basins, with and without biochar, with conventional tillage in Zambia. It is an agronomic trial with no farmer adoption or household analysis and only soil and biomass outcomes, so methodology (and arguably population) fails despite the climate-smart framing.
exclusion_reason: Concept and methodology: biophysical soil-moisture/temperature field trial with no adaptation process or farmer adoption/outcome analysis; no producers studied.
population_rationale: Practice (planting basins) is described as smallholder practice, but the study is a plot experiment in Mkushi; no farmers or households are surveyed or analysed. Evidence: "is a commonly used minimum tillage practice among small holders in southern Africa" [p.1, Abstract]
concept_rationale: Soil physics measurements (soil moisture, soil temperature, thermal conductivity) of a climate-smart practice under experimental plots; no adaptation process (decision, adoption, learning) and no household-level outcomes. Biomass yield is a secondary measure on plots. Evidence: "Here, we determine the effect on soil moisture and temperature of CF planting basins in a Zambian Acrisol." [p.1, Abstract]
context_rationale: Drought and soil temperature under climate change drive the research question in rainfed Zambian agriculture. Evidence: "Projected climate change in Sub-Saharan Africa involves increased drought and elevated soil temperature." [p.1, Abstract]
methodology_rationale: Agronomic/soil-physical field trial with sensors and a lab test; no farmer adoption analysis, which the codebook excludes for trials without adoption analysis. Evidence: "following a completely randomized block design with four blocks" [p.2, Methods]
geography_rationale: Zambia (lower-middle income). Evidence: "The experiment was established in Mkushi, Zambia" [p.2, Methods]

population_rationale: Farmers in drought-prone Anantapur district, India (LMIC); NICRA beneficiary and non-beneficiary farmers; no sign of commercial-scale operations. Evidence: "The sample consists of 60 farmers as beneficiaries from NICRA villages and 60 farmers as nonbeneficiaries from non-NICRA villages were selected randomly." [p.1, Abstract]
concept_rationale: Analyses constraints to adoption of climate-resilient technologies and farmers' suggestions: an adoption process study. Evidence: "the objective, to explicate the constraints faced by the farmers in the adoption of climate resilient technologies and suggestions to overcome the constraints" [p.2, Introduction]
context_rationale: Climate risk (rainfall deficit, drought) drives the study and the NICRA programme context. Evidence: "lack of sufficient rainfall, lack of owned resources, lack of short duration and drought tolerant crop varieties" [p.1, Abstract]
methodology_rationale: Structured interview survey of 120 farmers with scoring and ranking. Evidence: "The data was collected through the personal interview method." [p.2, Methods]
geography_rationale: India (lower-middle income). Evidence: "The current study was carried out in the Anantapur district of Andhra Pradesh, India." [p.1, Abstract]

population_rationale: Artisanal/subsistence oyster collectors (mostly women) in three Ghanaian fishing communities; small-scale fishery. Evidence: "Fishermen in New Amanful are basically artisanal fisher folks" [p.3, Materials and methods]
concept_rationale: Documents adaptation strategies (indigenous and research-based) adopted by men and women, constraints on adaptation choice. Evidence: "This paper examines adaptation strategies to changes in climate among female and male oyster collectors, constraints in the choice of adaptation strategies" [p.1, Abstract]
context_rationale: Fisheries livelihood with explicit climate stressors (high temperatures, floods, heavy rains, prolonged dry periods) driving the research question. Evidence: "categorized based on three climate stimuli, rainfall-related, temperature-related and value chain addition (prolonged dry periods)" [p.4, Research approach]
methodology_rationale: Interviews, FGDs, key informant interviews, ranking and Kendall correlation analysis on empirical data. Evidence: "Kendall tau-b correlation analysis performed on adaptation practices showed no significant correlation" [p.1, Abstract]
geography_rationale: Whin Estuary, Western Region, Ghana (lower-middle income). Evidence: "The study was undertaken in the Whin Estuary" [p.3, Materials and methods]

population_rationale: Smallholder farmers (members of farmer associations) in mountain Haiti. Evidence: "We discuss the findings from the focus groups held with 104 smallholder farmers from mountain areas." [p.1, Abstract]
concept_rationale: Documents coping/adaptation strategies in dry and wet years, decision-making criteria and use of climate information. Evidence: "Discuss coping strategies (both reactive and proactive) used during aforementioned years" [p.5, Table 1]
context_rationale: Rain-fed agriculture with droughts and hurricanes/wet years as explicit drivers. Evidence: "Farmers use different adaption strategies in years when they receive either too much or too little rainfall." [p.6, Results]
methodology_rationale: Structured focus group protocol with constant-comparative qualitative analysis. Evidence: "we used the constant comparative method" [p.4, Methods]
geography_rationale: Haiti, LMIC. Evidence: "Haiti's agrarian society is highly sensitive to changes in weather and climate conditions." [p.1, Abstract]

population_rationale: Tajik Indigenous smallholder mountain farmers growing wheat and barley. Evidence: "Qualitative ecological and cultural (eco-cultural) research was undertaken among the Tajik, an Indigenous community in the Taxkorgan" [p.4, Methods]
concept_rationale: Documents farmers' adjustment of sowing/crop calendar in response to climate and evaluates its yield implications (adaptation process and outcome). Evidence: "Survey data revealed that the sowing dates of important crops began earlier than previous decades." [p.1, Abstract]
context_rationale: Agriculture with explicit climate variability/warming link, drought-prone region. Evidence: "Taxkorgan is a drought-prone region" [p.15, Discussion]
methodology_rationale: Interviews/FGDs plus PLS regression of yield on climatic indices and NDVI phenology: empirical method. Evidence: "regressed with crop production data (1988-2017) from Taxkorgan County of Xinjiang, China, using the partial least square regression (PLS) technique" [p.1, Abstract]
geography_rationale: Xinjiang, China (upper-middle income). Evidence: "Taxkorgan County (71.33E~77.02E, 35.62N~38.67N)" [p.4, Study area]

population_rationale: Registered smallholder maize farmers in South Africa (upper-middle-income). Evidence: "218 randomly sampled registered smallholder maize farmers in two selected municipalities of Ehlanzeni district" [p.2, Specifications Table]
concept_rationale: Documents utilisation of adaptation strategies and change in output and income attributed to climate. Evidence: "the prominent strategies used by the smallholder maize farmers were the use of crops rotation (90.4%)" [p.5, 2.3]
context_rationale: Maize production with explicit climate variability link driving the question. Evidence: "largely attributed to issues relating to the vagaries of climate variations experienced during these two growing seasons" [p.3, 2.1]
methodology_rationale: Structured-questionnaire household survey with descriptive statistics and paired t-tests. Evidence: "The collected data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and tTest analysis." [p.7, Methods]
geography_rationale: South Africa is upper-middle-income. Evidence: "Ehlanzeni district, Mpumalanga, South Africa" [p.2, Specifications Table]

lead_rationale: R2 include. Designs and evaluates an index-based livestock insurance tool for pastoralists; protocol admits studies that propose/apply a measurement tool. Aggregate data and no uptake measured make it marginal.
second_reviewer_summary: Designs and evaluates a composite climatic index for index-based livestock insurance for nomadic herders in Iran, using satellite, meteorological and mortality data. It proposes and tests an adaptation-aligned risk-management tool, which the protocol admits, though no uptake or herder outcomes are measured. I would include it, with medium confidence because of the tool-only concept and aggregate data.
exclusion_reason: Borderline on concept: insurance-index design/simulation on provincial aggregate data, no household-level adaptation process or outcome measured; population is not analysed at household level.
population_rationale: Nomadic small-ruminant herders in Kerman, Iran (upper-middle-income), small-scale pastoral livestock keepers; analysis is at provincial aggregate level. Evidence: "The primary activity of these nomads is raising small ruminants (sheep and goats)" [p.2, Introduction]
concept_rationale: Designs and simulates an index-based livestock insurance (a risk-transfer adaptation instrument) and relates climate index to mortality; no farmer adoption, behaviour or realised outcomes are measured, so it is a tool-design study. Aligns with adaptation objectives (risk reduction) but is borderline against 'adaptation action measured'.
