Evidence: "helps nomads adapt to the negative shocks resulting from climate change" [p.2, Introduction] | "the primary objective of this research is to design and evaluate a composite climatic index" [p.3, Introduction]
context_rationale: Drought and rangeland stress in an arid/semi-arid province drives the research question. Evidence: "Kerman province is one of the most vulnerable regions in Iran to drought and climate change" [p.2, Introduction]
methodology_rationale: PCA and threshold regression applied to 11 years of empirical mortality, climate and satellite data. Evidence: "livestock mortality statistics were collected for 11 years (2013/03–2024/03)" [p.3, 2.1.1]
geography_rationale: Iran is upper-middle-income. Evidence: "Kerman province was selected as the study area" [p.4, 2.3]
period_language_rationale: Published November 2025, English. Evidence: "Available online 7 November 2025" [p.1]

population_rationale: Smallholder wheat farmers in Ethiopia (low-income). Evidence: "the bulk of Ethiopian farmers are smallholders who primarily engage in rain-fed farming" [p.2, Introduction]
concept_rationale: Adoption of climate-smart practices is explicitly an adaptation process; determinants analysed. Evidence: "investigate the determinants of the adoption of CSAPs in Northwestern Ethiopia" [p.1, Abstract]
context_rationale: Rain-fed wheat with climate variability, drought and rainfall variability framing the question. Evidence: "agriculture in the region is predominantly reliant on rain-fed farming systems, rendering the sector highly susceptible to the effects of climate change and variability" [p.4, 3.1]
methodology_rationale: Household survey with multivariate probit. Evidence: "The factors that influence the adoption of CSAPs were determined using a multivariate probit (MVP) model." [p.1, Abstract]
geography_rationale: Ethiopia is low-income. Evidence: "East Gojjam zone ... located in the northwestern part of Ethiopia" [p.4, 3.1]

population_rationale: Smallholder farmers (heads of households deciding on the farm) in Musanze district, Rwanda. Evidence: "The Musanze district's smallholder farmers access and use climate services" [p.1, Abstract] | "Heads of households who make decisions about the farm were given the structured questionnaire." [p.3, Methods]
concept_rationale: Documents access to and use of climate information services (channels, products, perceived use for planning, seed choice, pest timing); access to services is a listed adaptation process and the study goes beyond perception alone. Evidence: "The availability of climatic services contributed to better selection of seeds and timing of pests and disease prevention." [p.1, Abstract] | "Planning and decisionmaking was highlighted by of 27% farmers, followed by 22% as the best option of selecting good seeds" [p.5, Results]
context_rationale: Rain-fed smallholder agriculture exposed to climate extremes (landslides, flooding, dry spells); climate shocks and extreme weather drive the research question. Evidence: "The Musanze district's smallholder farmers access and use climate services to lessen the effects of extreme events of weather and climate." [p.1, Abstract]
methodology_rationale: Structured questionnaire survey of 100 farmers analysed with SPSS; weak but measurable method. Evidence: "A total of 100 farmers in the district who are involved in agriculture and impacted on by climate change and variability were interviewed." [p.3, Methods]
geography_rationale: Rwanda is a low-income country. Evidence: "Rwanda Meteorology Agency, P.O Box 898 Kigali, Rwanda" [p.1]

population_rationale: Pastoral households keeping cattle, camels, goats and sheep in Borena zone (small-scale, mean income about ETB 26,600/yr). Evidence: "The average household is very poor with annual income of ETB 26,631" [p.8] | "index-based livestock insurance sold to pastoral households in southern Ethiopia" [p.2, Abstract]
concept_rationale: Evaluates uptake of drought index insurance (a formal risk-management/adaptation instrument) and its outcomes (income, milk production, herd size, savings, consumption) in drought and non-drought periods. Evidence: "we find that they increase household income and milk production during drought years" [p.2, Abstract]
context_rationale: Drought risk in arid/semi-arid pastoral southern Ethiopia drives the insurance design and analysis (June-September 2014 drought). Evidence: "including the severe drought from June to September 2014, which was followed by payouts to insurance holders" [p.3, Introduction]
methodology_rationale: Panel household survey, randomised encouragement design with IV. Evidence: "Exploiting random encouragement designs that generate exogenous variations for insurance uptake" [p.3, Introduction]
geography_rationale: Ethiopia is low income. Evidence: "the Borena zone of southern Ethiopia" [p.3]

population_rationale: Nationally representative rural farm households in Zambia (RALS, over 8,000 farmers) and Malawi (IHS3) relying on rain-fed subsistence agriculture; smallholder framing. Evidence: "Most households in rural areas of developing countries rely on rain-fed agriculture for their livelihoods" [p.2, Introduction] | "suggesting potential barriers to diversification for smallholders" [p.30, Conclusions]
concept_rationale: Analyses livelihood diversification (crop, livestock, labour, income) as an adaptation response to rainfall variability and links it to vulnerability indicators. Evidence: "The two case studies demonstrate that diversification is clearly an adaptation response" [p.1, Abstract]
context_rationale: Rainfall variability, drought and flood risk in Zambia and Malawi explicitly drive the research question. Evidence: "Climate variability, associated with farm-income variability, is recognized as one of the main drivers of livelihood diversification strategies in developing countries." [p.1, Abstract]
methodology_rationale: Chapter synthesises two empirical econometric studies on survey data merged with rainfall records; original Zambia analysis plus synthesised Malawi study, not a literature review. Evidence: "All models are estimated using tobit model specification" [p.20]
geography_rationale: Zambia and Malawi are LMICs. Evidence: "Zambia ranks 15th in the list of countries that are most vulnerable to climate change" [p.7]

population_rationale: Smallholder maize farmers (communal, A1, old resettlement) in Zimbabwe. Evidence: "Communal, A1 and old resettlement areas are classified as small-scale farming areas in Zimbabwe" [p.5, 2.3 Data]
concept_rationale: Analyses willingness to adopt (uptake) a climate-smart conservation agriculture package and its determinants (perceptions, extension, subsidies). Evidence: "further analyses how their overall perceptions, combined with key socioeconomic and institutional factors, shape their willingness to use the innovation for climate change adaptation" [p.3, Introduction]
context_rationale: Pfumvudza is framed as a climate-resilient practice (drought moisture conservation) that drives the question; climate is more than background. Evidence: "The Zimbabwean government introduced the Pfumvudza climate-smart agriculture initiative to promote climate-resilient agriculture" [p.2, Abstract]
methodology_rationale: Cross-sectional household survey (n=408), FGDs and key-informant interviews; endogenous switching probit. Evidence: "Data was collected from a representative sample of 408 smallholder farmers" [p.2, Abstract]
geography_rationale: Zimbabwe (lower-middle income). Evidence: "This study was done in Mashonaland East Province of Zimbabwe" [p.4, 2.1]

population_rationale: Wheat farmers (generic farmers label) in Kermanshah, Iran; not clearly commercial-scale. Evidence: "The population of this study comprised of wheat farmers in which 293 farmers were selected" [p.1, Abstract]
concept_rationale: Beyond hazard/vulnerability mapping, the survey records farmers' use of drought coping and adaptation practices (varieties, tillage, irrigation, forecasts, insurance) as adaptive-capacity indicators, so adaptation responses are measured. Evidence: "The ratio of farmers who used meteorological forecasting to the total number of farmers" [p.5, Table 6]
context_rationale: Drought in rain-fed, semi-arid agriculture drives the research question. Evidence: "Iran is located in a dry and semi-arid climate" [p.1, Introduction]
methodology_rationale: Questionnaire survey plus SPI/SDI station data with weighted index construction. Evidence: "Vulnerability questionnaire was distributed among the statistical population, and finally, 293 questionnaires were completed" [p.7, 2.2]
geography_rationale: Iran (LMIC). Evidence: "Kermanshah Township in the northwestern part of Iran" [p.1, Abstract]

lead_rationale: Both reviewers: fertilizer/yield-response study with no climate framing (concept and context fail).
second_reviewer_summary: An agricultural economics study of fertilizer use and yield response among smallholders in the Nigerian Sudan savannah. It has no climate-risk or adaptation framing, so concept and context clearly fail even though population, methods, geography and date are acceptable.
exclusion_reason: Concept and context fail: fertilizer/soil-fertility agronomy with no climate-adaptation measurement or climate-risk framing.
population_rationale: Smallholder mixed-farming households in Nigeria. Evidence: "Nigerian agriculture is dominated by smallholder and traditional farmers" [p.2, Introduction]
concept_rationale: About fertilizer use, soil fertility and productivity; no climate adaptation process or outcome is measured (general agronomy without climate-risk framing). Evidence: "this paper examines the extent to which the nutrient requirement for the major crops grown in the Sudan Savannah zone is met" [p.2, Introduction]
context_rationale: Drought appears in a single sentence as a consequence of soil degradation; the research question is nutrient depletion and productivity. Evidence: "The loss of fertility reduces yields and affects water holding capacity, leading to greater vulnerability to drought." [p.5]
methodology_rationale: FGDs and semi-structured interviews analysed with descriptive statistics. Evidence: "Analysis of the data was done using descriptive statistics including percentages, mean and ratios" [p.2, Methodology]
geography_rationale: Nigeria (LMIC). Evidence: "farmers selected from Sudan Savannah zone of Nigeria" [p.2, Methodology]

lead_rationale: Both reviewers: regional delta risk mapping with no producer population and no adaptation measured.
second_reviewer_summary: Regional multi-hazard risk and vulnerability mapping of two Chinese deltas with EbA policy recommendations. No smallholder producers are studied and no adaptation action or outcome is measured, so population and concept fail clearly.
exclusion_reason: Population (no smallholder/producer population; city-level units), concept (vulnerability/risk index with no producer adaptation action measured) and context (not an agricultural setting).
population_rationale: Unit of analysis is 36 cities in two urban-industrial deltas; no households or producers are studied. Agriculture is only one 'key sector' in a policy table. Evidence: "we mapped the multi-risk at the city level" [p.16, 4.3 Limitations]
concept_rationale: Vulnerability/risk index mapping (GDRI, DELTA-ES-SES) with EbA options proposed from literature and policy review; no adaptation action by producers is measured (codebook: vulnerability index without adaptation responses = exclude). Evidence: "map high disaster risk areas in the Pearl River and Yangtze River deltas" [p.1, Abstract]
context_rationale: Revised before comparison (resume check): climate hazards are explicit, but the setting is deltaic/urban social-ecological systems at city level, not an agricultural production setting; agriculture is only one sector row in Table 2. The codebook requires an agricultural setting with a climate link. Evidence: "multiple environmental hazards (flooding, cyclones, storm surges, drought, salinity intrusion and pollution) are considered" [p.5, 2.2]
methodology_rationale: Indicator-based quantitative risk assessment with expert consultation and policy review is a measurable method. Evidence: "An expert consultation was carried out to understand the socio-economic and environmental settings and determine final indicator lists" [p.5, 2.2]
geography_rationale: China is upper-middle-income. Evidence: "Pearl River and Yangtze River deltas, China" [p.1, title]
period_language_rationale: Published 2024/2025 in English. Evidence: "Received 15 December 2023; Received in revised form 1 October 2024; Accepted 4 December 2024" [p.1]

population_rationale: Smallholder maize farmers (99.7% smallholders; mean farm 1.08 ha) in Ghana. Evidence: "cross-sectional data covering 197 smallholder maize farmers in the Cape Coast Metropolitan Assembly" [p.2, Abstract]
concept_rationale: Adoption of climate variability adaptation strategies and their effect on maize yield (adaptation outcome). Evidence: "objective of this article is to examine the effect of climate variability adaptation strategies on maize yield" [p.2, Abstract]
context_rationale: Climate variability (rainfall, temperature) in rainfed maize production drives the question. Evidence: "erratic rainfall and droughts constitute major climate factors that cause food insecurities" [p.3, Introduction]
methodology_rationale: Household survey with multiple regression and IPWRA treatment-effect model. Evidence: "the study employs two empirical models: (1) multiple linear regression (MLR) and (2) inverse probability weighting regression adjustment (IPWRA)" [p.7, 2.7]
geography_rationale: Ghana is lower-middle-income. Evidence: "Ghana's Central Region, specifically, the Cape Coast Metropolitan Assembly" [p.5, 2.1]

population_rationale: Pastoral and agro-pastoral households keeping livestock in drought-prone southeastern Ethiopia. Evidence: "198 randomly selected households using a semi-structured questionnaire" [p.1, Abstract]
concept_rationale: Beyond perceptions, the study documents adaptation actions and outcomes: drought coping strategies (herd mobility, destocking, shifting to camel/goat), history of camel adoption, and drought mortality and milk yield by species (resilience). Not perception-only. Evidence: "cattle keepers shifting to have more camel and goat in response to prevailing drought in the study area" [p.1, Abstract] | "The Fig. 9 displays farmers coping strategic measures taken to reduce the impacts of recurring drought." [p.13, 3.5]
context_rationale: Drought, rainfall decline and warming in arid/semi-arid rangelands drive the question. Evidence: "Pastoralism in the study area is constrained by drought, erratic rainfall, poor livestock productivity" [p.3, 2.1]
methodology_rationale: Household survey, KIIs, FGDs and 32-year meteorological trend analysis. Evidence: "The study used a mixed research approach whereby quantitative and qualitative data were gathered from multiple sources" [p.1, Abstract]
geography_rationale: Ethiopia is low-income. Evidence: "Southeastern Ethiopia" [p.1, title]

population_rationale: Study focuses on smallholder (communal and emerging) cattle farmers in South Africa using NIDS household data; the sample is smallholder cattle households (mean herd 8). Evidence: "The study assessed the relationship between drought and cattle destocking as well as factors that affect farmers' destocking decision." [p.1, Abstract] | "Out of the 311 smallholder cattle households captured in the survey" [p.4, Results]
concept_rationale: Destocking is analysed as a drought coping/mitigation response and its determinants are estimated (adaptation action measured), not only impacts. Evidence: "This study investigated the coping strategy of smallholder cattle households towards drought shock." [p.2, Conceptualisation]
context_rationale: Drought (SPI) is the explicit climate hazard driving the research question in a livestock setting. Evidence: "This study used the SPI in the measurement of drought as shown in Table 2." [p.3, Methods]
methodology_rationale: Empirical quantitative analysis: correlation of SPI with beef output and zero-inflated Poisson regression on household survey data. Evidence: "determinants of destocking were identified through the zeroinflated Poisson (ZIP) regression model" [p.1, Abstract]
geography_rationale: South Africa is an upper-middle-income country (codebook names it explicitly). Evidence: "Empirical analysis of drought-induced cattle destocking in South Africa" [p.1, Title]
period_language_rationale: Published 30 March 2024, in English. Evidence: "Published: 30 Mar. 2024" [p.1]

population_rationale: 400 subsistence farm households, grouped as small/medium/large subsistence farmers (up to 15 acres); ~79% small subsistence farmers. Evidence: "Primary data of 400 subsistence farm households were collected using a structured questionnaire survey." [p.2, Sampling]
concept_rationale: Crop insurance is framed as an adaptation/risk-management tool to floods; willingness to purchase (adoption decision) and its determinants are measured. Hypothetical WTP rather than actual uptake, but this is an adoption-decision study of an adaptation instrument. Evidence: "Crop insurance has become an important adaptation tool for managing economic and environmental risk in the agricultural sector." [p.2, Introduction]
context_rationale: Flood risk in flood-prone districts drives the research question. Evidence: "Primary data were collected from 400 farm households through a structured questionnaire in four flood-prone districts" [p.1, Abstract]
methodology_rationale: Structured household survey with probit regression, risk perception scale and risk-attitude elicitation (ELCEM). Evidence: "A probit model approach was used to examine the influence of various socio-economic factors on farmers' decisions." [p.4, 2.6]
geography_rationale: Pakistan, lower-middle-income. Evidence: "four districts, namely, Charsadda, Mardan, Peshawar, and Nowshera of KP province, Pakistan" [p.2, Study area]

population_rationale: Rural subsistence farming households (mean farm size 3.77 ha) in Southwest Nigeria. Evidence: "The population of the study consists of rural farm families in the zone which predominantly practice subsistence farming." [p.6-7, 3.2]
concept_rationale: Adoption of CSA practices (adaptation) and its relation to food security/dietary diversity outcomes. Evidence: "The study investigates the effects of CSA practice on the food security status of rural farming households in Nigeria." [p.1, Abstract]
context_rationale: Climate variability/change, drought and flooding are the framing for CSA adoption and food security. Evidence: "climate-related events such as flooding and drought" [p.2, Introduction]
methodology_rationale: Household survey (480 households), HDDS/HFCS indices and probit regression. Evidence: "The Probit regression model was used to determine the effect of CSA practices on the food security status of rural farming households" [p.7, 3.2]
geography_rationale: Nigeria, lower-middle-income. Evidence: "The research was conducted in rural Southwest, Nigeria" [p.6, 3.1]
period_language_rationale: Published 2024 online / 2025 volume, English. Evidence: "Environment, Development and Sustainability (2025) 27:17077-17094" [p.1]

lead_rationale: Both reviewers uncertain on concept. Oasis farmers' responses to water scarcity in an arid zone (codebook: water scarcity in semi-arid/arid areas implies climate) with resilience assessment; include at the inclusive margin and flag.
second_reviewer_summary: Resilience and stakeholder analysis of Tunisian oasis farming under water scarcity. Population, method, geography and period are fine; whether it documents climate adaptation processes or outcomes rather than general SES sustainability is borderline. A lenient reading could include it as farmer responses to water scarcity in an arid zone.
exclusion_reason: Borderline on concept (and partly context): SES resilience/governance and stakeholder-perception study in which adaptation actions and the climate hazard are not clearly the measured focus.
population_rationale: Oasis farm owners in Gabes, Tunisia; most holdings are very small (67% below 0.5 ha), so small-scale producers. Evidence: "Notably, 67% of lands are below 0.5 ha" [p.5, Results 3.1]
concept_rationale: Documents governance, stakeholder connectivity, access to support and some farmer responses to water scarcity (off-farm income, extra wells, diversification) and co-developed improvement options, but adaptation actions are not measured as the core variables; the analysis is SES-resilience/power mapping, largely perception based. Evidence: "farmers have been adapting by making new decisions and adopting different strategies" [p.10, 3.5]
context_rationale: Arid oasis agriculture (100-300 mm/yr) with water scarcity driving the problem; codebook counts water scarcity/aridity in semi-arid areas. Climate is intertwined with industrial pollution, land tenure and finance. Evidence: "Rainfall is very low with only 100 to 300 mm/year" [p.3, 2.1 Study area]
methodology_rationale: Survey of 240 farmers plus 19 institutional stakeholders, power/influence scoring and a causal loop diagram: empirical method. Evidence: "a detailed survey was conducted with 240 farmers, 10 institutional stakeholders and 9 associations" [p.1, Abstract]
geography_rationale: Tunisia (lower-middle income). Evidence: "The oases of Gabès, located in southeastern Tunisia" [p.3, 2.1]

population_rationale: 600 smallholder farm household heads in three districts of Oromia, Ethiopia; rain-fed small-scale farming. Evidence: "introduced a hypothetical package of improved climate services to 600 randomly selected smallholder farmers in three districts" [p.1, Abstract]
concept_rationale: Assesses demand/preferences and WTP for climate information services (access to services) and participatory decision-making, plus current use of climate services and coping strategies; aligned with adaptation processes (access to services, decision-making). Evidence: "Climate services that are demand-driven, cost-effective, timely, and easy to access and understand can help vulnerable communities to adapt to climate variability" [p.1, Introduction] | "Fig. 5 shows the different coping strategies and the share of farmers who implement these strategies." [p.7, Section 3.3]
context_rationale: Rain-fed agriculture exposed to rainfall variability, drought and flooding drives the research question. Evidence: "climate related risks and variability will continue to have far-reaching consequences for the agricultural sector in Africa" [p.1, Introduction]
methodology_rationale: Household survey with discrete choice experiment and G-MNL econometric model; empirical. Evidence: "Primary data were collected through a survey of 600 household heads in the three districts in October 2017." [p.3, Section 2.2]
geography_rationale: Ethiopia (low income). Evidence: "The study was carried out in three districts of the Oromia region: Kersana Malima, Ada'a and Dodota" [p.3, Section 2.2]

lead_rationale: R2 include. Technical report with a primary household survey including weather-information use and adaptive capacity; climate-adaptation share of the report is moderate. Include at the margin.
second_reviewer_summary: Africa RISING technical report on evergreen agriculture for smallholder resilience in semi-arid Tanzania and Malawi, including an analysis of weather-information use and adaptive capacity. Meets the criteria at the inclusive margin; the climate-adaptation share of the report is moderate, hence medium confidence.
exclusion_reason: Concept borderline: adaptation is not clearly the measured object (baseline constraints survey plus literature review of evergreen agriculture); climate/adaptation content is largely descriptive or recommendatory.
population_rationale: Smallholder maize-mixed and agro-pastoral farmers (1-4 ha, household heads) in Tanzania and Malawi. Evidence: "60% of the population owns small land holdings (1- 4 ha per household)" [p.3, Narrative summary] | "Trees/shrubs are an integral component of small-scale farming systems in the region" [p.2]
concept_rationale: Report is mainly a baseline of constraints plus a literature synthesis of evergreen agriculture. Adaptation is addressed through documentation of farmers' coping/adaptation strategies, access/use of weather information and tree retention/fertilizer use, but little is measured as an adaptation process or outcome. Genuine borderline. Evidence: "Women in Kiteto and Kongwa adapt climate changes by working for food, relief food, selling hand crafts" [p.54, 3.4.5] | "The awareness of farmers on weather forecast information from the Tanzania Mateorological Agency (TMA) is low and farmers rarely use this information" [p.5, Output 4]
context_rationale: Semi-arid districts with erratic rainfall; drought is the main stated vulnerability and drives the weather-information and yield-stability components. Evidence: "drought, which was the factor most farmers (85.4%) associated with low crop yield" [p.31, 3.2.1] | "The main source of vulnerability in this farming system is drought, which leads to crop failure" [p.11]
methodology_rationale: Primary structured household survey (n=365), PRA/FGDs, soil analysis, tree inventory and Landsat classification; some sections are literature review but the report also contains original empirical data. Evidence: "About 365 farmers were interviewed in Kiteto and Kongwa districts" [p.13, 2.2.1] | "The satellites images used were Landsat of year 1987 and Landsat of 2010." [p.14, 2.2.3]
geography_rationale: Tanzania and Malawi are LMICs. Evidence: "This research was carried in Kongwa and Kiteto districts in Tanzania." [p.12]

lead_rationale: Both reviewers: regenerative farming framed around mitigation; climate background only (context fails).
second_reviewer_decisive_issue: context (climate as background only; concept mitigation-oriented)
second_reviewer_summary: Survey of Pakistani farmers on communication campaigns and resistance to adopting regenerative farming. Climate is global background and the practice is mitigation/soil oriented, with no climate hazard or adaptation objective in the research question, so context clearly fails.
exclusion_reason: Concept and context criteria fail: regenerative-farming adoption intention framed around mitigation/carbon with climate only as background; no adaptation to a climate hazard.
population_rationale: Crop farmers in Punjab, Pakistan; no commercial-scale focus stated (generic farmers label in an LMIC). Evidence: "the respondents must be farmers, direct growers of the crops and (b) they must be adults" [p.8, Research Design]
concept_rationale: Measures intention to adopt regenerative farming and innovation-resistance barriers; regenerative farming is framed mainly as carbon sequestration/mitigation and soil conservation, not as adaptation to a climate hazard. Generic technology-adoption psychology. Evidence: "regenerative farming can considerably contribute to the reversal of climate change by decreasing the agriculture sector's carbon footprints" [p.2, Introduction]
context_rationale: Climate change is background (emissions, soil carbon); no climate hazard (drought, flood, variability) drives the research question. Evidence: "Climate change is pretentious and a severe threat to the world, fueled by growing carbon dioxide (hereafter CO2) and greenhouse gasses" [p.2, Introduction]
methodology_rationale: Cross-sectional survey of 863 farmers analysed with SEM. Evidence: "A sample of 863 farmers participated by responding to the self-administrated questionnaire." [p.1, Abstract]
geography_rationale: Pakistan (lower-middle income). Evidence: "data was collected from 863 farmers located in the Punjab region of Pakistan" [p.8, Research Design]

population_rationale: Smallholder paddy and vegetable farmers (and landless) in the Ayeyarwaddy Delta, Myanmar (LMIC). Evidence: "finding new low cost techniques for smallholder farmers to restore the soil fertility, fight pests and diseases, and reduce farmers' vulnerability to climate change" [p.1, Abstract]
concept_rationale: Documents farmer-led testing and farmer-to-farmer extension of agroecological practices as responses to climate stress, with outcomes (yield, gross margin, quality) and processes (learning, participation). Evidence: "reduce farmers' vulnerability to climate change, thus enhancing the resilience of their farming systems" [p.1, Abstract]
context_rationale: Agricultural setting with explicit climate hazards (floods, cyclones, erratic rainfall, sea-level rise) motivating the practices, although soil fertility and pests are equally prominent drivers. Evidence: "Due to climate change, farmers also face new challenges like floods, strong winds, and heavy and unstable rains." [p.1, Abstract]
methodology_rationale: On-farm trials with control plots, indicators and gross-margin analysis; empirical descriptive case. Evidence: "All the trials compared farmers' practices (control plot) called Farmer's Practice plot (FP) and Innovative Practice plot (IP)" [p.4, Results and Discussion]
geography_rationale: Myanmar is lower-middle income. Evidence: "Bogale and Mawlamyinegyun townships" [p.1, Introduction]
period_language_rationale: English; trials in 2016-17 and references to 2017 imply publication 2017 or later (no year printed). Evidence: "in summer 2016-17, six paddy innovative farmers made trials" [p.4]

lead_rationale: Both reviewers: perception of organic farming; climate appears only in the abstract (concept and context fail).
second_reviewer_summary: Perceptions of organic farming among Indonesian smallholders. The abstract invokes climate adaptation but the body has no climate hazard or adaptation measurement; a perception-only analysis of an agronomic innovation fails concept and context.
exclusion_reason: Concept (perception/adoption of organic farming without measured climate adaptation) and context (climate as background only) criteria not met.
population_rationale: Smallholder horticultural (vegetable) farmers in one village in Indonesia (upper-middle income). Evidence: "Giripurno Village is a representation of horticultural farmers funded by the government to develop 10 hectares of organic farming" [p.3, Methods]
concept_rationale: Measures farmers' perceptions of organic farming innovation characteristics and adoption stage; no adaptation action is measured beyond perception, and organic farming is treated as a sustainability innovation rather than adaptation in the analysis. Perception alone is excluded. Evidence: "This research aims to analyze the factors that shape farmers' negative perceptions of organic farming and characteristics of the farmers" [p.1, Abstract]
context_rationale: Climate change appears in the abstract framing only; introduction and analysis concern soil health, chemical use and diffusion of innovation, with no climate hazard measured or driving the question. Evidence: "However, there has been no research on farmers' knowledge and perceptions of implementing organic farming as a climate change adaptation strategy." [p.1, Abstract]
methodology_rationale: Structured survey of 80 farmers analysed with second-order CFA. Evidence: "This research used Second Order CFA with WarpPLS 5.0." [p.1, Abstract]
geography_rationale: Indonesia is lower/upper-middle income. Evidence: "Giripurno Village, Bumiaji District, Batu City, East Java, Indonesia was the site of the study." [p.3, Methods]
period_language_rationale: Published 2024 in English. Evidence: "Journal of Tekirdag Agricultural Faculty, 21(3): 722-731." [p.1]

lead_rationale: Both reviewers uncertain on context. Participatory scenario planning aimed at learning and adaptive capacity of marginalised small-scale fishers; climate is one of four drivers. Include at the margin and flag.
second_reviewer_decisive_issue: context (climate link weak: one of four drivers, not core to research question)
second_reviewer_summary: Participatory scenario-planning with marginalised South African small-scale fishers, aimed at learning and adaptive capacity; methodology and population fit. Climate is only one of four drivers and was not selected as a core scenario axis (income and rights were), so the climate-context criterion is borderline. A margin-inclusive map could keep it if the adaptive-capacity framing is accepted as aligned with adaptation objectives.
exclusion_reason: Borderline on context criterion: climate variability is one driver among several and not what drives the research question; otherwise criteria met.
population_rationale: Marginalized small-scale handline fishers (crew in the small-scale linefishery) of Melkhoutfontein, South Africa; fisheries count as small-scale agricultural production. Evidence: "These small-scale fishers act as crew in the small-scale commercial linefishery of the southern Cape and are vulnerable to global change" [p.3, Methods]
concept_rationale: Documents an adaptation process: participatory scenario planning as a route to learning, proactive decision-making and adaptive capacity among fishers. Evidence: "not only important for improving their adaptive capacity but also began to capacitate them to meaningfully engage in more formalized structured decisionmaking processes" [p.1, Introduction]
context_rationale: Environmental variability and climate change are named drivers (one of four KDFs, 'climate change (variability)') and fishers' reactive responses to change are the motivation, but participants chose access to rights and income as core drivers and the paper's focus is scenario planning for EAF implementation; climate is a background driver added by researchers. Evidence: "The four KDFs identified by participants were climate change (variability), changes to the biophysical system, sufficient disposable income, and access to marine resources." [p.6, Results] | "It was somewhat surprising that the participants settled on these two drivers, given that they had earlier emphasized the role of changes in weather patterns" [p.6, Results]
methodology_rationale: Empirical case study with workshops and scenario construction (qualitative participatory). Evidence: "three workshops were convened with the fishers from Melkhoutfontein (further referred to as participants)" [p.4, Methods]
geography_rationale: South Africa is upper-middle income. Evidence: "the historically marginalized fisher community of Melkhoutfontein" [p.3, Methods]

population_rationale: Farm women in watershed villages in India (marginal/small/medium farmer categories); smallholder agricultural producers in an LMIC. Evidence: "from each watershed a sample of 40 farm women was selected through purposive sampling and thus total of 120 farm women were chosen" [p.2, Sampling technique]
concept_rationale: Analyses adoption of soil and water conservation technologies and its determinants (adaptation process). Evidence: "assess the level of adoption of SWC technologies by farm women, impact of various factors on the adoption of technologies" [p.2, Introduction]
context_rationale: Semi-arid, drought-prone, erratic-rainfall rainfed agriculture; watershed programmes framed to address climatic variability. Climate link is somewhat background but water scarcity in semi-arid regions counts per codebook. Evidence: "Semi-arid regions (SARs) of India are characterized by limited rainfall and often prone to droughts." [p.1, Abstract]
methodology_rationale: Structured household interviews with regression and correlation analysis. Evidence: "The selected dependent and independent variables were analyzed using a regression model in SAS program" [p.2, Method of data analysis]
geography_rationale: India (LMIC). Evidence: "three project watersheds of ICAR-Indian Institute of Soil and W ater Conservation (IISW C), Dehradun" [p.2, Study areas]

lead_rationale: R1 uncertain, R2 exclude: baseline constraints/perception survey; no adaptation practice or outcome measured (codebook: perception alone excluded).
second_reviewer_decisive_issue: concept (perception/awareness and agronomic constraints only; no adaptation measured)
second_reviewer_summary: Baseline survey of Cambodian upland farmers' constraints, knowledge of conservation agriculture and future plans. Drought is a top perceived constraint and adaptation is mentioned as a downstream implication, but no adaptation practice or outcome is measured; this is perception plus general agronomy. Exclude, though a lenient reader could treat reported non-adjustment of sowing dates as marginal adaptation evidence.
exclusion_reason: Borderline on concept: baseline constraints and perception survey; no adaptation action measured beyond current practices and interest in conservation agriculture.
population_rationale: 391 farm families in upland cropping districts of Cambodia; generic farmers in an LMIC, mean farm 4.4 ha (range up to 40 ha), not commercial-scale. Evidence: "A face to face survey of 391 farm families was conducted in the Districts of Samlout in Battambang Province and Sala Krau in Pailin Province" [p.2, 2.1]
concept_rationale: A baseline survey of production constraints, knowledge of conservation agriculture, current residue practices and interest in post-monsoon cropping. It documents perceptions of drought and farmer knowledge/willingness to learn (adaptation-relevant processes) but measures no adaptation action taken in response to climate; the authors note farmers have not changed practices. Borderline between perception-only and adaptation process. Evidence: "The reason farmers have not changed their farming practices in response to changing climatic conditions is currently unknown." [p.6, 3.3] | "The survey highlighted opportunities for farmer education and adoption of farming system modifications to improve productivity and sustainability of the farming system in Northwest Cambodia, and assist with climate change adaptation." [p.1, Abstract]
context_rationale: Drought and heavy rain are the top-ranked constraints, with detailed questions on dry-spell duration, season onset and drought yield losses. Evidence: "Climate extremes formed the basis for the two highest answers with 69% of respondents reporting drought as their greatest constraint to production" [p.6, 3.3]
methodology_rationale: Structured face-to-face survey with descriptive statistics. Evidence: "Data were summarised into tables or figures of means, proportions, ranges and frequencies, via Excel (2013)." [p.2, 2.4]
geography_rationale: Cambodia (LMIC). Evidence: "Northwest Cambodia" [p.1 title]

population_rationale: Smallholder rice-farming households in irrigated schemes in Burkina Faso; household heads surveyed. Evidence: "random sampling techniques were used to select smallholder rice farming households in each scheme" [p.4, 2.2]
concept_rationale: Inventories 17 adaptation strategies to water scarcity and analyses determinants of their adoption and association with yield. Evidence: "farmers implemented seventeen different adaptation strategies that could be categorized into seven groups" [p.1, Abstract]
context_rationale: Water scarcity and drought in dry Sudanian and Sudano-Sahelian zones, supported by SPEI drought trend analysis. Evidence: "annual SPEI_12 exhibits decreasing trends" [p.9, 3.2]
methodology_rationale: Structured household survey (n=572) with logistic and Poisson regression plus expert interviews and climate records. Evidence: "We carried out the household survey using a structured questionnaire." [p.5, 2.2]
geography_rationale: Burkina Faso (low-income LMIC). Evidence: "The survey was carried out in Burkina Faso" [p.3, 2.1]
period_language_rationale: Published 2023, English. Evidence: "Accepted: 7 February 2023 / Published online: 31 March 2023" [p.1]

population_rationale: Landholding farm households in Mewat district, India; about 90% are marginal/small (up to 2 ha). Generic farmers in an LMIC, not commercial-scale. Evidence: "Nearly 90% of the surveyed farm households possess marginal to small landholding (up to 2 ha of land)." [p.5, Findings b]
concept_rationale: Documents adaptation strategies actually used (water, crop and land management, livelihood diversification, canal irrigation) and their determinants, not perception alone. Evidence: "Those responses can be broadly categorized as 1) water management, 2) crop and land management, 3) livelihood diversiﬁcation and outmigration" [p.9, Findings d]
context_rationale: Climate-driven groundwater salinity and declining rainfall/rising PET in a semi-arid district drive the research question. Evidence: "It falls under the subtropical, semiarid climatic zone with extremely hot temperatures in summer." [p.2, Study area]
methodology_rationale: Primary survey of 250 farmers, four case studies, and Mann-Kendall analysis of climate data. Evidence: "Thus, a total of 250 landholding farmers were surveyed." [p.4, Method]
geography_rationale: India is lower-middle income. Evidence: "This paper presents an empirical study in the Mewat (recently renamed as Nuh) district of Haryana." [p.2, Introduction]

population_rationale: Farming households (crop and livestock) in Ghoryan district, Afghanistan, including marginal and small holders; not commercial-scale. Evidence: "A total of 147 households were included in the survey, representing the three irrigation categories (low, medium, and high)." [p.5, Sample size]
concept_rationale: Documents drought adaptation and preparedness measures adopted (storing harvest, crop calendar, low-water crops, livestock sales, migration) and their determinants, not perceptions alone. Evidence: "The main agricultural adaptation strategies were reducing water waste during drought, using low-water-consuming crops, reducing the cultivated area, and changing the crop calendar." [p.11, 2.6]
context_rationale: Drought in an arid western Afghanistan setting drives the research question. Evidence: "Drought is a significant natural hazard in Herat Province, Afghanistan." [p.1, Abstract]
methodology_rationale: Structured questionnaire survey with non-parametric tests plus SPI from precipitation records. Evidence: "A questionnaire was completed by 147 farming households." [p.1, Abstract]
geography_rationale: Afghanistan is a low-income country. Evidence: "district Ghoryan (Figure 1) has been taken as the study area for micro level analysis" [p.3]
period_language_rationale: Published 2018, English. Evidence: "J. Mt. Sci. (2018) 15(8): 1741-1756" [p.1 header]

lead_rationale: Both reviewers: fire-risk/land-use economics with mitigation framing; no climate-hazard adaptation (concept and context fail).
second_reviewer_decisive_issue: concept and context (fire/land-use economics with mitigation framing; no climate-risk adaptation)
second_reviewer_summary: Econometric study of how fire risk locks Amazonian smallholders into low-yield, fire-using land uses. It is about fire management and poverty traps with greenhouse-gas mitigation framing, not climate-hazard adaptation. Population, methods, geography and date are fine, but concept and context fail.
exclusion_reason: Context criterion: no climate hazard drives the research question (anthropogenic fire risk; climate only background); concept is borderline and mitigation-oriented.
population_rationale: Analysis restricted to small farmers (up to 4 fiscal lots, 55-75 ha) in Brazil, an upper-middle-income country. Evidence: "The analysis is conducted only among small farmers, owning up to 4 fiscal lots as defined by the Brazilian law (8.629/93)" [p.4, 4.1]
concept_rationale: Studies fire use versus adoption of capital-intensive fire-free land uses and the revenue effects of neighbours' fire risk (a land-use adoption process), but it is framed as fire-poverty trap and climate change mitigation (emissions, forest degradation), not adaptation to climate stress. Evidence: "we show that smallholders in consolidated farm-forest frontier regions are locked into a vicious cycle that inhibits their adoption of fire-free practices" [p.1, Abstract]
context_rationale: Fire risk is anthropogenic and the research question is not driven by a climate hazard; drought is only mentioned in passing, and the keywords frame the topic as climate change mitigation. Codebook: climate as background only is excluded. Evidence: "there are no natural ignition sources in the rainforest (Cochrane, 2003). All fires are anthropogenic and mainly related to agricultural activities" [p.1, Introduction] | "if fire risk increased by one standard deviation (SD), for instance because of a drought" [p.5, 5.2]
methodology_rationale: Household survey data combined with MODIS fire data in IV-GMM regressions. Evidence: "Using a combination of household interviews and remotely sensed data on fire occurrence in Eastern Amazon municipalities of Paragominas and Santarém" [p.1, Abstract]
geography_rationale: Brazil is upper-middle income. Evidence: "Survey and watershed level data were collected in 2010-2011 in the municipalities of Paragominas and Santarém, in the state of Pará, Brazil" [p.4, 4.1]
period_language_rationale: Published 2020, English. Evidence: "Global Environmental Change 63 (2020) 102096" [p.1 header]

population_rationale: Mober farmers, fishers and former herders of Bosso (Niger) practising small-scale flood-retreat, irrigated and rainfed farming and fishing. Evidence: "They were initially herders and farmers who developed flood-retreat farming and sophisticated irrigation systems." [p.1, Abstract]
concept_rationale: Documents adaptation actions (shift to flood-retreat polder farming, irrigated sweet pepper, pluriactivity) and their livelihood/income outcomes. Evidence: "It is a case study of dynamic adaptation of a Sahelian society to a major environmental change." [p.2, Introduction]
context_rationale: Drought and rainfall decline driving Lake Chad shrinkage and agricultural/fishing change is the central research question. Evidence: "Since 1973, Lake Chad has shrunk, mainly because of the decrease in rainfall in its southern hydrological basin" [p.1, Abstract]
methodology_rationale: Empirical interdisciplinary case study with farmer interviews, soil and hydrological surveys. Evidence: "This research was carried out as an interdisciplinary work involving agronomy, social anthropology and hydrology." [p.3, Materials and methods]
geography_rationale: Niger (low-income) with some reference to Nigeria. Evidence: "eastern Niger near the Yobe River and in Lake Chad" [p.1, Abstract]
period_language_rationale: Published 2011 online / 2012 in issue, English. Evidence: "Reg Environ Change (2012) 12:507–521" [p.1 header]

lead_rationale: Both reviewers uncertain. Technical potential of fog harvesting with no producers studied and no adaptation process or outcome measured. Recommend exclude.
second_reviewer_decisive_issue: population/concept (technology-potential study with no producers or adaptation outcomes measured)
second_reviewer_summary: Hydro-technical pilot and design study of fog harvesting for irrigation in southern Bolivia, motivated by water scarcity and farmer resilience to dry spells. Context and methodology qualify under the protocol, but no producers are studied and no adaptation process or outcome is measured, only technical potential. Genuine borderline; under inclusive-margin rules it could be retained.
exclusion_reason: Borderline on concept: fog-harvesting potential and theoretical irrigation design, with no measured adaptation process or outcome among farmers.
population_rationale: Small-scale rainfed farming communities of Valles Cruceños, Bolivia (LMIC); the irrigation system is designed for smallholder family plots. Evidence: "The main economic activity in the region is agriculture, which is mostly small-scale and rainfed, and water scarcity represents a key constraint" [p.2, Study area]
concept_rationale: Studies a candidate adaptation technology (fog-water harvesting for dry-season irrigation) but only measures fog yields and a theoretical irrigation design; no farmer adoption, behaviour or outcomes (yield, income) are measured. Genuine borderline: technology feasibility rather than adaptation process/outcome. Evidence: "analyzing the feasibility of a suitable, scalable, fog-based irrigation system that can enhance the resilience and the food security of rural settlements" [p.2, Introduction]
context_rationale: Water scarcity, dry spells and a long dry season in semi-arid valleys drive the question (codebook: water scarcity in semi-arid areas counts). Evidence: "orographic fog is a phenomenon occurring all year round, representing a sustainable water source for improving farmers' resilience to dry spells" [p.1, Abstract]
methodology_rationale: One-year field measurements at 10 sites plus a CROPWAT-based water-balance design with sensitivity analysis; empirical data with a model. Evidence: "The collection of hydrometeorological observations, including fog collection, was made from January to December 2018." [p.3, Materials and methods]
geography_rationale: Bolivia is lower-middle-income. Evidence: "Valles Cruceños region (a macroregion including the three provinces of Florida, Vallegrande, and Manuel María Caballero)" [p.2]
period_language_rationale: Published 2023 (online 2022), English. Evidence: "Journal of Arid Environments 208 (2023) 104884" [p.1 header]

lead_rationale: Both reviewers: adaptation to market and conservation-policy change, not to a climate hazard (context fails).
second_reviewer_decisive_issue: context (adaptation to economic/institutional change; no climate hazard drives the question)
second_reviewer_summary: Well-executed study of coping-to-adaptation trajectories in a Mexican smallholder community, but the stressors are market and conservation-policy changes rather than climate hazards. Climate is background at most, so the context criterion is clearly not met despite good fit on the other criteria.
exclusion_reason: Context criterion fails: adaptation to economic (NAFTA, price) and institutional (Biosphere Reserve) change; no explicit climate hazard or stress.
population_rationale: Smallholder ejido community (maize, coffee, palm, livestock) in Chiapas, Mexico (upper-middle-income). Evidence: "The smallholder community Tierra y Libertad (TyL) is near the ridge of the Sierra Madre de Chiapas mountain range" [p.3, Study area]
concept_rationale: Documents coping and adaptation responses (land-use diversification, decision-making, social organisation) and adaptive capacity, so processes and outcomes are assessed; but the drivers are economic and institutional, not climatic. Evidence: "We found that coping (between 1990 and 2000) was gradually replaced by adaptations (1995-2010)" [p.1, Abstract]
context_rationale: The drivers are trade liberalisation (NAFTA), price drops and Biosphere Reserve land-use restrictions; climate is mentioned only in passing as a possible future change, so there is no explicit climate hazard driving the research question. Evidence: "Adaptive capacity is most commonly analyzed and discussed in the context of climate change, however the term can be used more broadly to include responses to economic and institutional drivers" [p.3, Adaptive capacity assessment] | "These pressures included a strong decline in the price of their main produce as a result of (i) trade liberalization, and (ii) land-use limitations" [p.2, Introduction]
methodology_rationale: Key-informant interviews, household survey (n=75) and Lorenz-curve analysis in a case study. Evidence: "We used a 50% proportional stratified systematic sampling method to identify the households to be interviewed." [p.4, Household survey]
geography_rationale: Mexico is upper-middle-income. Evidence: "a community in the buffer-zone of a Biosphere Reserve in Chiapas, Mexico" [p.1, Abstract]
period_language_rationale: Published 2014, English. Evidence: "Land Use Policy 41 (2014) 31-44" [p.1 header]

population_rationale: Smallholder irrigators and agropastoralists along sand rivers in Kenya and Zimbabwe (LMICs). Evidence: "alternative ways of investing in smallholder irrigation in Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA) that are adaptive and avoid capital lock-in" [p.1, Abstract]
concept_rationale: Documents farmers' incremental irrigation investments and livelihood diversification as responses to risks (drought, floods) and opportunities; adaptation decisions/processes are the object of analysis. Evidence: "in face of risks, farmers diversify their livelihoods, make small investments incrementally especially in response to opportunities and risks created by external triggers" [p.1, Abstract]
context_rationale: Semi-arid/arid agricultural setting; drought, floods and water scarcity are explicit triggers, and irrigation framed as climate adaptation in drylands. Evidence: "These sand rivers play an important role in climate adaptation in the drylands by virtue of providing shallow nature-based water storage." [p.2, Introduction] | "drought is a frequent risk. This may trigger rainfed farmers to shift to irrigation (M14)." [p.8, Results 5.2]
methodology_rationale: Empirical retrospective multi-case study using baseline surveys, in-depth interviews and workshops. Evidence: "This involved a baseline survey of all irrigation activity along a 2.5 km stretch of the river, and a set of deeper interviews with 23 selected farmers." [p.6, Data collection 4.2]
geography_rationale: Kenya (lower-middle income) and Zimbabwe (lower-middle income). Evidence: "three case studies representing different stages of irrigation development along shallow sand river aquifers in Kenya and Zimbabwe" [p.1, Abstract]

population_rationale: Transhumant goat/cattle/sheep herders ('fragile peasants', smallholders with mixed herds) in Argentina (upper-middle income). Evidence: "Fragile peasants are smallholders with mixed herds, dominated by goats, with the lowest resource levels and longest distance to urban areas." [p.2, Study area]
concept_rationale: Documents pastoralists' adaptive strategies (reducing consumption, consuming adult animals, off-farm income, diversification into orchards/fowl, adopting radio/truck/phone, hiring labour) in response to drought; not perception alone. Borderline because the method is perception/discourse mapping. Evidence: "The main strategies against the unfavourable productive situation were associated with a reduction in the demands and consumption of the family (# 9), and the consumption of adult animals" [p.5, Results] | "off-farm income is a relevant strategy to partially dissociate family incomes from productivity losses" [p.7, Discussion]
context_rationale: Arid/semi-arid rangeland livestock system where drought drives the perceived problems. Evidence: "the main cause was attributed to the fact that the last three or four years were dry or bad in terms of lack of rainfall and snowfall" [p.5, Results]
methodology_rationale: Empirical semi-structured interviews (n=18) analysed by cognitive mapping and network analysis. Evidence: "a total of 18 interviews were carried out between June and November 2011" [p.3, 2.2]
geography_rationale: Argentina, upper-middle-income country. Evidence: "The study area was located in North-West Patagonia (Argentina)" [p.2, 2.1]

population_rationale: Rural farming and pastoral households (crops, goats, sheep, cattle, poultry) in Bauchi and Gombe, Nigeria; very low incomes indicate smallholders. Evidence: "Overall, income levels are exceedingly low, with most respondents earning far less than $1 per day." [p.5, Results]
concept_rationale: Documents and statistically compares coping/adaptation strategies (diversification, premature harvest, livestock relocation, sharecropping, outmigration) to climate stress. Evidence: "significant gender differences in coping mechanisms: women engaged more in premature harvesting and livelihood diversification, while men relied on sharecropping and outmigration" [p.1, Abstract]
context_rationale: Sahelian agriculture/pastoralism with climate hazards (drought, floods, heat, rainfall shifts) driving the study, alongside COVID-19. Evidence: "Respondents also reported a rise in extreme weather events, including floods, intense heat, heavy rainfall, and strong winds." [p.7, 3.1]
methodology_rationale: Household survey (n=3,041) with chi-square analysis. Evidence: "A total of 3,041 individuals participated in the questionnaire survey across the two target states (Gombe and Bauchi)" [p.3, Methods]
geography_rationale: Nigeria, lower-middle income. Evidence: "gender-specific adaptation strategies in Bauchi and Gombe States" [p.1, Abstract]
period_language_rationale: Published May 2025, English. Evidence: "Available online 16 May 2025" [p.1]

population_rationale: Crop farming households in Nigeria (GHS-Panel); generic farmers label in an LMIC with no commercial-scale focus. Evidence: "The GHS-Panel data set represents a crosssection of approximately 5,000 households from the country's six geopolitical zones." [p.3, Methodology]
concept_rationale: Analyses determinants and income outcomes of adopting packages of climate-smart practices (adoption process and outcome), by gender. Evidence: "This study estimated the economic impact of the adoption of multiple climate-smart agriculture (CSA) practices in Nigeria through a gender lens" [p.1, Abstract]
context_rationale: Climate threat to agriculture frames the CSA adoption question; climate shock and climate zone variables are included. Climate framing is moderately strong (CSA labelling). Evidence: "Climate change poses a severe threat to agricultural productivity in Nigeria, manifesting through irregular rainfall patterns, increased temperatures, and more frequent extreme weather events" [p.2, Introduction]
methodology_rationale: Empirical econometric analysis of national household panel data (multivariate probit, endogenous switching regression, fixed effects). Evidence: "A two-stage endogenous switching regression model was used to analyse CSA adoption and farm income data." [p.1, Abstract]
geography_rationale: Nigeria is lower-middle income. Evidence: "This study was conducted in Nigeria" [p.3, Methodology]

population_rationale: Women and men smallholder farmers in Mindanao, Philippines (an LMIC); commercial plantations are mentioned only as context. Evidence: "this paper presents an analysis of focus groups (n = 14) and interviews (n = 77) to showcase gendered vulnerabilities of smallholder farmers to climate change" [p.1, Abstract]
concept_rationale: Primarily a gendered vulnerability and loss-and-damage study, but it documents farmers' coping/adaptation responses (off-farm work, livestock as insurance, home gardens, migration, remittances) in a dedicated results section and Table 4, so adaptation actions are documented. Borderline because the framing is vulnerability. Evidence: "The key climate-related risks experienced by women, men, households and coping mechanisms are listed in Table 4." [p.8, 5.4] | "Migration and mobility from rural farms is a key coping strategy for young women to stabilise family income" [p.11, 5.6]
context_rationale: Droughts, floods and typhoons affecting farm production drive the research question. Evidence: "the dominant hazard across the study sites were the repetitive cycle of droughts and floods" [p.7, 5.2]
methodology_rationale: Empirical qualitative case study using semi-structured interviews and FGDs analysed in NVivo. Evidence: "Data gathered from the interviews and FGDs were analysed using a grounded theory analysis approach" [p.6, 4.2]
geography_rationale: Philippines is lower-middle income. Evidence: "Five municipality sites were selected from three provinces: Agusan del Norte, North Cotabato and Sultan Kudarat." [p.3, Section 3]
period_language_rationale: Published online January 2017; English. Evidence: "Available online 10 January 2017" [p.1]

lead_rationale: Both reviewers: compliance with traditional rangeland rules; no adaptation measured; climate background only.
second_reviewer_summary: Study documents compliance with traditional Maasai pasture-reserve management rules for rangeland conservation. No adaptation action or outcome is measured and climate is background only, so concept and context fail.
exclusion_reason: Fails concept (no climate adaptation process/outcome assessed; traditional rangeland compliance) and context (climate only as background).
population_rationale: Maasai pastoral households keeping livestock in northern Tanzania (indigenous, small-scale pastoralism). Evidence: "Pastoralism is the major economic activity through which the indigenous Maasai community generates its family wealth for sustained livelihood" [p.4, Study area]
concept_rationale: The study characterises traditional rangeland-conservation rules and measures compliance with them; it does not assess adaptation to climate risk (processes or outcomes) in the codebook sense. Compliance with conservation/grazing rules is governance of rangeland sustainability, with no adaptation action or outcome framed against climate. Evidence: "this study aimed to characterize the traditional and indigenous principles and guidelines used to guide compliance in the process of utilizing and locally managing the Maasai Alalili systems." [p.3, Introduction]
context_rationale: Climate change is listed among background pressures (with land-use change, biodiversity loss, socio-cultural transition); the research question is about degradation and compliance, not a climate hazard. Dry-season reserve pastures are a drought-buffering practice, but the authors do not frame or analyse them against a climate stress. Evidence: "However, the Alalili systems and their associated biodiversity are undergoing decline and degradation partly because of socio-cultural transformation, changes in climate, unsustainable land use practices, and political regimes" [p.3, Introduction]
methodology_rationale: Mixed-methods empirical design: household survey, KIIs, FGDs, observation, literature review, chi-square and t-tests. Evidence: "The study used a mixed-method approach" [p.2, Abstract]
geography_rationale: Tanzania is lower-middle income. Evidence: "The sample districts were Longido, Ngorongoro, and Monduli for the Arusha region and Simanjiro and Kiteto for the Manyara region." [p.4, Research design]
period_language_rationale: Published online 17 May 2025; English. Evidence: "Published online: 17 May 2025." [p.1]

population_rationale: Rice cultivators (generic 'farmers') in Shushtar County, Iran; no commercial-scale focus (mean 12 ha irrigated land is moderate). Generic farmer label in LMIC accepted under codebook. Evidence: "The statistical population for this research was composed of all rice cultivators in Shushtar County." [p.4, 2.3]
concept_rationale: Determinants of adoption of climate-smart agriculture practices (adaptation uptake) are measured with PMT/SEM; adoption is the outcome variable. Evidence: "this study investigates the factors influencing the adoption of CSA practices among rice farmers in Shushtar County" [p.1, Abstract]
context_rationale: Arid region with temperature rise and water decline framed as the driver for CSA adoption. Evidence: "Against the backdrop of rising temperatures and declining water availability, adopting CSA practices in Shushtar is crucial" [p.4, 2.2 Study area]
methodology_rationale: Structured questionnaire survey (n=385) with PLS-SEM analysis. Evidence: "Data were collected via a structured questionnaire and analyzed using structural equation modeling." [p.1, Abstract]
geography_rationale: Iran is an LMIC (explicitly listed in codebook). Evidence: "Shushtar County, situated in Khuzestan Province in southwestern Iran" [p.4, 2.2]
period_language_rationale: English; online 19 Nov 2025, issue year 2026 (outside the 2005-2025 protocol window by issue year only). Evidence: "Available online 19 November 2025" [p.1]

lead_rationale: R2 include (low). Agroforestry adoption explicitly framed as climate adaptation and resilience; climate link is general, not hazard-specific. Include at the margin.
second_reviewer_summary: Smallholder agroforestry adoption determinants in Ethiopia, explicitly framed as climate adaptation and resilience, using a survey and BBN. Climate link is general rather than hazard-specific, so it is borderline on context but eligible under an inclusive map.
exclusion_reason: Context criterion borderline: climate change is only framing/background; no climate hazard or stress is measured or drives the question (leaning exclude).
population_rationale: Smallholder farm households practising agroforestry woodlots in three districts of Amhara, Ethiopia. Evidence: "The population mainly consists of smallholder farmers and agriculture as the mainstay of the economy." [p.4, 3.1]
concept_rationale: Adoption of agroforestry innovations is the analysed process, with an extension-policy scenario; authors frame agroforestry as climate adaptation, though the adoption drivers analysed are mostly socioeconomic and market variables. Evidence: "illustrating how to propel the adoption of AFI as part of diverse climate change adaptation policy strategies" [p.2, Introduction]
context_rationale: Climate appears as framing ('forest sector based climate solutions', adaptation and carbon sequestration) but no climate hazard (drought, rainfall variability) is measured or drives the research question; innovations are market-oriented woodlots (charcoal, poles, furniture). Codebook: climate as background only -> exclude; leaning exclude. Evidence: "Improving adoption rate is vital for realizing agroforestry innovations’ financial and environmental benefits including fostering climate change adaptation and resilience efforts." [p.1, Abstract] | "Poor price • Volatile market • Weather variability" [p.5, Table 1 (bamboo risks)]
methodology_rationale: Household survey (n=327) with Bayesian Belief Network and train/test validation. Evidence: "Finally, 327 farmers who were or have been practicing AFI were selected by applying a simple random sampling procedure" [p.4, 3.2]
geography_rationale: Ethiopia (low-income). Evidence: "This study was conducted in Ethiopia." [p.4, 3.1]

lead_rationale: R1 uncertain, R2 exclude: information and communication in groundwater governance; no adaptation practice or outcome measured.
second_reviewer_summary: Paper examines how information and communication affect farmers' commitment to participatory groundwater governance in Morocco. It measures no adaptation practice or outcome, and climate is peripheral. Borderline only if water governance in semi-arid areas is read as adaptation.
exclusion_reason: Concept borderline: information/communication and governance engagement with no adaptation action or outcome measured; climate is background (leaning exclude).
population_rationale: Small farmers (0-10 ha) with at least one well in the Saiss plain, irrigated agriculture. Evidence: "This third stage consists on choosing small farmers with lands’ area varying from 0 to 10 ha and having as a minimum one well." [p.5, 2.2.1]
concept_rationale: Measures information access, communication channels and commitment to participatory groundwater governance (governance/access-to-information processes), but no adaptation action is measured; farmers do not perceive scarcity as a risk and climate change is background to groundwater governance. Borderline: governance/information processes are listed in the brief, but alignment with adaptation objectives is weak. Evidence: "the aim of this paper is to show with field experiment how information sharing, dialogue, interactive communication and trust in relationships could contribute to strengthening stakeholders’ ownership of participatory groundwater governance (PGWG)" [p.4, Introduction]
context_rationale: Semi-arid plain with documented rainfall decline and groundwater overdraft; water scarcity in a semi-arid area counts under the codebook. Evidence: "Due to the combined effects of the decrease of rainfalls since the 1980′s, which has reduced the natural recharge of groundwater, and increased groundwater pumping for irrigation, Saiss aquifers suffer from overexploitation" [p.4, 2.1]
methodology_rationale: Structured survey of 20 farmers plus interviews/case study; empirical though small. Evidence: "From 30 farmers randomly selected and having all criteria, only 20 were finally chosen (4 farmers from each commune)." [p.6, 2.2.1]
geography_rationale: Morocco is a lower-middle-income country. Evidence: "Case of SAISS Aquifers, Morocco" [p.1, title]

population_rationale: Crop farmers in four agricultural communities in the Peruvian Andes (LMIC); small-scale agricultural communities; generic farmers label, not commercial. Evidence: "In small-scale agricultural communities with diverse identities (Erwin et al. 2021), ILK systems are considered essential" [p.1, Introduction] | "semi-structured interviews with a total of 108 farmers in the four Colca Valley districts" [p.2, Methods]
concept_rationale: Documents farmer and institutional responses to climate change (planting timing, reservoir funding requests, experimentation with sprinklers, institutional limits to adaptation), i.e. adaptation processes (decision-making, institutions, access to resources), not perception alone. Evidence: "as well as by experimenting with water-saving irrigation methods" [p.6, Discussion] | "farmers told us they had insufficient funds to build additional reservoirs for water storage" [p.5, Results]
context_rationale: Crop agriculture with explicit climate stress (shifting rainy season, warming, frost) driving the research question, corroborated with climate trend analysis. Evidence: "shifts in the rainy season together with warmer weather affected farmers" [p.1, Abstract]
methodology_rationale: Qualitative semi-structured interviews (n=108) with thematic coding plus Mann-Kendall trend analysis of gridded climate data. Evidence: "using thematic coding and process coding strategies" [p.2, Methods] | "We used the Mann-Kendall test (Hirsch et al. 1982) with significance level of 0.05" [p.3, Methods]
geography_rationale: Peru (upper-middle-income). Evidence: "four agricultural districts in the Colca Canyon area of Caylloma province of Peru" [p.2, Methods]

lead_rationale: Both reviewers: replicated agronomic field trial with no farmer adoption or outcome analysis.
second_reviewer_summary: Replicated agronomic field trial of tillage, residue and irrigation on rice-wheat yield and water productivity in Haryana. There is no farmer adoption or outcome analysis, so it is a crop trial excluded by the codebook, despite the CSA platform setting.
exclusion_reason: Methodology: on-farm/platform agronomic field trial without farmer adoption analysis; context: climate is background (labour and water scarcity); population not analysed.
population_rationale: A replicated field experiment at a research/learning platform; no farmers or households are sampled or analysed, so there is no identifiable smallholder population beyond the farmer-practice treatment. Evidence: "The experiment was conducted in a split-plot design with three replications." [pdf p.4 (journal p.175), Materials and Methods]
concept_rationale: Evaluates conservation-agriculture practices (zero tillage, direct seeding, tensiometer irrigation, residues) for water productivity and yield (an outcome measure), but no adoption, decision-making or farmer process is measured and the practices are agronomic technology tests. Evidence: "This study evaluated a set of CA-based improved" [pdf p.5 (journal p.176), Conclusion]
context_rationale: The driving problem is labour and water scarcity in rice-wheat systems; climate is only background (semi-arid site description, 'climate smart agriculture' platform name) and no climate hazard such as drought or heat is analysed. Evidence: "Labour and water scarcity in Indo-Gangetic Plain (IGP) of India are driving researchers and farmers to find alternative management strategies" [pdf p.3 (journal p.174), Abstract]
methodology_rationale: A crop agronomic/variety-type trial of management treatments with no farmer adoption analysis: codebook/protocol exclusion for crop trials without farmer adoption analysis. Evidence: "The experiment was conducted in a split-plot design with three replications." [pdf p.4 (journal p.175), Materials and Methods]
geography_rationale: Haryana, India (lower-middle-income). Evidence: "Taraori, Karnal, Haryana, were used to compare the, effects of tillage practices" [pdf p.3 (journal p.174), Abstract]
period_language_rationale: Published 2016 in English. Evidence: "Annals of Biology 32 (2) : 174-177, 2016" [pdf p.3 header]

population_rationale: Pastoralist/agropastoralist households in Marsabit, northern Kenya; smallholder and pastoralist households. Evidence: "The sample used in this study is a balanced panel of 579 randomly selected pastoralist households" [p.7, Data]
concept_rationale: Assesses uptake of index-based livestock insurance (a climate risk management/adaptation measure) and its outcomes on income and downside income risk. Evidence: "We found that uptake of IBLI increased household income and reduced pastoralists' exposure to downside risk." [p.1, Abstract]
context_rationale: Drylands where drought drives the research question. Evidence: "IBLI has been promoted in this context as an asset protection policy that was developed to cushion pastoralists against drought." [p.5, Context]
methodology_rationale: Four-wave household panel with 2SLS IV using randomised subsidy coupons. Evidence: "We rely on exogenous variation in the subsidy coupons provided to households purchasing index insurance as a valid instrument." [p.12, Econometric strategy]
geography_rationale: Kenya (lower-middle-income). Evidence: "four waves of household surveys conducted in Marsabit district (now Marsabit county), northern Kenya" [p.7, Data]
period_language_rationale: Published 2025 (Appl Econ Perspect Policy 2025;47), English. Evidence: "Appl Econ Perspect Policy. 2025;47:863-891." [p.1 footer]

lead_rationale: R2 include (low). Farm-level economic appraisal of tank rehabilitation framed as response to water scarcity and climate in semi-arid India; method specified. Include at the margin.
second_reviewer_summary: Farm-level economic appraisal (IRR) of tank rehabilitation options in semi-arid Tamil Nadu, framed as climate adaptation and water-scarcity response. Adaptation wording is light, but actions align with adaptation objectives and methods are specified.
population_rationale: Farm households under irrigation tank commands in Tamil Nadu, India, mostly paddy growers; dependents include marginal and small farmers. Evidence: "the total sample size for the study was 150 farm holds" [p.10, Methods] | "more than 90 percent of the tank beneficiaries has cultivating paddy" [p.14, Methods]
concept_rationale: Tank rehabilitation is framed as an adaptation strategy against climate change in semi-arid regions; study measures outcomes (water availability, cropping area, yield, net benefit, IRR). Climate link is thin. Evidence: "has been considered as the potential instrument of adaption strategy against climate change in the semi-arid regions" [p.4, Introduction]
context_rationale: Semi-arid water scarcity and erratic rainfall are stated as the setting (codebook: semi-arid water scarcity counts), but climate change is background and no climate variable or hazard is analysed; the question is investment prioritisation. Evidence: "Accounting semi-arid conditions, climate change, and looming water scarcity, the necessity for rehabilitating the tanks seeks major attention." [p.6, Introduction]
methodology_rationale: Farm survey (150 farm holds) plus engineering/administrative records; IRR and impact tables. Evidence: "Both primary, as well as secondary data was used for this study." [p.10, Methods]
geography_rationale: India (lower-middle-income). Evidence: "Tamil Nadu, India, has purposively selected for this study" [p.8, Methods]
period_language_rationale: Copyright 2021, English. Evidence: "Copyright 2021 by Balasubramanian Mohan, Korabandi Suhasini" [p.2]

population_rationale: Household heads of rainfed smallholder farming communities in Ethiopia. Evidence: "the factors influencing smallholder farmers to adopt various strategies to overcome water scarcity in the context of climate change" [p.1-2, Abstract]
concept_rationale: Analyses determinants of adoption of five water-scarcity adaptation strategies (rainwater harvesting, water rules, watershed protection, capacity building, infrastructure) using a multivariate probit. Evidence: "Five distinct but interrelated adaptation strategies for water scarcity were analyzed using a multidimensional econometric model." [p.2, Introduction]
context_rationale: Water scarcity under climate change (drought, erratic rainfall) in rainfed agriculture drives the research question. Evidence: "Over the recent decade, drought, erratic rainfall, and flood frequency have been increasing and degrading" [p.2, Introduction]
methodology_rationale: Household survey (N=1946) with multivariate probit regression. Evidence: "Data were collected through the socioeconomic survey (N = 1946) was analyzed using the Stata software Version 15." [p.4, Data analysis]
geography_rationale: Ethiopia (low income). Evidence: "five districts from the western parts of Oromia National Regional State" [p.2, Study area]
period_language_rationale: English; published online March 2026 (volume 30, 2026), outside the 2005-2025 protocol window but after 2005. Evidence: "Received 20 November 2025; Received in revised form 2 March 2026; Accepted 4 March 2026 Available online 4 March 2026" [p.1]

lead_rationale: Both reviewers: adoption of improved varieties/fertilizer with climate only as motivation (general agronomy).
second_reviewer_summary: A technology-adoption study of improved finger millet and maize practices among Kenyan smallholders. Climate change adaptation is mentioned only as motivation; no climate hazard or climate-risk response is measured, so it is general agronomy under the codebook. Population, methods, geography and period are fine.
exclusion_reason: Concept and context criteria fail: study is on adoption of improved agronomic inputs (modern varieties, fertilizer) with climate change only as background; no climate hazard drives the research question.
population_rationale: Small-scale finger millet farmers in western Kenya. Evidence: "With an average farm size of 1.61 ha, most households in our sample were small-scale farmers." [p.7, Descriptive results]
concept_rationale: Studies adoption of modern varieties and chemical fertilizer to close the yield gap; climate adaptation is mentioned only as a potential of traditional cereals, no climate-related adaptation action is the object of measurement. Reads as general agronomy/technology adoption without climate-risk framing. Evidence: "The present study aims to assess the factors that influence adoption decisions among finger millet farmers in western Kenya." [p.1, Abstract]
context_rationale: Climate change appears as background (finger millet resilient to erratic rainfall; future climate adaptation role) and does not drive the research question, which concerns productivity and technology diffusion. Evidence: "Traditional food grains have however an important potential to improve food security, reduce micronutrient deficiencies, and enhance smallholder adaptation to climate change." [p.1, Abstract] | "the important role that traditional African cereals could play in the context of climate change adaptation, food security and nutrition" [p.13, Conclusions]
