methodology_rationale: Household survey with multivariate probit and Cobb-Douglas production function. Evidence: "We conducted a household survey among 270 finger millet farmers in western Kenya in 2012." [p.3, Data collection]
geography_rationale: Kenya (lower-middle income). Evidence: "Our research was carried out in Western Province (Kakamega and Busia counties)" [p.3]

population_rationale: Farmers in rainfed/limited-irrigation rice-wheat systems in Nepal's Terai; on-farm experiments in farmers' fields (plots 300-600 m2), not commercial-scale. Evidence: "Participatory on-farm experiments" [p.2, Experimental sites]
concept_rationale: Evaluates farmer-field performance of DSR and ZTW as climatic risk minimisation practices (yield, cost, profit, yield stability) and includes DSR adopters' perceptions and yield stability. Evidence: "DSR and ZTW as climatic risk minimization technologies" [p.9, Section 4.3]
context_rationale: Rainfall variability, early-season drought and terminal heat stress frame the study and the stability analysis. Evidence: "increased rainfall variability and temperature due to climate change have threatened the stability and performance of the current rice-wheat system" [p.2, Introduction]
methodology_rationale: On-farm experiments with farmer survey on perceptions of DSR and yield measurements on adopters' fields; not a bare variety trial. Evidence: "Farmers' perception on the risks associated with DSR establishment (in the initial 30 days) were elicited from 185 purposively selected DSR adopter farmers" [p.3, Experiment II]
geography_rationale: Nepal (lower-middle income). Evidence: "in the western Terai region of Nepal" [p.1, Abstract]

population_rationale: Smallholder farmers (crop and agropastoral) in Makueni and Kajiado, Kenya, a low/lower-middle income context; 146 farmers in FGDs. Evidence: "support for CSA has not achieved widespread uptake among smallholder farmers" [p.1, Introduction] | "We conducted 24 mixed focus group discussions (FGDs) with 7-12 male and female farmers per group in two regions of Kenya" [p.2, Study context and methodology]
concept_rationale: Examines barriers to adoption (uptake) of CSA practices and farmers' adaptation strategies per climate risk; adoption/uptake of CSA is an inclusion scenario under the codebook. Evidence: "This paper seeks to identify the leading social, economic, political, and cultural barriers to the adoption of climate-smart agriculture in Kenya." [p.1, Abstract]
context_rationale: Agriculture under drought, flood and temperature stress is the explicit driver of the research question. Evidence: "changing weather patterns have resulted in more frequent and severe droughts and floods" [p.2, Literature review]
methodology_rationale: Primary qualitative data (FGDs, key-informant interviews) analysed with thematic analysis and process tracing with Bayesian updating; a targeted literature review is only one of three evidence sources. Evidence: "The study is based on primary qualitative data collected from 146 farmers in Southern Kenya, 22 key informants, and a targeted literature review." [p.1, Abstract]
geography_rationale: Kenya is a lower-middle-income country. Evidence: "two regions of Kenya—Kajiado and Makueni" [p.2, Study context and methodology]
period_language_rationale: English; published 2026, which is after 2005 but outside the 2005-2025 protocol window (flagged). Evidence: "Published online: 11 February 2026" [p.1 header]

lead_rationale: Both reviewers uncertain. Adoption decisions for agroecological practices in semi-arid Tunisia with links to dryland stress and resilience; include at the margin and flag.
second_reviewer_decisive_issue: concept and context (agroecological transition with dryland/climate background rather than climate-adaptation focus)
second_reviewer_summary: A participatory case study of drivers and barriers of agroecological transition among farmers and stakeholders in semi-arid northwest Tunisia. It documents adoption decisions and perceptions and links to resilience and dryland stress, but climate risk is not the driver of the research question. Genuine borderline; I lean slightly toward inclusion under the inclusive-at-margin rule.
exclusion_reason: Borderline on context: climate/drought is background to an agroecological-transition (sustainability) study rather than the driving question; adoption and perception outcomes otherwise fit.
population_rationale: Farmers and farmer organisations (livestock, cereals, olive) in north-west Tunisia, holdings mostly 1-50 ha, described as smallholders; Tunisia is a lower-middle-income country. Evidence: "It supports small-scale farmers in diversity and ensures a long-term balance between food production and the sustainability of natural and environmental resources." [p.2, Introduction] | "The land holdings of the farmers range from 1 to 50 hectares in the survey and 0–100 hectares in the questionnaire" [p.6, 3.4]
concept_rationale: Assesses adoption of agroecological practices (crop rotation, direct seeding, conservation agriculture), farmers' perceived changes in practices and decisions, and drivers/barriers; adoption processes under dryland stress. Evidence: "Table 8 illustrates the number and percentage of farmers adopting and not adopting new agroecological practices by age and gender." [p.8, 4.4]
context_rationale: Drylands with water scarcity and erratic rainfall are cited and climate change/drought appear among threats, but the research question is agroecological transformation for sustainability, with climate as background rather than the driving hazard. Evidence: "Focusing on dryland areas is crucial due to their unique challenges and characteristics such as water scarcity, erratic rainfall, and fragile ecosystems." [p.2, Introduction] | "This research contributes to addressing the climate change crisis and to enhancing the resilience of food systems." [p.2, Introduction]
methodology_rationale: Primary data from interviews, workshops, a survey (n=69) and a perception questionnaire with statistical analysis. Evidence: "The research methodology is based on a participatory approach supplemented by quantitative and qualitative analysis." [p.3, 3 Methodology]
geography_rationale: Tunisia is a lower-middle-income country. Evidence: "The case study is conducted in the northwest region of Tunisia" [p.3]

population_rationale: Livestock farm households in flood-affected villages of four Punjab (Pakistan) districts; Pakistan is lower-middle income; generic farmers/smallholders, not commercial-scale. Evidence: "Primary data were collected from 204 farm households through a structured interview in flood-prone areas of Punjab." [p.1, Abstract]
concept_rationale: Livestock insurance is framed as a non-structural adaptation measure to flood risk; the study analyses adoption intention (willingness to pay) and its determinants including risk perception. Evidence: "In a situation like this, more adaptation measures must be implemented to mitigate the intensity of the effects of flooding events." [p.2, Introduction] | "Insurance against flood-related damages is one of the nonstructural strategies" [p.2]
context_rationale: Flood risk linked to climate change drives the research question. Evidence: "Pakistan is the world's most susceptible country to extreme climatic events, such as floods." [p.1, Abstract]
methodology_rationale: Structured household survey with contingent valuation and logit regression. Evidence: "Data was analyzed with descriptive statistics and logistics models." [p.1, Abstract]
geography_rationale: Pakistan is a lower-middle-income country. Evidence: "Four districts of the Punjab region, Dera Ghazi Khan, Layyah, Muzaffargarh, and Rajanpur, that have experienced flooding were the subject of this investigation." [p.6, 4.1]

population_rationale: Smallholder farmers in northern Ghana receiving the m-learning module. Evidence: "promoting climate-resilient agriculture among smallholder farmers in northern Ghana" [p.7, Research Design and Methods]
concept_rationale: Documents an adaptation-oriented learning/information-access intervention (climate-resilient practices, indigenous crop diversification) with engagement metrics and farmer feedback on practice impact; adaptation process (learning, access to services). Evidence: "feedback survey was carried out via phone interviews with 66 farmers" [p.8, Methods]
context_rationale: Agricultural setting with climate crisis framing driving the intervention (climate-resilient agriculture, climate-resilience of indigenous crops). Evidence: "address the challenges of sustainable agriculture in the context of climate change" [p.4, Introduction]
methodology_rationale: Empirical: platform engagement metrics, baseline survey (n=367), phone feedback survey (n=66), workshops. Evidence: "The quantitative evaluation metrics of the m-learning module encompassed reach rates, listening rates, and completion rates" [p.8]
geography_rationale: Ghana, lower-middle-income. Evidence: "Upper East, Northern, and Upper West Region of Ghana" [p.8]

lead_rationale: Both reviewers uncertain. Researcher-run rainout-shelter trial with no farmers or adoption analysis; codebook explicitly excludes crop trials without farmer adoption analysis. Recommend exclude.
second_reviewer_decisive_issue: population and methodology (agronomic trial with no farmers studied)
second_reviewer_summary: Rainout-shelter field experiment testing maize-pigeonpea-gliricidia intercrops under drought in semi-arid Tanzania. Concept and context clearly fit (drought adaptation, resilience outcomes), but it is a researcher-run agronomic trial without farmers as participants or adoption analysis. Borderline; inclusion is defensible under the experimental-trial allowance.
exclusion_reason: Borderline on methodology/population: controlled on-station agronomic experiment with no farmer or household data and no adoption analysis.
population_rationale: Research plots on a smallholder's land in a smallholder maize system; no households or farmers are studied, only crop plots framed as representing low-input smallholder systems. Evidence: "the site was under continuous maize cultivation by the landowner, a smallholder farmer" [p.3, Study Site]
concept_rationale: Tests intercropping as a drought adaptation practice and measures adaptation outcomes (yield, drought resistance, resilience). Evidence: "diversification of maize-based cropping systems via intercropping constitutes a tool adapted to low-input smallholder systems" [p.10, Conclusions]
context_rationale: Drought in semi-arid Tanzania drives the research question; drought imposed with rainout shelters. Evidence: "imposing drought in monocultures and additive intercrops" [p.1, Abstract]
methodology_rationale: Measurable empirical field experiment with indicators, but it is an agronomic on-station trial without farmer adoption analysis, which the codebook lists as an exclusion (crop variety trial without farmer adoption analysis). Evidence: "Datasets are available on request." [p.10, Data availability]
geography_rationale: Tanzania, lower-middle-income. Evidence: "Manyusi village, Kongwa District, Dodoma, Tanzania" [p.3]

population_rationale: Smallholder subsistence farm households in the Ethiopian Nile Basin. Evidence: "Farming is characterized by small-holder subsistence farmers. Farm size is on average quite small (less than one hectare)." [p.2, Introduction]
concept_rationale: Analyses determinants of adaptation (changing varieties, soil and water conservation) and its outcome on downside yield risk. Evidence: "whether having adapted to climate change ... affects current environmental risk exposure" [p.2]
context_rationale: Rainfall variability, drought and temperature rise drive the question. Evidence: "Rainfall variability and associated drought have been major causes of food shortage and famine in Ethiopia." [p.2]
methodology_rationale: Household survey, endogenous switching regression with counterfactual analysis. Evidence: "We account for the endogeneity of the adaptation decision by estimating a simultaneous equations model with endogenous switching" [p.3]
geography_rationale: Ethiopia, low-income. Evidence: "The survey was carried out in the Nile River Basin in Ethiopia in 2005." [p.4]
period_language_rationale: Published 2013 online / 2014 in print, English. Evidence: "Environ Resource Econ (2014) 57:553–577" [p.1]

lead_rationale: R2 include. FGDs and key informant interviews code producer adaptation measures to climate threats along value chains.
second_reviewer_decisive_issue: none (all criteria met; adaptation content is partly policy-oriented value-chain analysis)
second_reviewer_summary: Qualitative FGD and key-informant study with Mongolian herders and vegetable growers on climate threats and adaptation measures along value chains. It meets all criteria; the only soft spot is the value-chain and nutrition emphasis, but producer adaptation responses are coded and reported.
exclusion_reason: Borderline on concept: largely perceived climate impacts and proposed (not measured/adopted) adaptation measures.
population_rationale: Herders and vegetable growers (plus traders, consumers) in Mongolia, an LMIC; family herders/small vegetable households are the main FGD participants; commercial scale not the focus. Evidence: "we implemented focus group discussions with 214 livestock and vegetable producers, traders, and food consumers" [p.1, Abstract]
concept_rationale: Core data are producers' perceived climate impacts plus a value-chain analysis proposing adaptation interventions; actual adopted adaptation practices are not measured. Borderline: perception/impact focus (exclusion) vs. documented adaptation strategies and recommendations (Section 3.2). Evidence: "To identify perceived effects of climate change and measures to reduce climate change impacts in Mongolia’s’s key food value chains" [p.1, Abstract] | "climate adaptation strategies to livestock and vegetable production and supply chains" [p.3, Methods (coding categories)]
context_rationale: Pastoral livestock and vegetable production with explicit climate hazards (dzud, drought, heat stress, floods) driving the question. Evidence: "Herders identified five main perceived impacts of climate change across all agro-ecological zones" [p.3, Results]
methodology_rationale: Empirical qualitative study: 19 FGDs and 30 KIIs with thematic analysis. Evidence: "we conducted a thematic analysis in Microsoft Word, drawing on information from the focus groups, the key informant interviews and collected literature" [p.3, Methods]
geography_rationale: Mongolia is a lower-middle-income country. Evidence: "three provinces across four agroecosystems" [p.1, Abstract (paraphrase of 'four agroecosystems in three provinces')]

lead_rationale: Both reviewers uncertain. Storms, floods and salinity are real hazards and livelihood responses are documented, within a multi-risk human-security framing. Include at the margin and flag.
second_reviewer_decisive_issue: concept and context (multi-risk human-security framing; climate hazards only part of the risks)
second_reviewer_summary: Qualitative comparative study of livelihood risks and responses among coastal fishing, shrimp and salt-farming communities in Bangladesh and India. Responses (credit, migration) and storm/flood exposure partly align with adaptation, but the study is framed around human security with crime and conflict dominant. Genuine borderline; inclusive-at-margin could justify keeping it.
exclusion_reason: Borderline on context: climate hazards (storms, floods, salinity) are one of several livelihood risks in a human-security framing; adaptation responses are generic coping (loans, migration).
population_rationale: Small-scale shrimp/crab/fish producers, renu collectors and salt farmers in Bangladesh and India (LMICs); fisheries/aquaculture-dependent communities. Evidence: "The communities studied in Bangladesh depend mainly on the shrimp and fish resources of the Sundarbans mangrove forest." [p.1, Abstract]
concept_rationale: Documents community responses to livelihood risks (accessing loans, labour migration) and assesses their adequacy and governance dimensions; adaptation-aligned though not always labelled climate adaptation. Evidence: "The two main responses to the described livelihood risks in the research regions in Bangladesh and India are accessing loans and migration." [p.13, 3.2]
context_rationale: Storms, floods, salinity and cyclone Aila are central environmental risks, but the paper is framed as multi-risk human security and the dominant risks reported are crime, conflict and resource extraction; climate is one driver among several. Evidence: "While storms and floods are common environmental risks in both countries, related livelihood risks are case-specific." [p.1, Abstract] | "In Bangladesh, attacks by criminals are the major threat to human well-being, while in India, it is violent conflict between lake users." [p.1, Abstract]
methodology_rationale: Empirical qualitative case study: 169 respondents, individual interviews and FGDs plus secondary disaster data. Evidence: "Qualitative research is the main method applied in this study." [p.4, 2.2]
geography_rationale: Bangladesh and India are LMICs. Evidence: "The study was carried out in southwest Bangladesh and East India." [p.4, 2.2]

population_rationale: Agro-pastoral and farming households in Uganda's cattle corridor, a low-income country. Evidence: "seventy-five percent of agro-pastoralists live below the poverty line and lack resources" [p.3, 3.1]
concept_rationale: Measures adoption of 33 drought adaptation strategies and evaluates their effects on income, assets and welfare. Evidence: "This study evaluates the effectiveness of gendered adaptation strategies to boost resilience to climate hazard and risks." [p.2, 1.2]
context_rationale: Recurrent drought and rainfall variability drive the research question in dryland agriculture. Evidence: "proneness to extreme climatic events, particularly recurrent and severe droughts, prolonged dry spells, and unpredictable rainfall patterns" [p.3, 3.1]
methodology_rationale: Household survey (n=1106), FGDs, KIIs with chi-square, PCA and regression. Evidence: "This cross-sectional, exploratory mixed-methods study aimed to investigate households in the Rakai, Nakasongola, and Nabilatuk districts" [p.4, 3.2.1]
geography_rationale: Uganda is a low-income country. Evidence: "three districts, namely Rakai in the South" [p.3, 3.1]
period_language_rationale: Published April 2025, English. Evidence: "Available online 23 April 2025" [p.1]

population_rationale: 76 agro-pastoralists (men and women) in two villages of Kaffrine, Senegal, rain-fed smallholder systems. Evidence: "This study gathered 76 agro-pastoralists to whom the different tools were explained." [p.3, Data collection]
concept_rationale: Documents adaptation processes (participatory planning, decision-making, adoption of climate-smart practices, institutions) and farmer-perceived adoption drivers. Evidence: "Also determinant drivers of adoption of the technologies were identified." [p.1, Abstract]
context_rationale: Drought, flooding and strong winds drive the research question in rain-fed Sahelian agriculture. Evidence: "The three main hazards said, both by men and by women, to mostly affect livelihood resources were strong winds, flooding and drought" [p.4, Results]
methodology_rationale: Empirical participatory tools (vulnerability matrices, CRiSTAL, VAP) plus a stakeholder survey. Evidence: "a survey was conducted to evaluate the perception of the stakeholders on the most significant activities of the project" [p.4, Data collection]
geography_rationale: Senegal is a lower-middle-income country. Evidence: "This study was conducted in the Kaffrine Region, intervention site of the Climate Change, Agriculture and Food Security (CCAFS) program in Senegal." [p.2, Study area]
period_language_rationale: Published 2017, English. Evidence: "Sanogo et al. Agric & Food Secur (2017) 6:13" [p.1]

population_rationale: Pastoral households (livestock keepers, small agro-pastoralism) in Marsabit, Kenya. Evidence: "These communities rely on livestock as their primary livelihood source." [p.2, Study area]
concept_rationale: Analyses livelihood diversification/exit pathways and income and herd outcomes conditional on drought, with IBLI insurance and credit as variables; livelihood response to climate stress per codebook. Evidence: "this study quantitatively determined the dynamic transitions between livelihood categories conditional on drought incidences." [p.1, Abstract]
context_rationale: Drought in arid/semi-arid northern Kenya drives the research question. Evidence: "The effect of drought as indicated by CZNDVI was significant across all the four pastoralist livelihood pathways" [p.6, Results]
methodology_rationale: Six-round household panel and dynamic multinomial logit with NDVI. Evidence: "this study applied a generalized structural dynamic multinomial logit model to determine the effect of drought on pastoralist livelihood pathways." [p.5, Modelling strategy]
geography_rationale: Kenya, lower-middle income. Evidence: "The study was conducted in Marsabit County in northern Kenya (Fig. 1)." [p.2]
period_language_rationale: 2022, English. Evidence: "Kirui et al. Pastoralism: Research, Policy and Practice (2022) 12:23" [p.1]

population_rationale: 900 dairy farmers (smallholder milk producers) in four West African countries; no commercial-scale focus. Evidence: "Individual interview and Focus Group Discussions were conducted among 900 dairy farmers." [p.2, Abstract]
concept_rationale: Beyond perceptions, documents and typologises adaptation strategies adopted (fodder, water, milk conservation). Evidence: "Multiple Correspondence Analysis and hierarchical clustering on principal component analysis were used to access the adaptation strategies of dairy farmers." [p.2, Abstract]
context_rationale: Rainfall decline and temperature/drought drive the research question. Evidence: "Currently, dairy production has become vulnerable due to climate variability." [p.2, Abstract]
methodology_rationale: Primary interviews with statistical and multivariate analysis. Evidence: "Data were collected using semi-structured interviews." [p.3, Data collection]
geography_rationale: Benin, Burkina Faso, Mali, Niger. Evidence: "The study was carried out in four West African countries Benin, Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger." [p.3]
period_language_rationale: Preprint 2021; published 2022; English. Evidence: "A version of this preprint was published at Climatic Change on February 1st, 2022." [p.1]

population_rationale: Survey of 160 wheat-producing farmers in Bangladesh (mean farm size 1.31 ha, 0.60 ha wheat); generic farmers in an LMIC, not commercial-scale. Evidence: "The average farm size of the farmers was 1.31 ha, while an average of 0.60 ha of land is devoted to wheat farming." [p.5, Socioeconomic characteristics]
concept_rationale: Beyond perceptions, the study documents adopted adaptation strategies and their determinants (MNL), plus barriers; adoption/uptake of adaptation is an included process. Evidence: "Key adaptation strategies identified were more irrigation, switching to other crops, and changing fertilizer and insecticide usage." [p.1, Abstract]
context_rationale: Agricultural setting with explicit drought, rainfall and temperature stress driving the research question. Evidence: "The northwest region, on the other hand, is predominantly prone to drought and receives significantly less rainfall than the rest of the country" [p.2, Introduction]
methodology_rationale: Structured household survey with multinomial logit analysis and descriptive statistics. Evidence: "Face-to-face interviews with respondents were conducted using a structured interview schedule." [p.3, Study area and data]
geography_rationale: Bangladesh, lower-middle-income. Evidence: "two northwestern districts, Dinajpur and Thakurgaon, were selected purposively" [p.3, Study area and data]
period_language_rationale: Published 2022/2023, English. Evidence: "Environmental Science and Pollution Research (2023) 30:32839–32853" [p.1 header]

population_rationale: Rice-farming households (about 2 ha) in the Mekong Delta; authors refer to results as smallholder perception. Evidence: "Our results improve our knowledge of the smallholder perception of climate change in Vietnam’s Mekong Delta" [p.4, Introduction]
concept_rationale: Analyses numbers of farm and household financial adaptation strategies adopted by operators and spouses, not perception alone. Evidence: "the study investigates the impact of the perception of climatic stress on the operators’ and spouses’ intra-household adaptation strategies (farm and household financial strategies)" [p.1, Abstract]
context_rationale: Climatic stresses (flood, drought, salinity, heat, sea-level rise) affecting rice production drive the question. Evidence: "Vietnamese agriculture is affected by natural disasters such as flooding, drought, saltwater intrusion and torrential rains and typhoons" [p.2, Introduction]
methodology_rationale: Household survey with probit and negative binomial hurdle models. Evidence: "The study uses probit and negative binomial count data approaches to evaluate the empirical model." [p.1, Abstract]
geography_rationale: Vietnam, lower-middle-income. Evidence: "The study uses household survey data from Vietnam’s Mekong Delta." [p.1, Abstract]
period_language_rationale: Published 2017, English. Evidence: "International Journal of Climate Change Strategies and Management Vol. 9 No. 4, 2017 pp. 501-516" [p.1]

lead_rationale: R2 include. Water-conservation behaviour of farmers in a drought-stressed basin (behaviour change as adaptation process); framing is partly pro-environmental. Include at the margin.
second_reviewer_summary: Survey-based SEM of Iranian farmers' water conservation intention and behaviour in a drought- and climate-stressed semi-arid basin. The concept link is moderate (behavioural determinants of water saving framed as moral/pro-environmental), but at the inclusive margin of a systematic map it meets adaptation process (behaviour change) criteria.
exclusion_reason: Borderline on concept and context: water-conservation behaviour driven by moral norms for lake restoration; climate/adaptation framing is secondary.
population_rationale: Generic farmers (300 male farmers, irrigating from groundwater, 70% own land) in Iran; no commercial-scale focus. Smallholder status is not stated explicitly, so the generic-farmer rule applies. Evidence: "In terms of land ownership, over 70% of the participants held ownership rights to their agricultural lands." [p.6, Results]
concept_rationale: Measures farmers' water-saving intention and behaviour (optimising waterways, fallowing, reduced water use), which is behaviour change under water scarcity, but the framing is pro-environmental/moral motivation to restore Urmia Lake rather than adaptation of farm livelihoods to climate risk; authors only loosely link it to adaptation. Evidence: "it is essential to facilitate adaptation by assisting farmers in creating water-conserving revenue streams and growing local enterprises" [p.10, Policy insights] | "I reduce my water consumption by optimizing the route, shape, dimensions, and cover of waterways" [p.6, Table 1]
context_rationale: Semi-arid water scarcity with climate change and drought named as stressors on the lake, which counts under the water-scarcity rule, but the driver of the research question is lake desiccation and agricultural over-abstraction, with climate partly background. Evidence: "Water bodies across (semi)arid regions are being pressured by climate change and agriculture." [p.1, Abstract]
methodology_rationale: Structured questionnaire survey of 300 farmers analysed with CFA and SEM. Evidence: "a quantitative cross-sectional survey was designed to target a cohort of 300 selected farmers" [p.5, Methods]
geography_rationale: Iran, an LMIC (codebook lists Iran). Evidence: "the ULB situated in northwest Iran" [p.3, Case study]
period_language_rationale: Published December 2024 / volume 2025, English. Evidence: "Environmental and Sustainability Indicators 25 (2025) 100567" [p.1 header]

population_rationale: Farm households in Yulin, Shaanxi, China (upper-middle-income); sample restricted to farms of 6.67 ha or less, i.e. small-scale farmers. Evidence: "This study selected samples of farmers with a family-cultivated land area of 6.67 ha or less, totaling 746 samples." [p.5, 3.2 Data collection]
concept_rationale: Assesses adoption (56.4% already adopted) and intention to adopt, publicise and pay for water-saving irrigation, an adaptation-aligned water management practice; adoption determinants are an included process. Intention rather than only behaviour, which is mildly borderline. Evidence: "SmartPLS 4 was used to perform PLS-SEM" [p.6] | "56.4% had adopted WSI" [p.6, 4.1.1]
context_rationale: Study site is a drought-prone, low-rainfall semi-arid area where water scarcity is the stated bottleneck (codebook: water scarcity in semi-arid regions counts), but climate hazards are framed as background; the research question is about policy evaluation and technology acceptance. Evidence: "experiences a continental monsoon climate characterized by drought, low rainfall, and frequent sandstorms, with 76% of its arable land classified as dry land" [p.4, 3.1 Study region] | "WSI addresses water scarcity in arid and semi-arid regions and ensures stable grain production." [p.13, Conclusions]
methodology_rationale: Primary face-to-face survey of 746 farmers analysed with ordered logit and PLS-SEM. Evidence: "a face-to-face questionnaire survey of farmers in the six northern counties of Yulin City conducted by the research team from December 2023 to January 2024" [p.5, 3.2]
geography_rationale: China is upper-middle-income. Evidence: "Yulin City is the second largest granary in Shaanxi" [p.4]
period_language_rationale: English; published March 2026, which is after 2005 (codebook) but outside the protocol window upper bound of 2025. Evidence: "Available online 25 March 2026" [p.1]

population_rationale: Interviewed rice and fish farming households in a coastal commune in Vietnam (LMIC); small-scale household producers. Evidence: "Residents mainly worked in rice and ﬁsh farming." [p.6, Methodology]
concept_rationale: Household survey documents adaptation measures taken (crop restructuring, salt-tolerant varieties, shift to aquaculture, livelihood conversion, borrowing) and assesses adaptive capacity; adaptation is measured, not only impacts. The soil-salinity ML mapping part is impact assessment but is accompanied by the adaptation component. Evidence: "66 % of interviewed households said they had to change the crop structure to suit the saline intrusion or switch to non-agricultural occupations to earn more income." [p.12, 4.4.1]
context_rationale: Agriculture in a delta where saline intrusion is tied to sea level rise, dry-season low river flow and climate change; climate-driven hazard drives the question. Evidence: "they have become highly susceptible to the effects of climate variability and sea-level rise" [p.2, Introduction]
methodology_rationale: Machine learning validated with field EC samples, Sentinel imagery and structured interviews with 87 households. Evidence: "A total of 87 households were interviewed." [p.6, Methodology]
geography_rationale: Vietnam is lower-middle-income. Evidence: "Red River Delta of Vietnam" [p.4, Fig. 1]

population_rationale: Small-scale brackish-water shrimp aquaculture households in Vietnam (LMIC); described as small-scale, low-income producers. Evidence: "dominated by small-scale brackish water aquaculture producers" [p.9, Discussion]
concept_rationale: Evaluates adoption of an adaptation practice (shrimp-tilapia polyculture), its profitability (NPV, BCR) and perceived adaptive capacity/resilience outcomes, plus barriers to adoption. Evidence: "We study the private profitability and farmer perceived resilience effects of adaptation through polyculture of shrimp with mono-sex tilapia" [p.1, Abstract]
context_rationale: Climate hazards (erratic rainfall, 'Tieu Man' flooding and salinity swings, temperature extremes) motivate the practice. Evidence: "farmers identified erratic rainfall, extreme and unpredicted temperature fluctuation, and poor water quality as the main causes of shrimp and fish diseases" [p.6, 4.1]
methodology_rationale: Household survey with inverse-probability-weighted cost-benefit analysis and Likert perception items. Evidence: "profitability analysis of shrimp-tilapia polyculture followed a two-step procedure, combining inverse-probability weighting with CBA" [p.5, 3]
geography_rationale: Vietnam is lower-middle-income. Evidence: "The study was conducted in Hoang Phong commune in Thanh Hoa province within the NCC region of Vietnam" [p.3, 3]

population_rationale: Women in climate-sensitive agropastoral/crop and livestock livelihoods in Garissa County, Kenya (LMIC), targeted by a community-based adaptation programme. Evidence: "communities rely heavily on climate-sensitive livelihood strategies such as crop production and livestock rearing" [p.2, 1.2]
concept_rationale: Documents adaptation interventions (income diversification, participatory scenario planning, climate field schools) and their outcomes on adaptive capacity, food security, income and health. Evidence: "Adaptive agricultural practices consisted of" [p.3, 2.4]
context_rationale: Arid and semi-arid agricultural setting with droughts and floods driving the programme and research question. Evidence: "Garissa has experienced more severe flooding and droughts as a result of climate change" [p.2, 1.2]
methodology_rationale: Single interpretivist case study analysing six grey-literature programme reports with a systematic analysis framework; no primary data. Counts as narrative/documentary empirical case study rather than a formal systematic or literature review, but it is borderline. Evidence: "Data was collected from grey literature published and was analysed using a systematic framework." [p.1, Abstract]
geography_rationale: Kenya is lower-middle-income. Evidence: "Garissa County in Kenya" [p.1, Abstract]

lead_rationale: Both reviewers: narrative overview chapter with no own method (methodology exclusion).
second_reviewer_summary: A narrative overview chapter on the push-pull IPM technology in which climate adaptation is a single sub-section. No defined measurement method or indicators, and climate is not the main driver of the research question, so the methodology criterion (literature/overview exclusion) and concept/context weaken it. Excluded, with moderate confidence.
exclusion_reason: Methodology (narrative review, no own method) and context (climate as secondary; IPM focus); concept borderline.
population_rationale: Smallholder farmers in East Africa. Evidence: "over 55,000 smallholder farmers in East Africa are practicing push–pull technology" [p.6, 13.2.3]
concept_rationale: Primarily an IPM/pest-management technology; climate adaptation (drought-tolerant companion plants) is one sub-section. Uptake and yield outcomes are reported but mostly as technology benefits, not as adaptation assessment. Evidence: "adapted to dry conditions associated with climate change by identifying and incorporating drought-tolerant companion plants" [p.2, Abstract]
context_rationale: Climate change is background/secondary; the research question is stemborer and striga control. Only section 13.2.6 addresses drought. Evidence: "Although the technology was originally devised to control insect pests" [p.12, 13.5]
methodology_rationale: Narrative book-chapter review of prior push-pull studies with no stated methods, sampling or analysis of its own (review/opinion-type). Evidence: "The development of this technology, its benefits and subsequent efforts to expand its geographical suitability and effectiveness are described." [p.2, Abstract]
geography_rationale: Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania, Ethiopia are LMICs. Evidence: "smallholder farmers in drier parts of Kenya, Tanzania, and Ethiopia" [p.9, 13.2.6]
period_language_rationale: Published 2014, English. Evidence: "© Springer Science+Business Media Dordrecht 2014" [p.1]

lead_rationale: R2 include (low). Farmer adoption survey of quinoa as a drought- and salinity-tolerant diversification option; much of the paper is market analysis. Include at the margin.
second_reviewer_summary: Value-chain, adoption and market assessment of quinoa, framed as an adaptation/diversification option for drought and salinity in dry Moroccan smallholder areas, with a farmer adoption survey. Concept fit is partial because much content is consumer marketing, but under inclusive mapping rules it is retained.
population_rationale: Smallholder subsistence farmers in Rehamna, Morocco, with women interviewed; consumer survey is additional. Evidence: "There are about 6000 smallholders' farmers in the region living on a subsistence" [p.9, Discussion]
concept_rationale: Assesses adoption/interest in a stress-tolerant crop as adaptation and its income margins, but the focus is value chain and consumer marketing; adoption is limited to awareness, interest and current cultivation. Evidence: "The purpose of this study is to evaluate the adoption of quinoa and its market in Morocco" [p.3]
context_rationale: Drought, salinity and water scarcity in a dry region motivate introducing quinoa as adaptation. Evidence: "Agriculture faces many challenges such as climate change, droughts, and salinity, which requires urgent interventions for fast adaptation" [p.1, Abstract]
methodology_rationale: Farmer survey (~500), consumer survey (544), production cost analysis and secondary import data. Evidence: "interviewing about 500 farmers including 318 men and 182 women" [p.3, Methods]
geography_rationale: Morocco is lower-middle-income. Evidence: "Rehamna region is one of the driest regions in Morocco" [p.9]

population_rationale: Household-level sample of crop farmers (paddy, groundnut) in two Tamil Nadu villages; 70% are marginal (<1 ha) farmers, so smallholders are analysed as a distinct group by landholding class. Evidence: "Seventy percent of the total samples are marginal farmers who have the lowest FRI of 0.47" [p.1, Abstract]
concept_rationale: Measures resilience/adaptive capacity (an adaptation outcome under the codebook) with an index whose variables include adaptation-relevant factors (access to credit to prevent disaster, climate information, extension, knowledge of flood-resistant varieties, drainage). Borderline because it is an index and no specific adaptation practice is tracked, but resilience is a listed outcome. Evidence: "The outcomes of the index reveal the current adaptive capacities of the farmers and have the potential to support future planning decisions." [p.1, Abstract]
context_rationale: Agricultural setting with explicit precipitation-extreme hazards (Cyclone Thane 2011, 2015 floods) driving crop loss. Evidence: "The recent past two disasters namely Cyclone Thane (2011) and the South Indian floods (2015) had caused major crop loss in Cuddalore, India." [p.1, Abstract]
methodology_rationale: Household questionnaire survey, PCA-weighted composite index, correlation and Wilcoxon tests; empirical. Evidence: "The principal component analysis (PCA) has been done for the variables under each dimension for each village separately for fixing the weights." [p.9, 3.1]
geography_rationale: India (lower-middle income). Evidence: "coastal farming communities of Tamil Nadu, India" [p.1, Title]
period_language_rationale: Published June 2021, English. Evidence: "Available online 21 June 2021" [p.16]

population_rationale: Rain-fed subsistence farming households in southern Malawi. Evidence: "Agriculture in the Shire River Basin is characterized by subsistence farming on customary land tenure" [p.4, 2.1]
concept_rationale: Documents coping/adaptation responses to crop failure (irrigation, crop diversification, off-farm labour, etc.) and their determinants; authors frame coping as first step in adaptation. Evidence: "This paper examines farmers’ coping strategies for crop failure and the determinants of their choices" [p.1, Abstract]
context_rationale: Drought, flood, erratic rainfall and temperature are the main stated causes of crop failure. Evidence: "more than half of the households (53%) listed climatic factors as the major causes" [p.7, 3.1]
methodology_rationale: Household survey with probit regression. Evidence: "This study is based on primary data collected through household surveys during the agricultural season of 2009." [p.5, 2.2]
geography_rationale: Malawi (low income). Evidence: "household level data from rural southern Malawi" [p.1, Abstract]

population_rationale: Village farmers (about 0.4-0.5 ha cultivated per capita) and herders in four villages; non-commercial rural households. Evidence: "The per capita area of cultivated land of each farmer was 0.48 ha and 0.36 ha in Pingandi and Fenghuangling" [p.4, 3.1.1]
concept_rationale: Documents adaptation responses to drought (land abandonment, livelihood diversification, selling lambs, grazing elsewhere) and their income outcomes. Evidence: "Under drought, farmers tended to abandon rain-fed land, and herders tended to abandon grassland." [p.1, Abstract]
context_rationale: Drought in semi-arid agro-pastoral zone is the driver of the research question. Evidence: "drought is the main factor influencing land use and livelihoods" [p.1, Abstract]
methodology_rationale: PRA, interviews and questionnaire survey with income accounting. Evidence: "The methods of participatory rural appraisal and questionnaire survey were employed" [p.2, 2.2]
geography_rationale: China (upper-middle income). Evidence: "Ar Horqin Banner, located in the agro-pastoral ecotone of northwestern China" [p.1, Abstract]

population_rationale: 80 farmers in four villages of Kailaras block, Madhya Pradesh, India, practising mixed crop-livestock farming; generic farmers in an LMIC, not commercial-scale. Evidence: "Four villages Kailaras gramin, Kirawali, Shekhpur and Madhougarh were selected from one block and 80 farmers were selected from 4 villages." [p.2, Materials and Methods]
concept_rationale: Documents the actual coping/adaptation responses farmers adopt to flood, drought, pests, hail and water scarcity (shifting crops, fodder crops, tube-well irrigation, migration), plus information sources; adaptation actions are measured. Evidence: "the farmers were adopting many risk coping strategy in different situations" [p.2, Results and Data Analysis]
context_rationale: Agricultural risk from drought, flood, hail and water scarcity drives the survey; drought reported as most serious risk. Evidence: "Maximum agricultural households (59%) reported that drought risk was the most serious" [p.4, Conclusion]
methodology_rationale: Structured, pre-tested interview schedule on 80 farmers with percentage reporting; measurable empirical method. Evidence: "Primary data were collected from farmers by direct interview method with well structured, pre tested schedule" [p.2, Materials and Methods]
geography_rationale: Madhya Pradesh, India (lower-middle income). Evidence: "The present study will confine to Madhya Pradesh State." [p.2, Materials and Methods]
period_language_rationale: Published March 2015, English. Evidence: "Volume 6 | Issue 1 | March, 2015 | 140-144" [p.1 header]

population_rationale: Rural households in five Okavango Delta villages combining subsistence molapo/dryland arable farming and livestock keeping; smallholder subsistence producers in an upper-middle-income country. Evidence: "Households combine subsistence arable farming (molapo or dryland farming) and livestock with other livelihood activities" [p.6, 3.2]
concept_rationale: Objective 3 identifies and assesses household coping and adaptive strategies (labour switching, relocation, livelihood diversification, early harvesting) and adaptive capacity via capital access indices. Evidence: "(3) identifying and assessing household responses to extreme flooding" [p.2, Introduction]
context_rationale: Extreme flooding (climate variability) affecting crops and livestock drives the research question. Evidence: "The main impacts of extreme flooding were crop damage (53%), household displacement (18%), destruction of household property (12%), livestock drowning and mud-trapping (11%)" [p.8, 3.3]
methodology_rationale: Household survey of 623 households plus key informant interviews and focus groups, with capital access indices. Evidence: "a simple random sample of 623 households representing 40% of the accessible population was drawn" [p.3, 2.3.1]
geography_rationale: Botswana, upper-middle-income. Evidence: "The study was undertaken in the Okavango Delta situated in Ngamiland District of Botswana." [p.2, 2.2]
period_language_rationale: Published 2011, English. Evidence: "Physics and Chemistry of the Earth 36 (2011) 984–995" [p.1 header]

lead_rationale: R1 uncertain, R2 exclude: agroecological land-restoration adoption under an asset-based community development approach; climate is background and practices are not framed as adaptation.
second_reviewer_summary: Evaluation of an asset-based community development approach on agroecological practice integration among Kenyan smallholders. Population, method and geography fit, but climate risk is only background and the practices are not framed as climate adaptation, so context and concept are not met. A reviewer valuing the resilience elements of the tool could argue for uncertain.
exclusion_reason: Borderline on concept and context: agroecological land-restoration adoption with climate only as background framing; the paper never frames the outcomes as climate adaptation.
population_rationale: Smallholder farmer households and community groups in Homa Bay County, Kenya (lower-middle-income). Evidence: "to encourage 50,000 smallholder farmers to adopt sustainable restoration practices over 5 years" [p.2, Introduction]
concept_rationale: The study measures adoption of and behaviour change toward agroecological land-restoration (Regreening) practices, an adoption/participation process outcome. It is framed as agroecological integration and sustainable scaling, not explicitly as climate adaptation, so it is a borderline fit. Evidence: "improved adoption of context-specific sustainable and agroecological land restoration options" [p.8, 2.4.3]
context_rationale: Climate change appears among barriers and in the framing of land degradation. The research question is about ABCD, agroecology and scaling of restoration practices, not a specific climate hazard. Climate looks like background, but the conclusion links the work to climate-resilient livelihoods. Evidence: "Key biophysical factors included land degradation, climate change, limited access to water" [p.2, Introduction] | "The land restoration agenda must be driven by local communities to build climate-resilient livelihoods and landscapes" [p.19, 4.4]
methodology_rationale: Baseline and endline household panel survey analysed with a doubly robust difference-in-differences estimator; empirical and measurable. Evidence: "we used the doubly robust difference-indifferences (DRDID) estimator proposed by Sant’Anna and Zhao (2020)" [p.10, 2.4.4]
geography_rationale: Kenya (lower-middle income). Evidence: "this study was conducted in the Regreening Africa “intervention” site in Homa Bay County in the wider western region of Kenya" [p.5, 2.1]

lead_rationale: Both reviewers: national-scale seafood supply modelling; no small-scale producer population.
second_reviewer_summary: National-scale modelling of seafood self-sufficiency under climate-adaptive fisheries management in 31 small island nations. No smallholder or small-scale producer population is studied and adaptation is a hypothetical scenario, so population (and weakly concept) is not met; excluded with moderate confidence since a lenient reader could treat national fisheries governance as in scope.
exclusion_reason: Population criterion: national-scale fisheries projections, no small-scale producers/households studied; concept and methodology also borderline.
population_rationale: Unit of analysis is national-level wild fisheries catch and national seafood demand; no individuals/households or small-scale producers are studied or analysed as a distinct group. Evidence: "estimate potential seafood surpluses or deficits from by 2050 for 31 small island nations worldwide" [p.1, Abstract]
concept_rationale: Evaluates scenarios of climate-adaptive fisheries management (adaptation governance) and seafood self-sufficiency outcomes, but as modelled national projections, not documented adaptation processes/outcomes of producers. Evidence: "The adaptation scenarios from Free et al. [15] assume perfect and instant adaptation to climate-driven changes in fisheries productivity and distribution" [p.2, Methods]
context_rationale: Marine fisheries with explicit climate-change scenarios (RCPs) driving the research question. Evidence: "The projections explore four different future climate change scenarios (RCPs 2.6, 4.5, 6.0, 8.5)" [p.2, Methods]
methodology_rationale: Quantitative projection using existing bioeconomic model outputs and FAO data; no primary empirical data or validation. Not a review or purely theoretical, so borderline. Evidence: "We used the Free et al. [17] climate-linked fisheries bioeconomic model to examine country-level changes in seafood production" [p.3, Methods 2.2.4]
geography_rationale: Small island nations, mostly LMICs (Singapore excluded as high-income). Evidence: "we excluded Singapore from this analysis due to its vastly different economic classification" [p.2, Methods]

population_rationale: Smallholder rice/wheat farmers in Bihar, India (landholdings <2.5 acres), India is lower-middle income. Evidence: "Smallholder farmers are exposed to growing uncertainty and risks" [p.1, Introduction] | "land holding sizes of <2.5 acres" [p.4, Study Context]
concept_rationale: Evaluates adoption of varietal diversification as an adaptation strategy and outcomes (productivity, recovery from shocks). Evidence: "the ability of households to recover from agricultural production shocks" [p.1, Abstract]
context_rationale: Climate-sensitive Bihar; S4N aims to reduce vulnerability to climate change; climatic stressors and rainfall fluctuation motivate the study. Evidence: "Bihar is one of the most climate-sensitive states in India. Rainfall fluctuates greatly from one season to another" [p.4, Study Context]
methodology_rationale: Household survey with quasi-experimental doubly robust estimator and GMM system. Evidence: "this empirical analysis relies on a specific estimator used in quasi-experimental study, the doubly robust (DR)" [p.7, Empirical Analysis]
geography_rationale: India, LMIC. Evidence: "in Bihar, India from 2010 to 2017" [p.2, Introduction]

population_rationale: Household survey of 100 farm households in a Tunisian village (mean 15 ha, 26 sheep) in barley-rangeland-livestock systems; family farming, not commercial/industrial agriculture. Evidence: "Climate changes have been affecting the livelihoods of the low income households depending on family farming in central and southern parts of the country" [p.1, Introduction] | "a household owns about 15 ha and has 26 sheep (Table 1)" [p.4, Study site]
concept_rationale: Assesses adoption of and economic outcomes (NPV, IRR, income) of two tree-based adaptation options (olive plantation, cactus alley cropping) and farmer adaptation trends. Evidence: "We assess the social and private profitability of two alternative tree-based adaptation techniques" [p.1, Abstract]
context_rationale: Semi-arid Tunisia; water scarcity, drought and projected rainfall decline under climate change drive the question. Evidence: "Climate change exacerbates the effects of water scarcity on livelihoods." [p.1, Abstract] | "The drought frequency is 6 years in a decade." [p.4, Study site]
methodology_rationale: Empirical household survey (n=100) plus secondary yield and climate data used in a social/private cost-benefit analysis. Evidence: "The questionnaire was administered randomly to a stratified sample of 100 households" [p.5, 3.3 Economic data]
geography_rationale: Tunisia is a lower-middle-income country. Evidence: "The study was conducted at the Zoghmar village, Sidi Bouzid governorate, central Tunisia" [p.4, 3.1]
period_language_rationale: Published 2019, English. Evidence: "NEW MEDIT N. 2/2019" [p.2 header]

lead_rationale: R1 uncertain, R2 exclude: socio-economic profile of fishers with a brief coping section; climate hazards are one background risk among many.
second_reviewer_decisive_issue: context (climate is background; concept only weakly adaptation)
second_reviewer_summary: Descriptive socio-economic and fishing operation study of Sundarbans artisanal fishers. A short section on coping with vulnerabilities exists, but climate hazards are one background risk among many and not the driving question. Excluded on context, with concept borderline.
exclusion_reason: Context criterion borderline: climate hazards are one of several background drivers; study is a socio-economic profile with a coping-strategy section.
population_rationale: Artisanal (small-scale) fishers in two villages on the edge of the Sundarbans, Bangladesh; subsistence-oriented small boats. Evidence: "Artisanal fisheries are small-scale fisheries where fishers use traditional fishing techniques and small boats for the sake of subsistence living" [p.1, Introduction]
concept_rationale: Documents coping/adaptation strategies (occupational change, migration, association forming, household labour sharing, knowledge transmission) as a distinct results section, though the paper is mainly a socio-economic profile. Evidence: "the artisanal fishermen adopted different strategies to cope with the changing conditions by forming associations, violating the fisheries laws and regulations, migrating, sharing responsibilities with the household members" [p.1, Abstract]
context_rationale: Climate stressors (cyclones, flooding, salinity, higher temperature) are mentioned among many drivers of mangrove and livelihood decline, but the research question is socio-economic and fishing operations; climate is arguably background rather than the driver. Coping responses are mostly to poverty, resource decline, and insecurity. Evidence: "climate change issues manifested in the form higher temperature and higher salinity in the SMF rivers, anthropogenic disturbances like shrimp farming, natural disasters (cyclones and flooding) were responsible for the deterioration of mangroves" [p.6, Mangroves Resources for Making Livelihoods]
methodology_rationale: Empirical qualitative case study: 70 semi-structured interviews, 2 FGDs, 10 key informant interviews, thematic content analysis. Evidence: "In total, seventy interviews were concluded, fifty of which were with fishers (men 40 and women 10)." [p.3, Study Areas and Methods]
geography_rationale: Bangladesh (lower-middle income). Evidence: "The study was conducted with two artisanal fishing communities" [p.3, Study Areas and Methods]
period_language_rationale: Published 2018, English. Evidence: "Turkish Journal of Fisheries and Aquatic Sciences 18: 789-799 (2018)" [p.1 header]

lead_rationale: Split (R1 exclude, R2 include). R1 documents farms of 420 ha or more in the mechanized rainfed sector, which is large-scale commercial agriculture (codebook population exclusion). Recommend exclude; co-authors to confirm farm scale.
second_reviewer_decisive_issue: population (scale of mechanized farms is the only doubt)
second_reviewer_summary: Combines rainfall-onset analysis with interviews on sowing-date decisions and coping strategies under rainfall variability in eastern Sudan. Concept, context, method and geography clearly fit; population is the only doubt because the mechanized rainfed sector includes large farms, but the study does not clearly restrict to commercial scale. Include at the margin.
exclusion_reason: Population criterion: large-scale mechanized commercial rainfed farms, no smallholder analysis.
population_rationale: Focus is the rainfed mechanized/semi-mechanized sector of El Gedaref; farms observed are 1000-13,000 feddan (420 ha-5,460 ha) and an interviewee is a 'large scale farmer'. This is large-scale commercial agriculture, not smallholders; smallholders are mentioned only in passing and not analysed as a group. Evidence: "eastern Sudan is an illustrative case study to draw from the experience of the rainfed mechanized agricultural sector of El Gedaref State" [p.2, Problem statement] | "Most farms which are larger than 1000 feddan (420 ha) are semi-mechanized" [p.9, 5.3.5 Socio-economic factors]
concept_rationale: Analyses farmers' sowing-date decision-making and coping/adaptation practices (variety mixing, delayed sowing, resowing) to rainfall variability. Evidence: "the farmers' choice of an appropriate sowing date is one important adaptation and management strategy to climate change and variability" [p.2, Problem statement]
context_rationale: Rainfall variability and dry spells in Sahelian rainfed sorghum drive the research question. Evidence: "Inappropriate sowing date constitutes a major reason for crop failure and low yields in the African Sahel region." [p.1, Abstract]
methodology_rationale: Climatic onset/sowing-date methods applied to 1971-2010 daily rainfall plus semi-structured interviews and farm observations. Evidence: "Daily rainfall records for the period 1971–2010 are available from the meteorological station for El Gedaref city" [p.4, 4.2]
geography_rationale: Sudan is an LMIC. Evidence: "Taking El Gedaref State in eastern Sudan as a case study" [p.2]
period_language_rationale: Published 2016 (online Jan 2016), English. Evidence: "Land Use Policy 52 (2016) 316–328" [p.1 header]

population_rationale: Small farmers practising subsistence farming; 52% of farms are under 1 ha in the zone. Evidence: "The local population practices subsistence farming based on the cultivation of cereals" [p.5, Methodology] | "Fifty-two percent of the farms do not exceed 1 ha in size" [p.5]
concept_rationale: Documents adoption of adaptation strategies (drip irrigation, wells, planting date changes, diversification, migration). Evidence: "Sixty percent of the interviewees declared that they have implemented some actions to protect the water resource" [p.11]
context_rationale: Climate change, drought and temperature rise affecting saffron drive the research question. Evidence: "how do the saffron producers adapt to the climate change that is affecting the area" [p.3, Introduction]
methodology_rationale: Questionnaire survey of 60 farmers plus semi-structured stakeholder interviews. Evidence: "Sixty farmers chosen randomly were surveyed using a questionnaire" [p.5]
geography_rationale: Morocco is an LMIC. Evidence: "a study was carried out in the zone of Taliouine in the AntiAtlas, south of Morocco" [p.3]

lead_rationale: Both reviewers: ICT/leadership/farmer-independence survey; climate background only.
second_reviewer_summary: Survey of Indonesian rice farmers on ICT use, group leadership and farmer independence. Climate hazards are only introductory background and no adaptation measure or outcome is assessed. Excluded on concept and context.
exclusion_reason: Concept and context criteria fail: no climate adaptation measured; climate hazards are background only (ICT, leadership and farmer independence study).
population_rationale: Rice farmers who are members of farmer groups in Riau, Indonesia (LMIC); generic farmers, no sign of commercial scale. Evidence: "The study population consists of rice farmers who are members of farmer groups." [p.2, Materials and methods]
concept_rationale: The study tests ICT role -> group leadership -> farmer independence (PLS-SEM). No climate adaptation action, process or outcome is measured; independence is an empowerment construct. General development/extension without climate-adaptation measurement. Evidence: "The objectives of this study were to analyze the influence of ICT roles on group leadership roles, the impact of ICT roles on farmers' independence" [p.1, Abstract]
context_rationale: Flooding, drought and pests are mentioned only as background to falling rice output; they do not drive the research question or any measured variable. Evidence: "crop failure in rice cultivation is caused by climate change (Nur et al., 2023), floods and droughts (Jamil & Chairunnisya, 2023), as well as pest attacks and plant diseases." [p.1, Introduction]
methodology_rationale: Survey of 301 farmers with PLS-SEM; empirical method. Evidence: "The research approach is quantitative and uses a survey method supported by qualitative data." [p.2, Materials and methods]
geography_rationale: Riau Province, Indonesia (upper-middle-income). Evidence: "The study was conducted in Riau Province, which was deliberately selected (purposive)." [p.2, Materials and methods]
period_language_rationale: Published April 2025, English. Evidence: "Published Online: April 18, 2025" [p.1]

lead_rationale: Both reviewers: greywater treatment engineering study; no adaptation process or outcome measured.
second_reviewer_summary: Scanned PDF (read visually) describing a household greywater treatment plant in rural Iraq and its water-quality performance. Water scarcity is generic background and no adaptation processes or outcomes are measured. Excluded on concept and context.
exclusion_reason: Concept criterion fails (no adaptation process or outcome measured; engineering water-treatment performance only); context link to climate is weak/implicit (water scarcity only).
population_rationale: A single rural household (8 persons) with a 600 m2 home garden in rural Iraq (upper-middle-income); small-scale household production, not commercial. Evidence: "a house was chosen in the village of Khairi in Al-Diwaniyah governorate. The greywater network is isolated from the sewage network and the family has 8 persons." [p.2, Materials and methods]
concept_rationale: Paper is an engineering design and water-quality performance test of a household greywater treatment plant. No adaptation process (adoption, decision-making, learning) or outcome (productivity, income, resilience) is measured; only effluent quality (BOD, COD, TSS, coliforms) is reported. Evidence: "The percentage of removal of suspended solids reached 94% and the nitrogen removal rate was 85 %." [p.1, Abstract] | "Samples were labeled using waterproof markers and noted in hard-cover, bound field books." [p.3, Greywater sampling]
context_rationale: Water scarcity is the stated rationale, which the codebook can treat as an implicit climate link in semi-arid settings, but no climate hazard (drought, temperature, rainfall variability) is named and climate does not drive the question; framing is sanitation, pollution and water supply. Evidence: "Iraq suffers from water scarcity in recent years and the problem is exacerbated by increasing population." [p.1, Introduction]
methodology_rationale: Empirical field/laboratory measurements of water quality before and after treatment over a year. Evidence: "Greywater samples for raw and treated grey water were collected on a monthly basis beginning in late January 2017 and ending in December 2017." [p.3, Greywater sampling]
geography_rationale: Al-Diwaniyah governorate, Iraq (upper-middle-income). Evidence: "a house was chosen in the village of Khairi in Al-Diwaniyah governorate." [p.2, Materials and methods]
period_language_rationale: Published 2017, English. Evidence: "Journal of Engineering and Applied Sciences 12 (Special Issue 6): 7944-7950, 2017" [p.1 header]

population_rationale: Smallholder triple-rice farming households (most with <3 ha) in An Giang, Vietnam (LMIC). Evidence: "In 2019, we interviewed 60 farmers in two communes of Phu Hiep and Phu Tan of Phu Tan district." [p.5, Methods 3.3.2] | "most of the household heads own small areas, of which the heads of households have less than 1 ha of cultivation area" [p.7, 4.1]
concept_rationale: Assesses livelihood sustainability (capital index) and farmers' acceptance/adoption of flood-based farming (3-3-2 cycle, flood-based crops) as adaptation options to changed flood regimes. Evidence: "This study also aims to identify measures that could enhance more beneficial flood adaptation strategies." [p.3, Introduction]
context_rationale: Flooding, flood regime change and climate variability (rainfall, drought, heat) in agriculture frame the research question and are measured as natural-capital indicators. Evidence: "Rapidly changing hydrological conditions under climate change, upstream developments, and local water infrastructures require transformative changes in water management strategies" [p.1, Abstract]
methodology_rationale: Household interviews, FGDs and an index calculation. Evidence: "We interviewed 160 rice farmers and conducted two focus group discussions in two communes in An Giang province." [p.1, Abstract]
geography_rationale: Vietnam (lower-middle-income). Evidence: "Phu Tan is one of the 11 districts of An Giang province" [p.3, Site description]
period_language_rationale: Published 2021 (online 2020), English. Evidence: "Agricultural Water Management 243 (2021) 106495" [p.1 header]

lead_rationale: R1 uncertain, R2 exclude: assesses the skill of indigenous rainfall forecasts, not an adaptation process or outcome among producers. Could be retained only under a broad 'climate information' reading.
second_reviewer_summary: Forecast-skill proof of concept for indigenous rainfall prediction among Ghanaian rice farmers; population, context, method and geography are fine. The paper assesses forecast accuracy rather than any adaptation process or outcome, so the concept criterion is not met; a lenient reading (climate information services as an adaptation enabler) is the only route to inclusion.
exclusion_reason: Concept borderline: measures indigenous forecast techniques and skill (climate information), not an adaptation action or outcome.
population_rationale: Twelve experienced rain-fed/irrigated rice farmers in Kumbungu district, Northern Ghana; subsistence smallholder agriculture. Evidence: "most communal areas in Northern Ghana practice rain-fed subsistence agriculture" [p.3, Introduction] | "These farmers practiced both irrigated and rainfed rice farming" [p.4, 2.2.1]
concept_rationale: Study measures accuracy of farmers' indigenous rainfall forecasts versus GMet and the mental model of indicators; it is about climate information/forecasting skill and learning, with no adaptation action, adoption or outcome measured. Framed as supporting adaptation via integrated climate services, so genuine borderline (knowledge/learning process vs. not adaptation). Evidence: "There are strong calls to integrate scientific and indigenous forecasts to help farmers adapt to climate variability and change." [p.2, Abstract] | "Forecasting skills are either learned from the elderly or developed through learning-by-doing" [p.6, 3.1.1]
context_rationale: Rainfall variability and crop failure in rain-fed agriculture drive the research question. Evidence: "Rainfall variability is a problem for Ghanaian farmers, particularly rain-fed farmers in the Northern part of the country" [p.2, Introduction]
methodology_rationale: Empirical: workshops, mental modelling, app-recorded forecasts, rain gauges, deterministic forecast verification. Evidence: "Farmers sent the daily IF data from April to October 2017 using the app." [p.5, 2.2.2]
geography_rationale: Ghana is lower-middle income. Evidence: "twelve experienced farmers were purposively selected from twelve different communities in Kumbungu district of Northern Ghana" [p.4, 2.2.1]
period_language_rationale: Published 2021 (online Nov 2020), English. Evidence: "CLIMATE AND DEVELOPMENT 2021, VOL. 13, NO. 6, 551-562" [p.2 header]

population_rationale: Smallholder livestock farming households in Punjab; authors describe most as extremely poor smallholders. Evidence: "Most smallholder livestock farmers in Pakistan are extremely poor, with limited capacity to adopt CSA practices." [p.2, Introduction] | "Our survey included 428 livestock farmers, most of whom were involved in subsistence crop production." [p.4, Data]
concept_rationale: Determinants of adoption of CSA (adaptation) practices and their impact on food security and income. Evidence: "we examine the determinants of livestock farmers' adoption of climate-smart agricultural (CSA) practices and the impact of adoption on food security and household income" [p.1, Abstract]
context_rationale: Climate change, temperature and rainfall variability and anomalies drive the question; arid/semi-arid districts. Evidence: "from arid and semiarid areas, which are more vulnerable to climate change" [p.4, Data]
methodology_rationale: Household survey, multinomial endogenous switching regression. Evidence: "employing a multinomial endogenous switching regression model to address potential selection bias" [p.1, Abstract]
geography_rationale: Pakistan is lower-middle income. Evidence: "Data were obtained from a survey conducted in Punjab Province, Pakistan" [p.4, Data]

population_rationale: Borana pastoral and agro-pastoral households (women and men) in southern Ethiopia, an LMIC; small-scale livestock/crop producers. Evidence: "The communities in the selected districts were engaged in both pastoral and agro-pastoral livelihoods." [p.4, Study Site and Methods]
concept_rationale: Documents adaptation processes under drought: shifts from pastoralism to agro-pastoralism, changes in gender roles/behaviour, women's decision-making power and resource access. Borderline because the focus is gender relations, but the changes are framed as responses to drought. Evidence: "their gains and losses under livelihood transition from pastoralism to agro-pastoralism in response to recurrent droughts and other stressors" [p.3, Introduction]
context_rationale: Recurrent drought in an arid/semi-arid pastoral system drives the research question. Evidence: "We examine the dynamics of gender relations in terms of changes in gender roles and access to resources under recurrent drought conditions" [p.2, Abstract]
methodology_rationale: Empirical mixed-methods: household survey (n=240) with chi-square tests, FGDs, key informant interviews. Evidence: "randomly selected, from the total of 23,976 households, 240 households with different economic backgrounds, wealth status, and ages for the household survey" [p.4, Site Selection and Data Collection]
geography_rationale: Borana zone, Ethiopia (low-income country). Evidence: "The Borana zone in southern Ethiopia (Fig. 1) is characterized by arid and semi-arid environments" [p.4, Study Site and Methods]

population_rationale: Survey of 900 sugarcane growers in Fiji (an upper-middle-income country); 83% farm <10 ha and authors classify the majority as smallholders. Not commercial/corporate estates. Evidence: "The majority can also be classified as smallholder farmers, cultivating less than five hectares (49%) or less than 10 hectares (34%)" [p.5, Demographic characteristics]
concept_rationale: Measures reactive/anticipatory responses to climate hazards (coping, adaptation, transformation strategies) and decisions to remain in or exit farming; adaptation processes are measured, not only impacts. Evidence: "Answers were classified and recoded into three different types of strategies" [p.4, Data analysis]
context_rationale: Agricultural setting with explicit climate hazards (tropical cyclones, floods) driving the research questions. Evidence: "the relationship between climatic and non-climatic stressors and farmers’ decisions to abandon sugarcane farming" [p.1, Abstract]
methodology_rationale: Structured household survey with frequencies, chi-square and Kruskal-Wallis tests. Evidence: "A total of 900 farmers were surveyed" [p.1, Abstract]
geography_rationale: Fiji is an upper-middle-income country. Evidence: "Fiji’s sugarcane industry" [p.1, Abstract]

population_rationale: Smallholder subsistence crop farmers who are beneficiaries of the ECRIMS small-grain project in rural Zimbabwe. Evidence: "smallscale farming of crops such as cotton, sunflowers, maize, sorghum and vegetables as well as livestock rearing for subsistence is practiced in rural communities of both districts" [p.3, Study area]
concept_rationale: Analyses uptake (adoption) of drought-tolerant small grains, a climate-adaptation practice, as a function of rainfall and soil type. Evidence: "assess ward to ward soil type and precipitation distribution and how they affect uptake of small grains" [p.2, Introduction]
context_rationale: Semi-arid districts with frequent droughts; rainfall variability drives the research question. Evidence: "experience frequent severe agricultural and meteorological droughts which limit growing of large grains" [p.2, Introduction]
methodology_rationale: Empirical mixed-methods study: household questionnaire (n=724), key-informant interviews, FGDs, field observation, GIS mapping of rainfall and soils. Evidence: "The research adopted a mixed methods research design to allow for data triangulation." [p.3, Methodology]
geography_rationale: Zimbabwe is a lower-middle-income country. Evidence: "The study was conducted in Zvishavane and Mberengwa districts" [p.2, Study area]

lead_rationale: R2 include: adaptation strategies and their perceived effectiveness are recorded among coastal households. Flag: published January 2026, outside the protocol's 2005-2025 window; generic coastal population.
second_reviewer_decisive_issue: none (flag: 2026 publication date; population generic coastal households)
second_reviewer_summary: Household survey of coastal Tanzanian communities that records adaptation strategies and their perceived effectiveness alongside climate awareness; adaptation is measured, not only perception. Meets the criteria with a generic population label and a January 2026 publication date that should be flagged against the 2005-2025 window.
population_rationale: Coastal households depend on small-scale fishing, small-scale agriculture and seaweed farming and the abstract mentions smallholder farmers, so small-scale producers are plausible. But the sample is general coastal households and respondents' occupations are not reported or analysed as a distinct group. Evidence: "most local communities in the region depend on fishing, small-scale agriculture, and seaweed farming" [p.4, Study Area] | "adaptation strategies employed by smallholder farmers to respond to it" [p.1, Abstract]
concept_rationale: Beyond perceptions, the study measures adaptation strategies employed (n and %) and their perceived effectiveness (Table 5), so it is not awareness alone. Evidence: "Coastal communities in Tanga employed several strategies to cope with climate change and variability." [p.9, Results]
context_rationale: Climate stressors (temperature rise, rainfall decrease/variability, drought) affecting fisheries and agriculture drive the question. Evidence: "rising temperatures, increased rainfall variability, coastal erosion, and shifts in marine ecosystems" [p.4, Study Area]
methodology_rationale: Cross-sectional household survey (n=388) plus 15 key-informant interviews with inferential statistics and thematic analysis. Evidence: "388 households selected via simple random sampling for the quantitative component and 15 key informants purposively selected" [p.1, Abstract]
geography_rationale: Tanzania is a lower-middle-income country. Evidence: "This study was conducted in the Tanga Region of northeastern Tanzania." [p.4, Study Area]
period_language_rationale: English; published 11 January 2026, which satisfies the 2005-or-later criterion but lies outside the 2005-2025 protocol window. Evidence: "Published: 2026-01-11" [p.1]

population_rationale: Smallholder agro-pastoral household heads/decision-makers in northern Ghana (LMIC). Evidence: "Smallholder farmers in the Talensi district are subject to institutional interventions such as capacity building and ecological restoration" [p.5, Study area]
concept_rationale: Assesses adaptive capacity (livelihood capitals supporting/constraining climate adaptation, access to credit, institutional support, information, networks) and how it differs by social group; adaptation-relevant processes/access to services are analysed, not just vulnerability. Evidence: "rate locally-derived indicators of each of the five livelihood capitals (human, social, natural, physical and financial), as to the level of support provided to adaptation" [p.12, Discussion]
context_rationale: Rain-fed dryland agriculture with explicit climate hazards (rainfall variability, drought, floods) driving the question. Evidence: "Talensi district has experienced major impacts of climate change, including drought, famine, crop loss, floods, wildfires, and pest infestations" [p.5, Study area]
methodology_rationale: Empirical mixed methods: household survey (n=130) with Chi-square tests, six FGDs, key informant interviews. Evidence: "Drawing from a systematic random sample of 130 smallholder farmers and six focus group discussions and employing descriptive and inferential statistics and narrative analysis" [p.2, Abstract]
geography_rationale: Ghana is lower-middle income. Evidence: "Fieldwork was conducted in the Talensi district in Ghana's northern savannah AEZ" [p.5, Study area]

lead_rationale: Both reviewers: psychological determinants of soil-conservation adoption; no climate hazard drives the question (context fails).
second_reviewer_summary: Psychological (self-control, hope) determinants of soil-conservation technology adoption among Nepali smallholders. Climate risk is not the driver of the research question, so context (and concept framing) is not met; the climate-adaptation link is only an incidental statement.
exclusion_reason: Context criterion fails: no explicit climate hazard drives the research question; climate change is background only (soil degradation/technology adoption study). Concept borderline.
population_rationale: Smallholder vegetable farmers (up to 10 ha) in Jhapa district, Nepal. Evidence: "Agriculture in Nepal is still largely subsistence-oriented, is dominated by smallholder farmers" [p.3, Case study]
concept_rationale: Measures adoption of soil-conservation practices (uptake) and its psychological/informational determinants; adoption is a process in scope, but the practices are framed around soil degradation, not climate risk. Evidence: "all aiming to protect soil degradation, which are sometimes referred to as "conservation agriculture"" [p.4]
context_rationale: Climate change is only background (one sentence says technologies could 'help adapt to climate change'); the research question is soil degradation and technology adoption in general. Codebook: climate as background only -> exclude. Evidence: "the adoption of agricultural technologies could improve farming practices, help adapt to climate change and steady soil degradation" [p.4, Case study]
methodology_rationale: Structured household survey (n=268) with multiple regression and moderation analysis. Evidence: "Data were collected from 268 households in the Jhapa district by a face-to-face questionnaire." [p.1, Abstract]
geography_rationale: Nepal is lower-middle income. Evidence: "Jhapa district in Nepal" [p.4, Sample]

lead_rationale: R1 uncertain, R2 exclude: groundwater-saving intention driven by social capital with no climate-adaptation framing or measured action.
